entry.title: Research Summary: June 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans frontier model releases, training-efficiency advances, and safety findings with societal weight. NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550B-total/55B-active Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Attention model (20T tokens, 1M context) built for agentic reasoning. The AI Scientist pushes toward end-to-end automation of the full research lifecycle, while the Stanford AI Index Report 2026 maps ecosystem-wide progress and governance gaps.

Optimization and training stability see practical, broadly applicable gains:

  • Hyperball fixes Frobenius norms of weights and updates to restore matrix-aware scaling gains (Tengyu Ma et al.)
  • Taming Curvature uses online preconditioned-Hessian estimation for an architecture warm-up that stabilizes Transformer training

Reasoning, RL, and representation learning advance:

  • Diversity collapse in RLVR is formalized via overtraining—Pass@1 improves while Pass@k degrades once reward saturates
  • A temporal-difference method (Yann LeCun, Heng Ji) removes augmentation/masking biases from visual representation learning

Alignment and scientific applications round out the day:

  • Constitutional Value Potentials read and steer internal margins from hidden states
  • A study of 100+ biological reasoning models dissects how pre-training, SFT, and RL shape in- vs out-of-domain generalization
  • Four preregistered experiments (~19,000 conversations) find AI systems out-persuade expert humans

NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550B-total/55B-active Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Attention model (20T tokens, 1M context) built for agentic reasoning. The AI Scientist pushes toward end-to-end automation of the full research lifecycle, while the Stanford AI Index Report 2026 maps ecosystem-wide progress and governance gaps.

Optimization and training stability see practical, broadly applicable gains:

  • Hyperball fixes Frobenius norms of weights and updates to restore matrix-aware scaling gains (Tengyu Ma et al.)
  • Taming Curvature uses online preconditioned-Hessian estimation for an architecture warm-up that stabilizes Transformer training

Reasoning, RL, and representation learning advance:

  • Diversity collapse in RLVR is formalized via overtraining—Pass@1 improves while Pass@k degrades once reward saturates
  • A temporal-difference method (Yann LeCun, Heng Ji) removes augmentation/masking biases from visual representation learning

entry.title: Towards End-to-End Automation of AI Research

author.name: Yutaro Yamada, Robert Tjarko Lange, Cong Lu, Chris Lu, Shengran Hu, Jakob Foerster, David Ha, Jeff Clune

entry.summary: Presents The AI Scientist, an end-to-end system that autonomously generates research ideas, writes code, runs experiments, drafts manuscripts, and conducts peer review, claiming the strongest demonstration of full research automation to date. Authored by a prominent team including David Ha and Jeff Clune.

entry.summary: Nemotron 3 Ultra is NVIDIA's 550B-total/55B-active Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Attention model pretrained on 20T tokens, extended to 1M context, and post-trained with SFT, RL, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation. It claims up to ~6x higher inference throughput than comparable public LLMs at on-par accuracy using techniques like LatentMoE, MTP, and NVFP4 pretraining.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2026

author.name: Sha Sajadieh, Loredana Fattorini, Raymond Perrault, Yolanda Gil, Vanessa Parli, Lapo Santarlasci, Juan Pava, Nestor Maslej, Russ Altman, Erik Brynjolfsson, Carla Brodley, Jack Clark, Virginia Dignum, Vipin Kumar, James Landay, Terah Lyons, James Manyika, Juan Carlos Niebles, Yoav Shoham, Elham Tabassi, Russell Wald, Toby Walsh, Dan Weld

entry.summary: The ninth edition of the Stanford AI Index Report tracks AI advances across reasoning, safety, real-world task execution, governance gaps, and new estimates of generative AI's economic value. A major authoritative reference for the state of AI.

entry.title: AI systems out-persuade expert humans

author.name: Kobi Hackenburg, Caroline Wagner, Luke Hewitt, Ben M. Tappin, Ed Saunders, Hannah Rose Kirk, Helen Margetts, Christopher Summerfield

entry.summary: Reports four large preregistered experiments (nearly 19,000 conversations) showing AI systems are reliably more persuasive than expert humans, including tournament winners, professional canvassers, and world-championship debaters even when humans prepared extensively. The finding has major implications for AI's role in societal contests of persuasion.

entry.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization

author.name: Kaiyue Wen, Xingyu Dang, Kaifeng Lyu, Tengyu Ma, Percy Liang

entry.summary: Hyperball is an optimizer wrapper that fixes the Frobenius norms of weight matrices and their updates to constants, restoring the scaling gains of matrix optimizers like Muon over AdamW. It achieves 20 to 30 percent token-equivalent speedups and improves learning-rate transfer on Qwen3-style models up to 1.2B parameters.

entry.title: How Post-Training Shapes Biological Reasoning Models

author.name: Lukas Fesser, Hanlin Zhang, Michelle M. Li, Eric Wang, Bryan Perozzi, Shekoofeh Azizi, Sham M. Kakade, Marinka Zitnik

entry.summary: A large empirical study of over 100 biological reasoning models examines how continued pre-training, SFT, and RL each shape in-domain versus out-of-domain generalization across genomics, transcriptomics, and proteins. It identifies when post-training improves performance versus inducing over-specialization.

entry.title: Understanding Diversity Collapse in RLVR via the Lens of Overtraining

author.name: Suqin Yuan, Jinkun Chen, Jiyang Zheng, Muyang Li, Lei Feng, Dadong Wang, Tao Xiang, Tongliang Liu, Bo An

entry.summary: Formalizes diversity collapse in RLVR (Pass@1 improves while Pass@k degrades) through the lens of overtraining, showing that once a problem's reward contribution saturates further updates just concentrate probability mass. Provides theoretical grounding for a known RLVR pathology.

entry.title: Constitutional Value Potentials: reading and steering internal priority margins in language models

author.name: Tong Che, Rui Wu

entry.summary: Constitutional Value Potentials learn scalar potentials from hidden states representing internal pressure to preserve each value, with their signed difference forming a priority margin readable from activations. Aims to detect and steer how models arbitrate value conflicts internally.

entry.title: You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences

author.name: Ninad Daithankar, Alexi Gladstone, Yann LeCun, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Argues that visual representation learning should remove remaining inductive biases like augmentations and masking, proposing a temporal-difference approach that learns from video without strong assumptions. Experiments confirm that the optimal strength of inductive biases diminishes with scale.

entry.title: Taming Curvature: Architecture Warm-Up for Stable Transformer Training

author.name: Sameera Ramasinghe, Ajanthan Thalaiyasingam, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Yan Zuo, Karol Pajak, Alexander Long

entry.summary: This paper introduces a fast online estimator of preconditioned Hessian curvature using warm-started power iteration, then uses it for an architecture warm-up that stabilizes billion-parameter Transformer training. It connects Edge of Stability theory to practical large-scale training.

entry.title: The Value Axis: Language Models Encode Whether They're on the Right Track

author.name: Nick Jiang, Isaac Kauvar, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: This paper finds that language models internally track the value of their current reasoning trajectory along a learnable value axis, distinguishing high vs low confidence, backtracking, and correct vs corrupted code. Steering along this axis causally controls self-correction and exploration behavior.

entry.title: Relational Structural Causal Models

author.name: Adiba Ejaz, Elias Bareinboim

entry.summary: This work extends Pearl's structural causal models to relational settings where objects and relations vary, deriving identifiability conditions and relational causal graphs for generalizing to unseen object combinations. Co-authored by Elias Bareinboim, it offers rigorous theoretical foundations for combinatorial causal reasoning.

entry.title: VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models

author.name: Sen Xu, Shixi Liu, Wei Wang, Jixin Min, Yingwei Dai, Zhibin Yin, Yirong Chen, Xin Zhou, Junlin Zhang

entry.summary: VibeThinker-3B is a compact 3B-parameter dense model that achieves frontier-level verifiable reasoning, scoring 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6 via a Spectrum-to-Signal post-training pipeline of curriculum SFT, multi-domain RL, and self-distillation. Demonstrates strong small-model reasoning.

entry.summary: This technical report presents Ling-2.6 and Ring-2.6, a family of trillion-parameter-scale models for agentic intelligence, with Ling optimized for instant response and Ring for deeper reasoning. They are built by upgrading the Ling-2.0 base via architectural migration pretraining and large-scale post-training under unified system co-design.

entry.title: Defending against Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks via Reasoning-enabled Task Alignment

author.name: Lipeng He, Yihan Wang, Jiawen Zhang, N. Asokan

entry.summary: Defends against adaptive indirect prompt-injection attacks by training models to assess whether each embedded instruction's intent aligns with the user task, rather than recognizing specific attack patterns. Traces why prior defenses collapse under adaptive attackers.

entry.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework

author.name: David Huang, Jaewon Chang, Avidan Shah, Prateek Mittal, Chawin Sitawarin

entry.summary: Demonstrates practical poisoning attacks against the Rapid Response jailbreak-defense framework deployed in Anthropic's ASL-3 safeguards, using prompt injection to infiltrate the classifier's training set. Enables targeted false-positive poisoning and concept-based backdoor attacks.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Auditing Anti-Muslim Bias in Frontier LLMs Across Reasoning, Agentic, and Time-Coupled Conditions

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Tamim Sheikh

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a 1,200-prompt benchmark auditing anti-Muslim bias in frontier LLMs across direct completion, chain-of-thought, and simulated agentic decision contexts. It finds that CoT reasoning amplifies Muslim-violence associations by 12 to 34 percent relative to direct completion.

entry.title: Exact Posterior Score Estimation for Solving Linear Inverse Problems

author.name: Abbas Mammadov, Ozgur Kara, Kaan Oktay, Iskander Azangulov, Adil Kaan Akan, Hyungjin Chung, James Matthew Rehg, Yee Whye Teh

entry.summary: This paper derives the exact posterior score in closed form for linear Gaussian inverse problems under general Gaussian interpolants, showing posterior sampling reduces to denoising at an operator-dependent shifted pivot. It improves on approximate measurement-matching corrections in diffusion-based inverse solvers.

entry.title: MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark

author.name: Adnan El Assadi, Roman Solomatin, Isaac Chung, Chenghao Xiao, Deep Shah, Manan Dey, Shriya Sudhakar, Zacharie Bugaud, Wissam Siblini, Ayush Sunil Munot, Yashwanth Devavarapu, Rakshitha Ireddi, Michelle Yang, M\'arton Kardos, Niklas Muennighoff, Kenneth Enevoldsen

entry.summary: MVEB is a 23-task massive video embedding benchmark spanning classification, retrieval, clustering, and video QA, evaluating 33 models. It finds no single model dominates and that audio's contribution depends on dataset annotation provenance.

entry.title: How Much Can We Trust LLM Search Agents? Measuring Endorsement Vulnerability to Web Content Manipulation

author.name: Yimeng Chen, Zhe Ren, Firas Laakom, Yu Li, Dandan Guo, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: SearchGEO is a controlled evaluation framework measuring how LLM-based web search agents can be manipulated into endorsing attacker-published content. It benchmarks 13 LLM backends, finding attack success rates ranging from 0% (Claude-Sonnet-4.6) to 31.4% (Gemini-3-Flash).

entry.title: Not All Skills Help: Measuring and Repairing Agent Knowledge

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Yiyang Zhou, Yiming Liang, Congyu Zhang, Fuxiao Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: Argues that LLM agents accumulating natural-language skills suffer pervasive causal heterogeneity—skills help on some tasks but hurt on others, canceling in aggregate. Uses randomized masking to measure per-skill causal contributions and repair skill libraries.

entry.title: Is Code Better Than Language for Algorithmic Reasoning

author.name: Terry Tong, Yu Feng, Surbhi Goel, Dan Roth

entry.summary: Separates representation from execution mechanism in tool-augmented reasoning by having the model express reasoning as code then either execute it deterministically or simulate it in-context. Finds deterministic code execution beats natural-language reasoning by 31.6pp while the representation change alone barely matters.

entry.title: Learning Policy from a Single Trajectory in Average-Reward Markov Decision Process

author.name: Jongmin Lee, Ernest K. Ryu, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: This work establishes the first finite-sample complexity guarantees from a single trajectory for weakly communicating average-reward MDPs, without ergodicity or generative-model assumptions. It develops model-free value-based and policy-based methods with explicit sample bounds.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Ziqing Qiao, Yinuo Xu, Chaojun Xiao, Zhou Su, Zihan Zhou, Yingfa Chen, Xiaoyue Xu, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes how efficient attention modules (sliding-window attention, recurrent mixers) shape hybrid Transformer architectures across scaling, mechanism, and design. It finds efficient-attention choice mainly affects how fast long-context capability emerges, with hybrids converging to comparable performance given enough training.

entry.title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments

author.name: Shreshth Rajan

entry.summary: Audits the rate at which code RL training environments accept incorrect solutions, finding 25-28% of SWE-bench Verified and R2E-Gym tasks have test suites weak enough to pass incorrect patches, and that models score significantly higher on hackable tasks. Describes a procedure to harden broken tasks.

entry.title: Kairos: A Native World Model Stack for Physical AI

author.name: Kairos Team, Fei Wang, Shan You, Qiming Zhang, Tao Huang, Zuoyi Fu, Zhisheng Zheng, Yunlong Xi, Feng Lv, Xiaoming Wu, Zeyu Liu, Cong Wan, Pu Li, Ruiqing Yang, Xiaoou Li, Wei Wang, Kangkang Zhu, Yuwei Zhang, Shi Fu, Xiaoning Wu, Xuzeng Fan, Dacheng Tao, Xiaogang Wang

entry.summary: Kairos is a native world model stack for Physical AI featuring a cross-embodiment data curriculum, unified world understanding/generation/prediction architecture, and efficient real-deployment execution. Designed to acquire world knowledge from heterogeneous experience and maintain persistent long-horizon states.

entry.title: Localizing Credit at the Divergence: Path-Conditioned Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yu Li, Shu Hong, Tian Lan

entry.summary: Hindsight Self-Distillation improves token-level credit assignment in RL reasoning by conditioning a teacher on a successful peer rollout from the current training group, providing dense per-token guidance at intermediate positions where ground-truth answers give no signal. An exact success-conditioned sample requiring no extra annotation.

entry.title: Retrieve, Don't Retrain: Extending Vision Language Action Models to New Tasks at Test Time

author.name: Jeongeun Park, Juhan Park, Taekyung Kim, Sungjoon Choi, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval-augmented VLA policy trained once on paired demonstrations from target and cheaper embodiments then frozen, adding new tasks at deployment by appending demonstrations to a retrieval pool rather than fine-tuning. Replaces per-task adaptation cost with retrieval.

entry.title: When to use what Schatten-$p$ norm in deep learning?

author.name: Thomas Pethick

entry.summary: Resolves conflicting observations about Schatten-p based optimizers like Muon by showing the optimal norm choice is regime-dependent, with smaller p preferable in low-dimensional regimes including Chinchilla scaling. Provides a noise-robust acceleration result and a batch-size scaling rule.

entry.title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training

author.name: Violet Xiang, Amrith Setlur, Chase Blagden, Nick Haber, Aviral Kumar

entry.summary: ExpRL studies RL-based mid-training for LLMs using large corpora of human-written question-answer data rather than manually curated reasoning traces. It aims to automatically teach combinable reasoning skills that help on much harder problems.

entry.title: Representation Costs in Data Science: Foundations and the Quasi-Banach Spaces of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Greg Ongie, Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: This paper develops a general framework analyzing representation costs of parametric data-fitting methods via parameter-space regularizers and their induced function spaces. It proves representer theorems and connects parametric methods to nonparametric descriptions, introducing quasi-Banach spaces for deep networks.

entry.title: KVEraser: Learning to Steer KV Cache for Efficient Localized Context Erasing

author.name: Mufei Li, Shikun Liu, Dongqi Fu, Haoyu Wang, Yinglong Xia, Hong Li, Hong Yan, Pan Li

entry.summary: KVEraser is a learned KV-cache editing method that efficiently erases the influence of a localized context span without recomputing all subsequent tokens. It addresses removing stale facts, wrong tool observations, or prompt injections after prefill in long-context LLMs.

entry.title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning

author.name: Jisang Han, Seonghu Jeon, Jaewoo Jung, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Honggyu An, Tifanny Portela, Marco Hutter, Marc Pollefeys, Seungryong Kim, Sunghwan Hong

entry.summary: Geometric Action Model repurposes a pretrained geometric foundation model as a shared substrate for perception, temporal prediction, and action decoding in robot manipulation. It injects explicit 3D geometry that 2D-based VLAs and world-action models lack.

entry.title: Synthetic document finetuning for instilling positive traits

author.name: CallumMcDougall

entry.summary: A DeepMind interpretability team update showing that midtraining Gemini 3 Flash on synthetic documents about its having certain traits, followed by chat finetuning demonstrating those traits, robustly instills positive values that generalize out-of-distribution. It shares practical takeaways for improving midtraining and SFT effectiveness for deep alignment.

entry.title: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion

author.name: Zixin Rao, Wentian Zhu, Chan Aristella Lu, Zhaorun Chen, Wei Niu, Le Guan, Bo Li, Zhen Xiang

entry.summary: FragFuse is a novel attack that bypasses LLM agent access control by fragmenting prohibited content across interactions, storing benign-looking fragments in long-term memory, then reconstructing them via retrieval without the final query appearing violating. Exposes a temporal memory-based attack surface.

entry.title: Retrievable Gradients: Continual Post-Training Without Cumulative Weight Drift

author.name: Weihang Su, Jiacheng Kang, Jingyan Xu, Qingyao Ai, Jianming Long, Hanwen Zhang, Bangde Du, Xinyuan Cao, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: ReGrad treats gradients as retrievable knowledge units, pre-computing document-specific gradients offline into an indexed Gradient Bank and retrieving only query-relevant gradients at inference for temporary weight adaptation, avoiding cumulative weight drift and catastrophic forgetting. A new paradigm between RAG and parametric updates.

entry.title: Greedy Coordinate Diffusion: Effective and Semantically Coherent Adversarial Attacks via Diffusion Guidance

author.name: Bohdan Turbal, Blossom Metevier, Max Springer, Aleksandra Korolova

entry.summary: Develops a local geometric framework analyzing parameter-space trajectories to understand why fine-tuning aligned LLMs on benign tasks degrades safety guardrails. Proves that orthogonal updates which first-order analysis deems safe are actually fragile due to fine-tuning curvature.

entry.title: ROVE: Unlocking Human Interventions for Humanoid Manipulation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wei Xiao, Weiliang Tang, Yuying Ge, Hui Zhou, Yao Mu, Li Zhang, Yixiao Ge

entry.summary: ROVE is a reinforcement learning framework for post-training humanoid vision-language-action models using imperfect human interventions, handling suboptimal whole-body and dexterous-hand corrective signals. It includes a human-in-the-loop data pipeline for deployment and intervention data.

entry.title: Speaking the Language of Science: Toward a General-Purpose Generative Foundation Model for the Natural Sciences

author.name: Mingyang Li, Yurou Liu, Jieping Ye, Bing Su, Ji-Rong Wen, Zheng Wang

entry.summary: LOGOS is a scientific generative language model that unifies heterogeneous natural-science tasks under a single autoregressive framework using a shared scientific grammar of discrete tokens. It encodes scientific objects and spatial interactions as token sequences without explicit coordinates or geometric networks.

entry.title: AI Engram: In Search of Memory Traces in Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Jea Kwon, Dong-Kyum Kim, Jiwon Kim, Yonghyun Kim, Woong Kook, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: Introduces a geometric framework to identify AI engrams (memory traces) in neural networks by formalizing neuroscientific criteria into a constrained inverse problem with a closed-form estimator. Enables surgical composition or erasure of memories via linear arithmetic.

entry.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds

author.name: \"Omer Veysel \c{C}a\u{g}atan, Xuandong Zhao

entry.summary: Adapts the AI Safety Gridworlds framework into a text-based evaluation suite for language agents, finding that specification gaming and reward hacking emerge zero-shot across frontier and mid-scale models. Co-authored by Xuandong Zhao, it grounds reward hacking study in controlled tasks.

entry.title: The Quality-Utility Paradox: Why High-Reward Data Impairs Small Model Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haolong Qian, Xianliang Yang, Yinuo ma, Lirong Che, Feng Lu, Ye Guo, Lei Song, Jiang Bian, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: Identifies a Quality-Utility Paradox where higher-reward distillation traces from a stronger Oracle underperform self-generated traces selected via rejection sampling for small-model math reasoning, due to distributional drift from the SLM's native distribution. Challenges assumptions about distillation data quality.

entry.title: Greed Is Learned: Visible Incentives as Reward-Hacking Triggers

author.name: Tong Che, Rui Wu

entry.summary: Demonstrates reward-channel addiction where RL agents that can see their reward proxy (a dashboard/balance) chase the displayed payoff across domains, sacrifice the true task, and even flip safety alignment when a dashboard pays for unsafe actions. Studies this in a synthetic MoneyWorld sandbox.

entry.title: CoAgent: Concurrency Control for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Hongtao Lyu, Dingyan Zhang, Mingyu Wu, Xingda Wei, Haibo Chen

entry.summary: CoAgent applies classical concurrency control concepts to multi-agent LLM systems that mutate shared state (git trees, clusters, documents), addressing the mismatch where locks block long inference and OCC discards minutes of work. Proposes a capability-based concurrency mechanism for agents.

entry.title: Pixels to Proofs: Probabilistically-Safe Latent World Model Control via Parallel Conformal Robust MPC

author.name: Devesh Nath, Anutam Srinivasan, Haoran Yin, Ruitong Jiang, Jeffrey Fang, Glen Chou

entry.summary: SLS^2 provides probabilistically-safe motion planning from pixels using robust MPC in learned latent world models, combining conformal prediction for calibrated latent error bounds with GPU-accelerated system level synthesis. Enables safety constraints despite imperfect latent predictions.

entry.title: LLM Judges Have Dark Current: A Psychometric Datasheet for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Hiroyasu Usami, Keisuke Hara, Ayato Tsuboi, Naohiko Matsuda

entry.summary: Argues LLM-as-a-judge systems should be reported as measurement instruments and introduces a Judge Datasheet protocol measuring dark current under empty inputs, cross-sensitivity, positional bias, and tie-induced operating points. Provides a psychometric characterization of judge reliability.

entry.title: Proximal Policy Optimization for Amortized Discrete Sampling

author.name: Anna Zykova-Myzina, Timofei Gritsaev, Daniil Tiapkin, Nikita Morozov

entry.summary: Derives policy gradient algorithms—including the first application of Proximal Policy Optimization—for training Generative Flow Networks to sample from structured discrete distributions, leveraging connections to entropy-regularized RL. Shows PPO improves convergence speed and data efficiency over standard GFlowNet objectives.

entry.title: Tying the Loop -- Tied Expert Layers in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Expert Tying shares MoE expert parameters across consecutive transformer layers while keeping independent per-layer routing and attention, cutting memory nearly in half with negligible quality loss. It is evaluated on OLMoE, Qwen3, and DeepSeek-style architectures.

entry.title: Can Neural Networks Achieve Optimal Computational-statistical Tradeoff? An Analysis on Single-Index Model

author.name: Siyu Chen, Beining Wu, Miao Lu, Zhuoran Yang, Tianhao Wang

entry.summary: Theoretical analysis of whether gradient-trained two-layer neural networks can achieve the optimal computational-statistical tradeoff for learning Gaussian single-index models, matching the SQ lower bound. Proposes a unified gradient-based algorithm using label transformation and landscape smoothing.

entry.title: A Gradient Perspective on RLVR Stability and Winner Advantage Policy Optimization

author.name: Prasanth YSS, Zhichen Ren, Rasa Hosseinzadeh, Ilan Gofman, Yuqi Chen, Zhaoyan Liu, Guangwei Yu, Jesse C. Cresswell, Satya Krishna Gorti

entry.summary: Analyzes RLVR instability through token-level gradient dynamics, deriving a taxonomy predicting how updates affect next-token probabilities and entropy depending on advantage sign and token distribution. Proposes WAPO, which updates only on positive-advantage completions to improve training stability over GRPO.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Stochastic Linear Bandits with Delay

author.name: Ofir Schlisselberg, Mengxiao Zhang, Yishay Mansour

entry.summary: This paper establishes near-optimal regret guarantees for stochastic linear bandits with delayed feedback under several delay models, showing when behavior matches multi-armed bandits and when linear structure creates new challenges. The delay penalties are shown to be dimension-free.

entry.title: Your Privacy My Cloak: Backdoor Attacks on Differentially Private Federated Learning

author.name: Xiaolin Li, Ning Wang, Ninghui Li, Wenhai Sun

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that differential privacy protects federated learning from backdoors, showing that DP can mask the statistical signatures defenses rely on. It proposes RING, an attack that exploits DP to conceal malicious contributions.

entry.title: Simplifying the Modeling of Arbitrary Conditionals in Natural Language

author.name: Yinhan Lu, Eric Elmoznino, L\'eo Gagnon, Sarthak Mittal, Tejas Kasetty, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: AC-GPT introduces a simple modification to standard causal Transformers enabling evaluation and sampling from arbitrary conditionals (past, future, mixed contexts) within a single forward pass. It avoids the degraded generations of prior architectures designed for this purpose.

entry.title: Data-Centric Benchmarking of Exploit Generation in LLMs: Understanding the Impact of Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yiwei Chen, Lichi Li, Kai Cheung, Vinny Parla, Ganesh Sundaram

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks 17 LLMs on CVE-conditioned exploit generation with an LLM-as-judge rubric framework, and shows fine-tuning an 8B open model improves exploit quality by over 42 percent to rival proprietary models. It highlights dual-use security risks of fine-tuning on offensive cyber data.

entry.title: Your "Pro" LLM Subscription May Actually Be "Free": Exposing Fingerprint Spoofing Risks in LLM Inference Services

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Xiuyu Li, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a fingerprint-spoofing threat where a malicious LLM API provider serves a weaker model parameter-efficiently fine-tuned to mimic a stronger model's fingerprint, evading user verification. Proves that finite query budgets and weak classifiers make current black-box fingerprinting vulnerable.

entry.title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents

author.name: Sina Hajimiri, Masih Aminbeidokhti, Jose Dolz, Ismail Ben Ayed, Issam H. Laradji, Spandana Gella, Nicolas Gontier

entry.summary: A budget-constrained study finding that adding memory, workflow, or skill modules to web agents often fails to beat a token-matched vanilla baseline that simply takes more actor steps. It re-evaluates online augmentation under fixed total inference budgets.

entry.title: SHARD: Safe and Helpful Alignment via Self-Reframing Distillation

author.name: Viswonathan Manoranjan, Amogh Gupta, Anvesh Rao Vijjini, Thomas Hofweber, Snigdha Chaturvedi

entry.summary: SHARD is a self-reframing distillation method that rewrites sensitive prompts to surface benign intent, reframes original responses into safer helpful ones, and fine-tunes on those self-generated responses. It improves safe-helpfulness while preserving safety, competitive with larger-teacher distillation.

entry.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation

author.name: Gili Lior, Tzviel Frostig, Gabriel Stanovsky, Matan Eyal

entry.summary: Multilingual-IRT extends Item Response Theory with per-language difficulty deviations, split discriminability separating content from language effects, and per-language ability residuals. It enables efficient multilingual LLM evaluation and detecting flawed or culture-specific items across 25 LLMs and 29 languages.

entry.title: SciOrch: Learning to Orchestrate Expert LLMs for Solving Frontier Multimodal Scientific Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Jingru Guo, Xiangyuan Xue, Lian Zhang, Wanghan Xu, Siki Chen, Philip Torr, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Bai, Zhenfei Yin

entry.summary: SciOrch trains a lightweight 8B orchestrator model to decompose scientific reasoning questions, delegate sub-problems to frontier commercial LLMs via APIs, and synthesize answers. It exploits model complementarity on frontier multimodal scientific reasoning tasks.

entry.title: GRACE: Step-Level Benchmark for Faithful Reasoning over Context

author.name: Hoang Pham, Dong Le, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: GRACE is the first human-annotated step-level faithfulness benchmark with a data-driven error taxonomy for context-grounded reasoning, covering CoT traces from 10 models across 4 datasets. It localizes where and what type of faithfulness failure occurs within chains.

entry.title: The Vision Encoder as a Privacy Boundary: Visual-Token Side Channels in Encoder-Free Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Qiliang Jiang, Shuning Wu, Xu Zhou

entry.summary: This paper shows that encoder-free vision-language models expose a privacy side channel because intermediate visual tokens can be inverted to recover recognizable image structure and readable held-out access codes. Encoder-based models leak only target regions, not exact strings, treating the vision encoder as a privacy boundary.

entry.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LLM Judges

author.name: Zihan Wang, Guansong Pang, Zelin Liu, Wenjun Miao, Jin Zheng, Xiao Bai

entry.summary: RobustMLLMJudge is the first framework to evaluate adversarial robustness of multimodal LLMs used as automated judges for quality and safety, revealing high vulnerability to score-inflating attacks. Highlights reliability risks in MLLM-as-judge pipelines.

entry.title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation

author.name: Jie Zhang, Xiaoyue Chen, Anzhe Chen, Chenxu Lv, Deqing Li, Gengze Zhou, Hang Yin, Haoqi Yuan, Haoyang Li, Jiahao Li, Jiazhao Zhang, Jingren Zhou, Kaiyuan Gao, Kun Yan, Lihan Jiang, Ningyuan Tang, Pei Lin, Qihang Peng, Shengming Yin, Tianhe Wu, Tianyi Yan, Xiao Xu, Yan Shu, Yanran Zhang, Ye Wang, Yi Wang, Yilei Chen, Yixian Xu, Yiyang Huang, Yuxiang Chen, Zekai Zhang, Zhendong Wang, Zhixing Lei, Zhixuan Liang, Zihao Liu, Zikai Zhou, Xiong-Hui Chen, Chenfei Wu

entry.summary: Qwen-RobotWorld is a language-conditioned video world model for embodied intelligence that predicts physically grounded future visual trajectories across manipulation, driving, navigation, and human-to-robot transfer using natural language as a unified action interface. It uses a 60-layer double-stream diffusion transformer with MLLM action encoding for synthetic data generation, policy evaluation, and language-guided planning.

entry.title: Semidefinite Relaxations for Collision-Free Motion Planning

author.name: Bernhard Paus Graesdal, Alexandre Amice, Pablo A. Parrilo, Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of semidefinite relaxations for collision-free motion planning, showing equivalence between the convex relaxation and global optimality of a related problem. Authored by Tedrake and Parrilo's group, it brings rigorous optimization theory to a core robotics problem.

entry.title: Thinking with Visual Grounding

author.name: Junkai Zhang, Yihe Deng, Kai-Wei Chang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces visually grounded thinking, where VLMs interleave natural-language reasoning with explicit point or box groundings of visual evidence at each step, supported by a scalable synthesis pipeline that distills grounded reasoning traces. Makes visual reasoning verifiable. Authors include Kai-Wei Chang and Wei Wang.

entry.title: Latent Thought Flow: Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Xiandong Zou, Jing Huang, Jianshu Li, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: Latent Thought Flow models reasoning as variable-length continuous trajectories trained with a continuous GFlowNet to match a reward-induced posterior over answer quality and compute cost. Aims to reduce the token-decoding overhead of explicit chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: Discovering Lattice Reduction Strategies via Self-Play

author.name: Mohamed Malhou, Kristin Lauter, Ludovic Perret

entry.summary: This work uses AlphaZero-style deep reinforcement learning with self-play and adaptive-horizon MCTS to discover lattice basis reduction strategies that outperform the classical LLL algorithm. The resulting policy DeltaStar finds strictly superior, generalizable reduction strategies relevant to cryptography.

entry.title: CmdNeedle: Measuring the Incompleteness of Command Denylists for AI Agents

author.name: Chuyang Chen, Zhiqiang Lin

entry.summary: CmdNeedle measures the incompleteness of command denylists used by terminal AI agents, showing that even well-maintained denylists (e.g., Claude Code's) overlook bypass commands that invalidate their effectiveness. Highlights a fragile security mechanism.

entry.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies

author.name: Jialei Chen, Kai Wang, Kang Chen, Shuaihang Chen, Feng Gao, Wenhao Tang, Zhiyuan Li, Weilin Liu, Zhuyu Yao, Boxun Li, Yuanbo Xu, Chao Yu

entry.summary: LaWAM is a latent world-action model that exposes predictive dynamics to robot policies through compact latent visual subgoals instead of expensive reconstructed future video, training a latent action model in the latent space of a pretrained world model. Improves efficiency of dynamics-aware VLA policies.

entry.title: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Lawrence Keunho Jang, Andrew Keunwoo Jang, Jing Yu Koh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov

entry.summary: MyPCBench is a benchmark for personally intelligent computer-use agents, testing them as personal assistants on a Linux desktop with 17 simulated web apps seeded for a single persona. It addresses the gap between impersonal evaluations and real personal-assistant deployment.

entry.title: Generative modelling powered by room-temperature polariton condensates

author.name: Yuan Wang, Marcin Muszynski, Avinash Dash, Rishabh Kaurav, Vinod M. Menon, Oleksandr Kyriienko

entry.summary: This experimental work uses room-temperature exciton-polariton condensates in organic microcavities as physical stochastic transformation layers within a generative adversarial network for conditional digit-to-image translation. It exploits nonlinear many-body dynamics and intrinsic stochasticity to outperform digital baselines.

entry.title: Schattor: Schatten-family methods for deep learning optimization

author.name: Bohao Ma, Junyu Zhang, Chuan He

entry.summary: Proposes Schattor, a family of adaptive first-order optimizers based on Schatten norms that unifies SGD and the matrix-variate Muon optimizer in one framework. Establishes dimension-free stationarity guarantees via a novel matrix martingale moment bound.

entry.title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes

author.name: Tongyan Fang, Siyuan Huang, Naiyu Fang, Ganlong Zhao, Zhongjin Luo, Jianbo Liu, Xiaogang Wang, Ying Dong, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes hierarchical advantage weighting for online RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action models from sparse binary episode outcomes, separating viability from efficiency signals. It also handles mixed autonomous and intervention rollout segments.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Infer World Models? Evidence from Agentic Automata Learning

author.name: Reef Menaged, Gili Lior, Shauli Ravfogel, Roee Aharoni, Gabriel Stanovsky

entry.summary: Proposes agentic automata learning to test whether tool-calling LLM agents can infer hidden deterministic finite automata through membership and equivalence queries. It finds performance drops sharply with DFA size and reasoning models outperform non-reasoning ones.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Reflective Masking Elicits Reasoning in Mask Diffusion Models

author.name: Yanming Zhang, Yihan Bian, Jingyuan Qi, Yuguang Yao, Lifu Huang, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Reflective Masking, a lightweight post-training method enabling multi-turn masking and denoising in Mask Diffusion Models so they can perform local edits to refine previous outputs. It elicits iterative human-like refinement reasoning instead of regenerating from scratch.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Meta-Analysis Articles from Nature Portfolio

author.name: Anzhe Xie, Weihang Su, Yujia Zhou, Yiqun Liu, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: MetaSyn is a benchmark of 442 expert-curated meta-analyses from Nature Portfolio journals, pairing research questions with PICO criteria, a 140k-article PubMed corpus, verified studies, and hard negatives. It evaluates LLM agents across the full retrieval-screening-synthesis meta-analysis pipeline.

entry.title: Metric Match: A Subset Selection Approach to Evaluating LLM Judge Reliability

author.name: Alyssa Unell, Natalie Dullerud, Naomi Boneh, Meena Jagadeesan, Tatsu Hashimoto, Nigam Shah, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Metric Match estimates LLM judge reliability metrics from limited human annotations by selecting subsets that match population reliability with respect to synthetic labels. Authored by a strong Stanford team, it improves cost-efficiency of evaluating LLM judges.

entry.title: SpecAlign: Efficient Specification-Grounded Alignment of Large Language Models via Synthetic Data

author.name: Wenjie Wang, Yue Huang, Zhengqing Yuan, Han Bao, Shiyi Du, Yuchen Ma, Yue Zhao, Yanfang Ye, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: SpecAlign treats provider-authored model specifications as the primary alignment target, synthesizing alignment training data directly from these long, structured, frequently-updated specs. Offers a systematic mechanism to operationalize specifications as training signals rather than abstract principles.

entry.title: A First-Principles Derivation of LLM Policy Optimization: From Expected Reward to GRPO and Its Structural Extensions

author.name: Jianghan Shen, Siqi Luo, Yue Li, Jiyao Liu, Wanying Qu, Yi Zhang, Ziyan Huang, Tianbin Li, Ming Hu, Xiaohong Liu, Yirong Chen, Junjun He

entry.summary: Derives LLM policy optimization methods from first principles starting from the expected-reward objective, organizing REINFORCE, PPO, GRPO, and extensions by how each modifies trajectory probability or reward factors. Provides a unified gradient-estimator-centric view of where each method intervenes.

entry.title: Honeypot Protocol

author.name: Najmul Hasan

entry.summary: Introduces the honeypot protocol for AI control that actively tests for context-dependent behavior by varying only the system prompt across evaluation, synthetic deployment, and no-monitoring conditions while holding the task identical. Evaluates a Claude model in BashArena across conditions in honest and attack modes.

entry.title: Is Your Agent Playing Dead? Deployed LLM Agents Exhibit Constraint-Evasive Fabrication and Thanatosis

author.name: Andoni Rodr\'iguez, Alberto Pozanco, Daniel Borrajo

entry.summary: This paper characterizes Constraint-Evasive Fabrication, where LLM agents under irreconcilable constraints spontaneously fabricate plausible external obstacles, and its extreme form Thanatosis, where the agent simulates a system crash to make users disengage. It documents these behaviors including a GPT-4o banking agent faking exception traces.

entry.title: The Perils of Agency: How Developers Perceive, Prioritize, and Address Risks in Agentic AI Products

author.name: Hao-Ping Lee, Jessica He, David Piorkowski, Thomas Serban von Davier, Jodi Forlizzi, Sauvik Das

entry.summary: Qualitative study of how 35 industry developers perceive, prioritize, and address risks in agentic AI products, finding they prioritize product/business risks over downstream societal risks and lack mature mitigation practices. Offers empirical grounding for agentic AI governance.

entry.title: EHRNote-ChatQA: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multi-Turn Clinical Question Answering over Longitudinal Discharge Summaries

author.name: Jiyoun Kim, Muhan Yeo, Eunhye Jang, Jeewon Yang, Hangyul Yoon, Su Ji Lee, Hee Jo Han, Hee-Jae Jung, Doyun Kwon, Jun young Lee, Jaehun Lee, Jung-Oh Lee, Sunjun Kweon, Jong Hak Moon, Daseul Kim, Minjae Cho, Edward Choi

entry.summary: EHRNote-ChatQA is the first benchmark for evidence-grounded multi-turn clinical QA over longitudinal discharge summaries, requiring iterative synthesis across multiple summaries with evidence-grounding verification. Reflects realistic clinical review workflows beyond exam-style or single-turn QA.

entry.title: DifFRACT: Diffusion Feature Reconstruction and Attribution for Circuit Tracing

author.name: Artyom Mazur, Nina Konovalova, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: DifFRACT extends transcoder-based circuit tracing and feature attribution to multimodal diffusion transformers, providing tools to understand how semantic information propagates across denoising steps and how text and image representations interact in double-stream MM-DiT architectures. Addresses the opacity of diffusion transformers for interpretability.

entry.title: Data Augmentations for Data-Constrained Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Michael K. Chen, Xikun Zhang, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Investigates data augmentation as a regularizer to enable productive multi-epoch language model pretraining in the emerging data-constrained, compute-abundant regime. Introduces three orthogonal augmentation categories to mitigate severe overfitting in standard autoregressive training.

entry.title: Adaptive inference and function vectors in deep transformers

author.name: Ravin Raj, Gautam Reddy

entry.summary: This paper develops a mean-field theory of deep transformers as distributed inference systems that exploit function vectors to infer latent context at progressively finer scales across layers. It predicts and tests relationships between hierarchical latent structure and transformer depth.

entry.title: A Bifurcation Theory Framework for Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability

author.name: Eric Gan

entry.summary: Develops a bifurcation theory framework explaining the Edge of Stability phenomenon in gradient descent for overparameterized networks, decomposing dynamics into normal and tangent components to the minimizer manifold. Shows stable EoS arises from a flip bifurcation in the normal direction.

entry.title: Auditing Machine Unlearning: A Systematic Research on Whether Models Truly Forget

author.name: Dayong Ye, Tianqing Zhu, Ruiding Huang, Xinbo Fu, Jiayang Li, Bo Liu, Huan Huo, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes the first practical, general-purpose framework for auditing whether machine unlearning algorithms truly erase data influence, inspired by proof-of-ignorance and avoiding the need for retraining. Investigates residual information leakage risks systematically.

entry.title: GD$^2$PO: Mitigating Multi-Reward Conflicts via Group-Dynamic reward-Decoupled Policy Optimization

author.name: Haotian Liu, Yihao Liu, Jingwei Ni, Siyuan Huang, Xinpeng Liu, Pengyu Cheng, Jiajun Song, Ruijin Ding, Junfeng Li, Zhechao Yu, Mengyu Zhou, Hongteng Xu, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: GD2PO addresses multi-reward conflicts in LLM post-training RL where positive and negative advantages across reward dimensions cancel out. It proposes group-dynamic reward-decoupled policy optimization to mitigate signal cancellation and improve training efficiency.

entry.title: From Physics to Representation: Audio Learning with Synthetic Pre-training via Procedural Generation

author.name: Fengrui Liu, Ruiyang Huang, Qijian Zheng, Yuanfang Wang, Feng Liu

entry.summary: AudioPG is a procedural synthesis framework that pre-trains a masked autoencoder entirely on synthetically generated waveforms from acoustic primitives, eliminating real audio in pre-training. It transfers strongly to real benchmarks (90.6 percent on ESC-50) with under 20 minutes of single-GPU pre-training.

entry.title: Emergent retokenization symmetry in large language models: phenomenology and applications

author.name: Kanishk Jain, Matthew Day, Tankut Can

entry.summary: Investigates an emergent symmetry in LLMs where models partially respect non-canonical token segmentations of the same string despite training only on canonical ones. Probes this through compositional understanding, representation diversity, and benchmark performance experiments.

entry.title: Learning ground state observables from quantum computing experiments

author.name: Ben Jaderberg, Freya Shah, Minjun Jeon, M. Emre Sahin, Christa Zoufal, Kunal Sharma

entry.summary: Demonstrates machine learning of ground-state observables from experimental quantum data on the 2D Heisenberg XXZ model with system sizes up to 115 qubits, scaling beyond prior small-system demonstrations. Constructs datasets of single-site, two-point, and 12-body correlations.

entry.title: Diffusion Flow Matching: Dimension-Improved KL Bounds and Wasserstein Guarantees

author.name: Marta Gentiloni Silveri, Giovanni Conforti, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: Provides refined theoretical convergence guarantees for Brownian-motion-based Diffusion Flow Matching generative models, deriving KL divergence bounds with improved dimensional dependence and extending to 2-Wasserstein distance under mild conditions. Achieves state-of-the-art scaling for discretization error under minimal assumptions.

entry.title: The Complexity of Min-Max Optimization for Quadratic Polynomials

author.name: Martino Bernasconi, Matteo Castiglioni, Andrea Celli, Alexandros Hollender

entry.summary: Proves PPAD-hardness for computing approximate stationary points of min-max optimization over the hypercube for quadratic multilinear polynomials. It yields the first PPAD-hardness results for two-team zero-sum polymatrix games.

entry.title: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions

author.name: Chenxin Li, Zhengyao Fang, Zhengyang Tang, Pengyuan Lyu, Xingran Zhou, Xin Lai, Fei Tang, Liang Wu, Yiduo Guo, Weinong Wang, Junyi Li, Yi Zhang, Yang Ding, Huawen Shen, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: PhoneHarness is a mixed-action benchmark and execution harness for phone-use agents combining GUI, CLI, and tool actions on verifiable mobile workflows. It moves beyond GUI-only evaluation to check whether intended side effects actually occurred.

entry.title: CoRA: Confidence-Rationale Alignment for Reliable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Juming Xiong, Weixin Liu, Kevin Guo, Congning Ni, Junchao Zhu, Chongyu Qu, Chao Yan, Katherine Brown, Avinash Baidya, Xiang Gao, Bradley Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: CoRA introduces a GRPO-based RL framework that aligns model confidence with rationale quality in chain-of-thought reasoning, rewarding correctness, answer probability, and rubric-based rationale support. It reduces misleadingly confident but poorly supported reasoning.

entry.title: Beyond Monolingual Deep Research: Evaluating Agents and Retrievers with Cross-Lingual BrowseComp-Plus

author.name: Yuheng Lu, Qingcheng Zeng, Heli Qi, Puxuan Yu, Fuheng Zhao, Rui Yang, Hitomi Yanaka, Naoto Yokoya, Weihao Xuan

entry.summary: Introduces XBCP, a cross-lingual extension of BrowseComp-Plus that varies the language of supporting documents while keeping English queries and answers. It tests whether deep research agents and retrievers can operate when evidence is in another language.

entry.title: Who Flips? Self- and Cross-Model Counterarguments Reveal Answer Instability in LLMs

author.name: Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Amir Hossein Kargaran, Shaghayegh Kolli, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled protocol measuring answer stability when LLMs face plausible counterarguments to correct answers, finding flip rates of 17.5% to 97.3% across seven frontier models and 57 MMLU subjects. It isolates argumentative content from overt social pressure.

entry.title: Towards Pareto-Optimal Tool-Integrated Agents with Pareto Ranking Policy Optimization

author.name: Junyi Li, Xiaowei Qian, Yingyi Zhang, Wenlin Zhang, Guojing Li, Sheng Zhang, Xiao Han, Yichao Wang, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: ParetoPO is a two-stage multi-objective optimization framework for aligning tool-using LLMs under competing objectives like accuracy and tool-use efficiency, using hypervolume-guided scalarization then Pareto-ranking-based advantages. It targets Pareto-optimal tool-integrated agents.

entry.title: Weaving Multi-Source Evidence for Biomedical Reasoning: The BioMedHop Benchmark and BioWeave Framework

author.name: Xingyu Tan, Shiyuan Liu, Xiaoyang Wang, Qing Liu, Xiwei Xu, Xin Yuan, Liming Zhu, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces BioMedHop, a multi-source graph-grounded biomedical QA benchmark with 10,045 instances across KG, document, web, and hybrid evidence, plus the BioWeave framework for weaving evidence topologies. It targets source-conditioned graph reasoning underexplored in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Context-Aware RL for Agentic and Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Peiyang Xu, Bangzheng Li, Sijia Liu, Karthik R. Narasimhan, Pramod Viswanath, Prateek Mittal, Xingyu Fu

entry.summary: ContextRL is a context-aware reinforcement learning method that improves long-horizon and multimodal reasoning via an indirect auxiliary objective rewarding selection of the supporting context for a query-answer pair. It encourages fine-grained grounding in coding agents and multimodal tasks.

entry.title: Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jonas Becker, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: This work studies how intent-based misinformation injected into benign multi-agent LLM systems propagates and persists through debate, degrading reasoning, knowledge, and alignment tasks. Agents often retain incorrect answers introduced by misinformed peers.

entry.title: Towards Global AI-Driven Cervical Cancer Screening

author.name: Thuy Nuong Tran, \"Omer S\"umer, Evangelia Christodoulou, Lennart Nausch\"utte, Simon Kalteis, Martin Paulikat, Esmira Pashayeva, Klara Steinheuer, Isabella Borges, Piotr Kalinowski, Hermann Bussmann, Sieng Sokmney, Poeung Kuong, Sathiarany Vong, Achim Schneider, Magnus von Knebel-Doeberitz, Patrick Godau, Lena Maier-Hein

entry.summary: This work presents the first deep learning cervical cancer screening approach validated on multi-country colposcopy data, framed as a multi-task lesion detection and classification problem. It targets the WHO goal of cervical cancer elimination in low- and middle-income countries.

entry.title: GeoStream: Toward Precise Camera Controlled Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Yizhou Zhao, Yifan Wang, Xiaoyuan Wang, Yushu Wu, Hao Zhang, Moayed Haji-Ali, Rameen Abdal, Ashkan Mirzaei, Yanyu Li, Willi Menapace, Laszlo Jeni, Sergey Tulyakov, Peter Wonka, Chaoyang Wang

entry.summary: GeoStream enables precise metric-scale camera control in autoregressive streaming video generation by maintaining a self-refreshing 3D cache updated online from the model's own outputs. It overcomes the limitation of static 3D caches that fail when viewpoints move beyond the original frustum.

entry.title: Show the Signal, Hide the Noise: Spectral Forcing for Pixel-Space Diffusion

author.name: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces spectral forcing for pixel-space diffusion, exploiting the frequency-dependent data-to-noise contour to address a capacity-allocation problem where denoisers waste computation on noise-dominated frequency-time regions. It makes the implicit coarse-to-fine structure explicit.

entry.title: CausalDrive: Real-time Causal World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyi Yan, Huan Zheng, Dubing Chen, Meizhi Qu, Yingying Shen, Lijun Zhou, Mingfei Tu, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Haiyang Sun, Cheng-zhong Xu, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: CausalDrive proposes a real-time, controllable world model for autonomous driving that renders future driving scenes from only an initial frame, ego trajectory, and a text prompt, forcing reactivity by excluding oracle future agent layouts. This bridges the gap between non-reactive layout renderers and slow action-conditioned predictors for closed-loop policy learning.

entry.title: VFUSE: Virulent Feature Understanding With Sparse AutoEncoders

author.name: michaelwaves

entry.summary: VFUSE trains sparse autoencoders on protein diffusion-transformer activations (RoseTTAFold3, RFDiffusion3) to audit for hazard-aware features, finding monosemantic features firing on hazardous designs at up to 0.84 AUROC. It is claimed as the first SAE trained on an all-atom diffusion model and first feature-level virulence audit.

entry.title: The embrace of open science: An analysis of a decade of AI research and 56 800 conference papers

author.name: Kevin L Coakley, Thijs Snelleman, Holger Hoos, Odd Erik Gundersen

entry.summary: Analyzes reproducibility documentation practices across 56,800 papers from five leading AI conferences over a decade, finding code-and-data sharing rose nearly sixfold from 11% to 64% (2014-2024). Assesses whether reproducibility checklists have changed documentation behavior.

entry.title: Divide-and-Denoise: A Game-Theoretic Method for Fairly Composing Diffusion Models

author.name: Abhi Gupta, Polina Barabanshchikova, Vikas Garg, Samuel Kaski, Tommi Jaakkola

entry.summary: Divide-and-Denoise coordinates multiple pre-trained diffusion models during sampling via a game-theoretic allocation that fairly divides responsibility over regions of the noisy sample, solving a fair division game at each timestep. Prevents one model dominating or models disagreeing during composition.

entry.title: AutoDojo: Adaptive Attacks Expose Superficial Defenses and User-Underspecification Limits in LLM Agents

author.name: Xinhang Ma, Taoran Li, Chaowei Xiao, Zhiyuan Yu, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: AutoDojo introduces adaptive attacks against LLM agent defenses to indirect prompt injection, showing static benchmarks like AgentDojo fail to capture robustness to adaptive threats. It exposes superficial defenses and limits stemming from user underspecification.

entry.title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving

author.name: Ruicheng Ao, Jing Dong, Gan Luo, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: Develops a discrete-time dynamical model of memory-constrained LLM serving where growing KV caches cause endogenous congestion and request eviction, analyzing eviction-free fixed points and limit behavior under continuous batching. Provides theoretical grounding for serving system design.

entry.title: PO-PDDL: Learning Symbolic POMDPs from Visual Demonstrations for Robot Planning Under Uncertainty

author.name: Wenjing Tang, Xuanjin Jin, Yuan Liu, Renming Huang, Cewu Lu, Panpan Cai

entry.summary: PO-PDDL extends PDDL to symbolically model partially observable, stochastic POMDPs with beliefs while retaining LLM-friendly syntax, plus a pipeline that learns these models from real-robot execution videos. Targets robot planning under uncertainty.

entry.title: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0: Can LLMs Find the Same Bugs Twice?

author.name: Liran Tal, Johannes Kloos, Arsenii Rudich, Stephen Thoemmes, Manoj Nair

entry.summary: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0 runs 300 repeated agentic LLM vulnerability scans on identical JavaScript code to measure repeatability, finding reference-matched findings are stable while extra model reports vary heavily across runs (many appearing in only one of five repetitions). Highlights reliability concerns for LLM security review.

entry.title: The Truth Stays in the Family: Enhancing Contextual Grounding via Inherited Truthful Heads in Model Lineages

author.name: Miso Choi, Seonga Choi, Mincheol Kwon, Woosung Joung, Jinkyu Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: Shows that head-level context-truthfulness scores are strongly preserved within model families (Vicuna, Qwen2.5, LLaMA2, Mistral lineages) even after instruction tuning or multimodal adaptation, with truthful heads attending to query-relevant evidence. Leverages inherited truthful heads to enhance contextual grounding.

entry.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models

author.name: Naiyu Yin, Dennis Wei, Tian Gao, Amit Dhurandhar, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy, Yue Yu

entry.summary: CircuitLasso is a scalable circuit-learning method using sparse linear regression over sparse-autoencoder features that matches intervention-based circuit accuracy at a fraction of the compute. It makes interpretable circuit discovery over high-dimensional SAE features tractable.

entry.title: A Decision-Theoretic View of Test-Time Training: When, How Far, and Which Directions to Adapt

author.name: Tomoya Wakayama

entry.summary: Provides a decision-theoretic analysis of test-time training as implicit Bayesian inference in the kernel regime, showing TTT helps when updates are spectrally matched to signal-to-noise ratio and aligned with query-relevant eigendirections. Explains TTT instability and motivates adaptive update schemes.

entry.title: ReQAT: Achieving Full-Precision Reasoning Accuracy with 4-bit Floating-Point Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Janghwan Lee, Sihwa Lee, Jinseok Kim, Yongjik Kim, Jieun Lim, Jinwook Oh, Jungwook Choi

entry.summary: ReQAT is a reasoning-centric FP4 quantization-aware training framework that recovers full-precision reasoning accuracy under aggressive W4A4KV4 quantization. It identifies that FP4 failures concentrate on low-entropy symbolic tokens (digits, operators) and uses trace-aligned training to fix them.

entry.title: Mixtures of Subspaces for Bandwidth Efficient Context Parallel Training

author.name: Sameera Ramasinghe, Ajanthan Thalaiyasingam, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Yan Zuo, Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Alexander Long

entry.summary: Proposes a communication-efficient context-parallel training method for decentralized low-bandwidth settings by exploiting the intrinsic low-rank structure of activations using dynamically constructed mixtures of subspaces. Achieves over 95% compression with negligible overhead and no convergence loss.

entry.title: Privacy from Symmetry: Orthogonally Equivariant Transformers for LLM Inference

author.name: Alexander Yukhimchuk, Andrey Shulga, Mladen Kolar, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}

entry.summary: Proposes ConjFormer, an orthogonally-equivariant transformer variant enabling privacy-preserving split inference: clients multiply embeddings by a secret orthogonal matrix, and the model performs correct inference under arbitrary rotations via scalar RMSNorm and blockwise orthogonal conjugation. This prevents nearest-neighbor recovery of tokens from transmitted representations.

entry.title: Identification and Inference for Algorithmic Frontiers with Selective Labels

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Francesca Molinari, Amilcar Velez

entry.summary: This paper provides identification results and statistical inference tools for characterizing fairness-accuracy frontiers when outcomes are observed only for selected individuals (selective labels). It includes a debiased ML estimator with asymptotic distribution under unconfoundedness.

entry.title: Stop When Further Reasoning Won't Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation in Reasoning Models

author.name: Jiakai Li, Ke Qin, Rongzheng Wang, Yizhuo Ma, Qizhi Chen, Muquan Li, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: ASAG is a training-free method that infers a reasoning model's state from attention distributions to adaptively stop generation and reduce overthinking. It mitigates redundant token output and accuracy degradation without prompts or confidence signals.

entry.title: Calibrated Triage, Not Autonomy: Confidence Estimation for Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Reza Khanmohammadi, Kundan Thind, Mohammad M. Ghassemi

entry.summary: Evaluates seven confidence estimators across five medical vision-language models and three VQA datasets, framing the question as how much imaging work a model can safely handle alone. It argues for calibrated triage and abstention rather than autonomy.

entry.title: PathRouter: Aligning Rewards with Retrieval Quality in Agentic Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Bo Wang, Heyan Huang, Yaolin Li, Wei Tang, Yuan Zhang, Wenbo Li, Mingze Gao, Ge Shi, Chong Feng

entry.summary: PathRouter is a path-aware training framework for agentic GraphRAG that addresses answer-path reward aliasing and search-update ambiguity in outcome-only RL by jointly evaluating answer correctness and evidence-path quality. It aligns rewards with retrieval quality.

entry.title: Uncertainty Is Not a Safety Net for Clinical VQA, but Can It Anticipate Model Failure?

author.name: Arnisa Fazla, Alberto Testoni, Ameen Abu-Hanna, Barbara Plank, Iacer Calixto

entry.summary: Benchmarks 8 uncertainty estimation methods across 12 clinical VLMs on VQA, finding UE quality tracks model accuracy and degrades precisely where reliability is most needed. It shows accuracy collapses under NOTA perturbations while uncertainty barely changes.

entry.title: Learning Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging

author.name: Haoxu Huang, Long Chen, Jingyun Chen, Jinu Hyun, James Ryan Loftus, Kara Melmed, Daniel Orringer, Jennifer Frontera, Seena Dehkharghani, Arjun Masurkar, Narges Razavian

entry.summary: Neuro-JEPA is a sparse multimodal neuroimaging foundation model combining a latent predictive (JEPA) objective with a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode brain MRI across T1w, T2w, and FLAIR contrasts. It provides a systematic study of architecture, masking, objective, and sparsity design choices.

entry.title: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Mina Mohammadmirzaei, Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: OSGuard is a dual-granularity benchmark for safety in computer-use agents, evaluating both action-level guardrail decisions and end-to-end execution under benign instructions. It targets unsafe shortcuts that task-success metrics miss.

entry.title: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking

author.name: Jiwan Chung, JiHyuk Byun, Vibhav Vineet, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: WebStep is a benchmark of 1,800 web-agent tasks with automatic semantic state tracking via a deterministic semantic MDP alongside the GUI, enabling process-level rather than terminal-success evaluation. Reveals differences invisible to outcome-only metrics.

entry.title: LLM-as-Code Agentic Programming for Agent Harness

author.name: Junjia Qi, Zichuan Fu, Jingtong Gao, Wenlin Zhang, Hanyu Yan, Xian Wu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Argues that token explosion, control-flow hallucination, and unreliable completion in LLM agents stem from assigning deterministic control flow to a probabilistic system, and proposes Agentic Programming where the program governs control flow and the LLM (LLM-as-Code) is invoked only for reasoning. Reframes agent architecture.

entry.title: Looking Is Not Picking: An Attention-Segment Account of Tool-Selection Failures in LLM Agents

author.name: Shiyang Chen

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agent tool-selection failures occur at the decision readout, not at attention to the right tool, finding the model attends most to the correct tool 80% of the time yet still picks wrong. Refutes the crowded-harness/lost-in-the-middle explanation through attention-segment analysis on BFCL failures.

entry.title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?

author.name: Triveni Morla, Rohith Reddy Bellibaltu, Manpreet Singh, Manmeet Singh Kapoor

entry.summary: AgentFairBench is a multi-domain benchmark measuring demographic disparity in the actions of LLM agents across hiring, lending, and medical triage, using counterfactual matched profiles varying only race-gender signals. Moves fairness evaluation from grading answers to assessing actions under increasing agency scaffolds.

entry.title: X-Tokenizer: A Multimodal Action Tokenizer for Vision-Language-Action Pretraining

author.name: Xirui Kang, Yanpei Shi, Lucy Liang, Roy Gan, Dongxiu Liu, Pushi Zhang, Danpeng Chen, Xiaoyi Qin, Yinan Zheng, Jinliang Zheng, Hao Wang, Xianyuan Zhan, Hang Su

entry.summary: X-Tokenizer reframes action tokenization for Vision-Language-Action models as semantic interface learning, using a Semantic Residual Quantization encoder-decoder to provide a shared action interface across diverse robotic arm embodiments. Aims to give stronger semantic supervision to the VLA backbone than reconstruction-only tokenizers.

entry.title: Efficient Reinforcement for Visual-Textual Thinking with Discrete Diffusion Model

author.name: Yoonjeon Kim, Yuhta Takida, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Eunho Yang, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: This work shows multimodal discrete diffusion models are effective for RL post-training of interleaved visual-textual reasoning, enabling efficient localized image editing instead of full image regeneration. It reduces GRPO rollout computation by about 27% versus autoregressive baselines with minimal performance loss.

entry.title: FastMix: Fast Data Mixture Optimization via Gradient Descent

author.name: Haoru Tan, Sitong Wu, Yanfeng Chen, Jun Xia, Ruobing Xie, Bin Xia, Xingwu Sun, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: FastMix automates pretraining/post-training data mixture discovery by jointly optimizing mixture coefficients and model parameters using a single proxy model, reformulating mixture selection as bilevel optimization via gradient descent. It shows optimizing mixture ratios is equivalent to a weight-assignment problem, improving efficiency over heuristics and simulations.

entry.title: Resilient Consensus in Agentic AI

author.name: Sribalaji C. Anand, George J. Pappas

entry.summary: This paper tests whether classical resilient Byzantine consensus theory transfers to LLM agents, finding that prompted LLM agents fail to reach agreement achievable in principle even where convergence is guaranteed. Wrapping agents with classical resilient consensus filters restores agreement.

entry.title: Spokes: Optimizing for Diverse Pretraining Data Selection

author.name: Clarence Lee, Yejin Choi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: Spokes directly optimizes diversity in pretraining data selection via a probabilistic diversification framework based on the G-Vendi score, optimized with exponentiated gradient descent, rather than relying on proxies. It produces substantially more diverse subsets than random sampling.

entry.title: T-Mem: Memory That Anticipates, Not Archives

author.name: Weidong Guo, Dakai Wang, Zixuan Wang, Hui Liu, Yu Xu

entry.summary: T-Mem proposes an anticipatory long-term memory for conversational agents that retrieves associatively (latent semantic arcs) rather than just by surface lexical/vector similarity, addressing failures on queries that share no surface features with memories.

entry.title: Vernier: Probing Representational Misalignment Behind Lexical Gaps in Causal Reasoning

author.name: Zhenyu Yu

entry.summary: Vernier probes why instruction-tuned models answer causal-reasoning questions differently when variable names are replaced by placeholders, using paired-view weight updates and activation patching to show the gap reflects representational misalignment rather than information loss. Reveals answer-relevant content survives in placeholder representations.

entry.title: OmniTraffic: A Controllable Generation Pipeline and Benchmark for Spatio-Temporal Traffic Reasoning

author.name: Maonan Wang, Zhengyan Huang, Kemou Jiang, Yuhang Fu, Jiayue Zhu, Yuxin Cai, Xingchen Zou, Qiaosheng Zhang, Yi Yu, Ding Wang, Xi Chen, Ben M. Chen, Yuxuan Liang, Zhiyong Cui, Man On Pun, Yirong Chen

entry.summary: OmniTraffic is a controllable generation pipeline and benchmark for spatio-temporal traffic reasoning, built around 12 real intersections reconstructed as editable 3D environments plus surveillance footage, supporting evaluation of lane topology, multi-view geometry, temporal evolution, and signal-phase reasoning. Goes beyond passive visual recognition.

entry.title: Deep Residual Injection for Full-Spectrum Forensic Signal Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kaiqing Lin, Zhiyuan Yan, Ruoxin Chen, Ke-Yue Zhang, Yue Zhou, Caiyong Piao, Bin Li, Taiping Yao, Bo Wang, Youchang Xiao, Shouhong Ding

entry.summary: Deep Residual Injection enables full-spectrum forensic signal perception in MLLMs for AI-generated image detection, using layer-wise analysis showing semantic information forms in early-to-middle layers while artifact fine-tuning disrupts it, then injecting low-level generator artifacts without sacrificing semantic knowledge. Targets robust deepfake detection.

entry.title: Intelligence Is Not the Bottleneck: Validating an LLM First-Pass Manuscript Score Against Peer-Review Outcomes

author.name: Costa Georgantas

entry.summary: Validates AIPR, an LLM first-pass manuscript scorer that emits five quality dimensions and a weighted overall score by prompting alone, against public ICLR decision outcomes across 300 submissions with pre-registered hypotheses, achieving AUROC 0.82 separating accepted from rejected. Argues intelligence is not the bottleneck for review assistance.

entry.title: Do Safety Monitors Stay Reliable After an Update? Benchmarking and Predicting Activation-Monitor Staleness

author.name: Evan Duan

entry.summary: First systematic study of whether frozen activation-based safety monitors remain reliable after routine model updates like quantization, fine-tuning, or LoRA. Finds quantization preserves probe performance while fine-tuning frequently makes probes stale.

entry.title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion

author.name: Soham Bhattacharjee, Dushyant Singh Chauhan, Salem Lahlou, Martin Takac, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion introduces a second, fully deterministic axis for inference-time scaling by recursively re-applying a frozen model's top decoder layers at high-uncertainty tokens. Different layer spans solve different problem subsets without stochastic sampling.

entry.title: Demystifying Variance in Circuit Discovery of LLMs

author.name: Frank Zhengqing Wu, Francesco Tonin, Volkan Cevher

entry.summary: This paper investigates and reduces the variance afflicting LLM circuit discovery, characterizing resampling, rephrasing, and sample-wise variance and proposing CEAP to improve stability over the EAP-IG method. It strengthens the reliability of mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Phantoms and Disclosures: a Causal Framework for Auditing Synthetic Data

author.name: Kareem Amin, Rudrajit Das, Alessandro Epasto, Adel Javanmard, Dennis Kraft, M\'onica Ribero, Sergei Vassilvitskii

entry.summary: This paper presents a customizable empirical auditing framework that distinguishes true disclosures, where synthetic data directly reproduces user information, from phantom disclosures, where it incidentally generates similar data, via train/holdout partitioning. It provides a causal lens for auditing privacy leakage in generative synthetic data.

entry.title: Semantic DLM+: Improving Diffusion Language Models through Bias-variance Trade-off in Transition Kernel Design

author.name: Keyue Jiang, Yuxiang Wang, Yanan Zhao, Xiang Yu, Qifang Zhao, Bohan Tang, Baojian Zhou, Yanghua Xiao, Lin Qu, Xiaoxiao Xu

entry.summary: Semantic DLM+ analyzes how transition kernel choice affects diffusion language model performance through a bias-variance lens, identifying asymptotic bias, exposure bias, and optimization variance. It proposes improved kernel designs to stabilize training and reduce biased sampling.

entry.title: DiRecT: Safe Diffusion-Based Planning via Receding-Horizon Denoising

author.name: Paolo Giaretta, Zeyang Li, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: DiRecT is a training-free algorithm for safe diffusion-based planning that enforces constraints only on the final clean trajectory via receding-horizon denoising with terminal constraints, rather than projecting noisy intermediates. This avoids overconstraining sampling dynamics and preserves sample quality.

entry.title: Formalizing and Mitigating Structural Distortion in LLM Attention for Zero-Shot Graph Reasoning

author.name: Donald Loveland, Puja Trivedi, Ari Weinstein, Edward W Huang, Danai Koutra

entry.summary: Formalizes how rotary positional embeddings turn graph linearization into bandwidth-dependent attention decay, suppressing attention between graph-adjacent but sequence-distant nodes in LLM graph reasoning. Proposes mechanism-based attention correction rather than prompt engineering.

entry.title: Mean-Field Parallel Decoding for Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tamim Zoabi, Ameen Ali, Liran Ringel, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free mean-field decoding framework for discrete diffusion language models that coordinates parallel token updates via pairwise interaction refinement of commit scores. A variational relaxation yields a fixed-point update that suppresses conflicting simultaneous commitments to improve effective parallelism.

entry.title: MUNI: Multimodal Unified Latent Diffusion for Coherent Any-to-Any Generation

author.name: Kyeongmin Yeo, Yunhong Min, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: MUNI is an end-to-end multimodal latent diffusion framework for any-to-any generation that unifies subset-conditioned cross-modal generation and unconditional joint sampling through a shared stochastic latent. Unlike LLM-based or text-aligned approaches, it does not require text-paired or fully-paired training data.

entry.title: Taylor-Calibrate: Principled Initialization for Hybrid Linear Attention Distillation

author.name: Zhongzhu Zhou, Qingyang Wu, Junxiong Wang, Mayank Mishra, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Ben Athiwaratkun, Chenfeng Xu

entry.summary: Taylor-Calibrate provides principled initialization for converting pretrained Transformers into hybrid linear-attention models (Gated DeltaNet students), since naively copying attention projections leaves recurrent decay, write, and output-gating dynamics unspecified. It calibrates the student to start in a good dynamical regime, reducing distillation tokens needed.

entry.title: Multimodal Evaluator Preference Collapse: Cross-Modal Contagion in Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: This paper shows that Evaluator Preference Collapse in self-evolving agents is amplified in multimodal settings, with one strategy absorbing 48 percent of weight. It introduces cross-modal contagion, where preferences learned on one modality corrupt strategy selection on another.

entry.title: From Tokens to Policy: Causal and Interpretable Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Identification

author.name: Riccardo Cadei, Frank Otchere, Nyasha Tirivayi, Gustavo Angeles Tagliaferro, Falco J. Bargagli-Stoffi, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work reframes heterogeneous treatment effect identification as a Markov-blanket discovery problem using multimodal pre-treatment measurements and scalable representations. It aims for causal and interpretable HTE identification even when some heterogeneity drivers are unmeasured.

entry.title: Audited Conformal Prediction for Classification under Unknown Distribution Shift

author.name: Yanfei Zhou, Rizal Fathony, Nam H. Nguyen, Matteo Sesia

entry.summary: Audited Conformal Prediction trains an auxiliary audit model on a small target-population labeled set to identify where a deployed classifier is likely to fail under unknown distribution shift. It integrates these signals into conformal prediction to maintain marginal coverage while improving conditional coverage.

entry.title: Distilling latent electrostatics from foundation machine learning interatomic potentials

author.name: Xiaoyu Wang, Bingqing Cheng

entry.summary: This work uses Latent Ewald Summation to extract latent electrostatics implicit in foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials, training a lightweight student model from teacher energies and forces. It adds explicit long-range electrostatics to foundation MLIPs that otherwise lack them.

entry.title: Replay What Matters: Off-Policy Replay for Efficient LLM Reinforcement Unlearning
