entry.summary: Introduces the Social World Model (SWM) framework, which uses LLMs to learn state-transition functions for how social beliefs evolve following major events, optimizing an evidence lower bound without human annotations or census data. Matters because it offers a computational approach to modeling social belief dynamics in social science.

entry.title: Which Speech Representation Better Matches Text-Native Reasoning? A Study of Speech-Text Alignment on Frame Rate and Representation

author.name: Zhen Ye, Xu Tan, Yiming Li, Guangyan Zhang, Chimin Chan, Haohe Liu, Zhengxi Liu, Hongzhan Lin, Zheqi Dai, Xinshen Zhang, Peiwen Sun, Qiuqiang Kong, Wei Xue

entry.summary: Studies why reasoning degrades when LLMs condition on speech instead of text, attributing it to temporal-granularity mismatch, and explores frame-rate and representation design with factorized FSQ and a non-autoregressive audio LM head. Relevant for improving spoken dialogue models.

entry.title: Damage-TriageFormer: A Foundation-Model Framework for Typology-Based Building Damage Assessment from Mono-Temporal Imagery

author.name: Yiming Xiao, Yu-Hsuan Ho, Sanjay Thasma, Junwei Ma, Ali Mostafavi

entry.summary: Presents Damage-TriageFormer, a single-image post-event footprint-conditioned foundation-model framework producing a building damage typology rather than a severity scale, with the DamageTriage-Bench benchmark spanning hurricanes and wildfires. Addresses limitations of severity scales and the unavailability of pre-event imagery for disaster response.

entry.title: How Seemingly Inconsequential Design Choices Dictate Performance of LLMs in Pathology

author.name: Kian R. Weihrauch, Thomas A. Buckley, William Lotter, Arjun K. Manrai

entry.summary: A systematic factorial analysis showing that seemingly trivial design choices (patch size, count, magnification, inference mode) dramatically affect general-purpose LLM performance on whole-slide pathology images. It challenges the assumption that domain-specific training is necessary by showing generalist LLM baselines are often unfairly configured.

entry.title: GraphGP: Scalable Gaussian Processes with Vecchia's Approximation

author.name: Benjamin Dodge, Philipp Frank, Susan E. Clark

entry.summary: Presents GraphGP, a GPU algorithm for Vecchia's approximation of Gaussian processes that scales to nearly a billion parameters with linear time and memory, using a bit-reversed k-d tree ordering and a differentiable CUDA implementation. It dramatically extends the practical scale of GP modeling.

entry.title: EC2’s formally verified “isolation engine” provides mathematical assurance of virtual-machine isolation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon announces the M9g/M9gd EC2 instances powered by Graviton5 and the new Nitro Isolation Engine, the first formally verified hypervisor deployed in commercial cloud, proven correct using the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant with 330,000 lines of machine-checked mathematics. It provides mathematical assurance of VM isolation.

entry.title: CRUMB: Efficient Prior Fitted Network Inference via Distributionally Matched Context Batching

author.name: Jamie Heredge, Mattia J. Villani, Pranav Deshpande, Akshay Seshadri, Niraj Kumar

entry.summary: CRUMB is an inference wrapper for prior-fitted tabular networks that clusters test queries and selects distributionally matched training subsets via MMD minimization to enable exact PFN inference on large datasets. It tackles the quadratic attention bottleneck limiting tabular foundation models.

entry.title: Physics-Distilled Neural Network enabled by Large Language Models for Manufacturing Process-Property Predictive Modeling

author.name: Ge Song, Kiarash Naghavi Khanghah, Anandkumar Patel, Rajiv Malhotra, Hongyi Xu

entry.summary: This framework uses LLMs to extract analytical physics priors from scientific literature into a privileged teacher model with graph-masked attention, then distills that knowledge into a lightweight student for data-scarce manufacturing process-property prediction. It improves accuracy and interpretability under limited data.

entry.title: Layer-Isolated Evaluation: Gating the Deterministic Scaffold of a Production LLM Agent with a No-LLM, Regression-Locked Test Harness

author.name: Sawyer Zhang, Alexander Wang, Sophie Lei

entry.summary: This paper proposes layer-isolated evaluation for production LLM agents, decomposing a deployed ordering agent into a taxonomy of layers each tested by deterministic no-LLM assertion slices in CI, validated by controlled regression injection. It reveals masking where aggregate task-success hides per-layer regressions.

entry.title: Substrate Asymmetry in User-Side Memory: A Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: This diagnostic framework decomposes user-side LLM memory into behavioral consistency, factual presence, and factual absence axes, showing no single substrate wins all three. Comparing per-user LoRA adapters against dense retrieval, it finds LoRA wins style while RAG wins factual recall, exposing trade-offs hidden by aggregate personalization metrics.

entry.title: Automated Creativity Evaluation of Language Models Across Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Min Sen Tan, Zachary Kit Chun Choy, Syed Ali Redha Alsagoff, Nadya Yuki Wangsajaya, Mohor Banerjee, Swaagat Bikash Saikia, Alvin Chan

entry.summary: This paper presents an automated, domain-agnostic framework for quantifying LLM creativity across open-ended tasks by separating the measurement apparatus from the creative task itself, measuring divergent creativity in a scalable, task-agnostic way. It addresses the over-coupling of existing creativity metrics to specific domains.

entry.title: Characterizing Software Aging in GPU-Based LLM Serving Systems

author.name: Domenico Cotroneo, Bojan Cukic

entry.summary: This paper presents an empirical methodology to characterize software aging in GPU-based LLM serving systems, running a 216-hour campaign across six co-located deployments and applying statistical analysis to find significant memory aging in all deployments with leak rates dependent on the serving runtime. It adapts aging studies to the distinctive Python-host plus CUDA-device LLM serving stack.

entry.title: Mathematical perspective on genetic algorithms with optimization guided operators

author.name: Anna Brandenberger, Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: This theoretical paper develops a mathematical model of genetic algorithms whose mutation and recombination operators are ML optimization-guided rather than random, reflecting recent inference-time evolutionary methods. It analyzes the tradeoff between higher-quality but computationally costlier operators.

entry.title: Seeing Before Colliding: Anticipatory Safe RL with Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: VLM-Safe-RL integrates a frozen vision-language model into the constrained-MDP Lagrangian update as an anticipatory cost term, addressing the structural lateness of reactive cost signals in high-speed racing where collisions are instantaneous. It uses decoupled dual-path CLIP and an augmented multiplier update.

entry.title: Learning from almost nothing: How neural networks survive heavy input corruption

author.name: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, Omri Lesser

entry.summary: This study examines how neural networks survive heavy input (attribute) corruption, finding MLPs maintain well-above-chance accuracy even with over 90% corrupted inputs, far beyond human recognition. It analyzes infinite-width networks to understand this robustness to additive and replacement noise.

entry.title: Beyond the Golden Teacher: Enhancing Graph Learning through LLM-GNN Co-teaching

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Hanlin Gu, Lixin Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the golden-teacher assumption in LLM-GNN methods for few-shot learning on text-attributed graphs, arguing neither model is reliable under sparse supervision since GNNs fail on cold nodes and LLMs fail on text-ambiguous nodes. It proposes a co-teaching framework where both models learn from each other rather than one supervising the other.

entry.title: Capacity-Constrained Online Convex Optimization with Delayed Feedback

author.name: Alexander Ryabchenko, Idan Attias, Daniel M. Roy

entry.summary: This paper studies online convex optimization with delayed feedback under a hard capacity constraint where only a limited number of pending rounds can be tracked. It introduces a semi-clairvoyant model and a reduction-based approach to a delayed-and-weighted setting.

entry.title: MemNovo: Look Back at the Spectrum for Balanced De Novo Peptide Sequencing from Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Dongxin Lyu, Jingbo Zhou, Hongxin Xiang, Yuqiang Li, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MemNovo addresses a pathology in Transformer de novo peptide sequencing where autoregressive decoders over-rely on sequence priors and under-use mass-spectrum evidence, producing plausible but unfaithful sequences. It proposes a mechanism to re-attend to the input spectrum for balanced predictions.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient On-Device RAG on a Mobile NPU: System Design and Benchmark on Snapdragon X Elite

author.name: Zhiyuan Cheng, Longying Lai

entry.summary: This work presents the first end-to-end RAG pipeline running all neural stages (embedding, reranking, LLM generation) on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU of the Snapdragon X Elite. It achieves large throughput and energy improvements over CPU and GPU baselines for on-device privacy-preserving retrieval.

entry.title: Interpretable Neural Marked Statistics for Cosmological Inference

author.name: Federico Semenzato, Benjamin D. Wandelt, Michele Liguori, Alvise Raccanelli

entry.summary: This work proposes a neural marking scheme for cosmological inference that generalizes marked statistics through interpretable, physically motivated field transformations to access non-Gaussian information beyond the power spectrum. It uses contrastive learning to align marked summaries with cosmological parameters.

entry.title: Enhancing Spectral Embedding through Robust and Flexible Knowledge Transfer in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Feiqing Huang, Zongqi Xia, Rong Ma, Tianxi Cai

entry.summary: This work proposes a spectral-based unsupervised representation learning framework for clinical concepts and patients in rare-disease EHR cohorts, transferring knowledge from a broader population sharing a partially overlapping subspace. It relaxes restrictive one-to-one signal-alignment assumptions for more flexible structured knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Renewable Lasso without Batch-Number Constraints: A Gradient-Enhanced Approach

author.name: Junzhuo Gao, Ling Peng, Xu Guo, Heng Lian

entry.summary: This work proposes a gradient-enhanced renewable Lasso for online estimation of high-dimensional generalized linear models with streaming data that removes the batch-number constraint of prior renewable methods. It extends to distributed master-client streaming where only gradient summaries are exchanged.

entry.title: UniIntervene: Agentic Intervention for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyuan Deng, Yitong Gao, Yudong Lin, Haichao Liu, Zhenyu Wu, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: UniIntervene is an agentic intervention model for human-in-the-loop RL that detects unproductive exploration and autonomously recovers the policy toward high-value states, reducing reliance on frequent human corrections. It uses future-conditioned action-value estimation for real-world robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Beyond Compaction: Structured Context Eviction for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Andrew Semenov, Svyatoslav Dorofeev

entry.summary: Context Window Lifecycle gives long-horizon LLM agents an effectively unbounded working horizon via graduated, semantically-aware eviction of typed dependency-linked episodes when a token budget is exceeded. It preserves user turns and active reasoning context while shedding completed action episodes deterministically.

entry.title: Scenario-based Probing and Steering Cultural Values in Large Language Models--Extended Version

author.name: Trung Duc Anh Dang, Tung Kieu, Sarah Masud

entry.summary: This paper probes and steers latent cultural values in LLMs along the World Values Survey Inglehart-Welzel axes by converting survey questions into scenario-based behavioral dilemmas and applying activation steering with country-conditioned prompting. It addresses how direct survey prompting elicits neutral, safety-aligned answers that hide underlying preferences.

entry.title: Notes2Skills: From Lab Notebooks to Certainty-Aware Scientific Agent Skills

author.name: Shi Liu, Jiayao Chen, Chengwei Qin, Yanqing Hu, Jufan Zhang, Linyi Yang

entry.summary: Notes2Skills converts informal lab notebooks, which intermingle validated observations and tentative judgments, into certainty-aware scientific agent skills, an underexplored input type for AI science agents. It aims to capture evolving scientific reasoning and author uncertainty rather than polished final results.

entry.title: Gumbel-BEARD: Automatic Layer Selection for Self-Supervised Adaptation of Whisper in Low-Resource Domains

author.name: Zilai Wang, Natarajan Balaji Shankar, Mohan Shi, Kaiyuan Zhang, Abeer Alwan

entry.summary: Structured PubMed is a corpus of over 23.2 million section-labeled biomedical abstracts, with 5.9 million author-structured and 17.2 million automatically labeled, addressing the bottleneck of unstructured abstracts for biomedical text processing. It supports information retrieval, text mining, and knowledge synthesis at scale.

entry.title: Beyond Third-Person Audits: Situated Interaction Auditing for User-Centered LLM Bias Research

author.name: Andr\'es Abeliuk, Cinthia Sanchez Macias, Valentina Alarc\'on, \'Alvaro Madariaga, Claudia Lopez

entry.summary: Proposes Situated Interaction Auditing (SIA), a user-centered framework for studying how LLMs adjust responses based on inferred user demographics, addressing a blind spot in third-person bias audits. Important for understanding personalized bias in real LLM interactions.

entry.title: SheafStain: Sheaf-Theoretic Schr\"odinger Bridge for Spatially and Biologically Coherent Virtual Staining

author.name: Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon, Eunjin Jang, Daeky Jeong, Won June Cho, Hwamin Lee

entry.summary: Proposes AGE-MIL, an anchor-guided evidence multiple instance learning framework for patient-level prediction that integrates evidence across multiple whole-slide images, addressing misalignment when patient-level supervision is imposed on slide-level MIL. Relevant for computational pathology diagnostics and prognostics.

entry.title: SG2Loc: Sequential Visual Localization on 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Nicole Damblon, Olga Vysotska, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Barath

entry.summary: Introduces SG2Loc, a lightweight sequential visual localization method using compact 3D scene graphs where nodes are objects and edges encode spatial relationships, avoiding storage of large image databases or point clouds. Targets robotics and AR localization in complex indoor environments.

entry.title: DynaTok: Token-Based 4D Reconstruction from Partial Point Clouds

author.name: Weirong Chen, Keisuke Tateno, Hidenobu Matsuki, Michael Niemeyer, Daniel Cremers, Federico Tombari

entry.summary: Proposes DynaTok, a point-based framework for correspondence-free 4D reconstruction from partial, unordered point cloud sequences without images, encoding frames into compact latent tokens aggregated over time via a transformer. Addresses geometry-only dynamic reconstruction with incomplete observations.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks on Learned Policies for Surgical Robotic Tasks

author.name: Shutong Jin, Ziyang Chen, Preethi Satish, Paavan Gupta, Florian T. Pokorny, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: Presents the first study of adversarial attacks on learning-based policies in surgical robotics, investigating disruptive attacks that interrupt execution and steering attacks that redirect actions via imperceptible visual perturbations. It evaluates three attack methods with increasing policy access on surgical tasks.

entry.title: Dual-Stance Evaluation of Sycophancy: The Structure of Agreement and the Limits of Intervention

author.name: Matthew James Buchan

entry.summary: Introduces dual-stance evaluation of sycophancy, testing whether a sycophancy-reduction steering direction also suppresses agreement with factually correct statements. Finds that on Llama-3-8B, sycophantic and factual agreement occupy geometrically distinct subspaces yet the steering direction projects equally onto both, harming correctness.

entry.title: Calibration Drift Under Reasoning: How Chain-of-Thought Budgets Induce Overconfidence in Large Language Models

author.name: Prakul Sunil Hiremath, Harshit R. Hiremath

entry.summary: Identifies Calibration Drift Under Reasoning, where increasing the chain-of-thought budget beyond a threshold makes LLMs systematically overconfident on incorrect answers. It analyzes theoretically and empirically a non-monotonic relationship between reasoning budget and expected calibration error.

entry.title: When Poison Fails After Retrieval: Revisiting Corpus Poisoning under Chunking and Reranking Pipelines

author.name: Xi Nie, Hongwei Li, Shenghao Wu, Mingxuan Li, Jiachen Li, Wenbo Jiang

entry.summary: Revisits corpus poisoning attacks on RAG under realistic multi-stage pipelines (chunking, dense retrieval, reranking, grounded generation), showing many existing attacks degrade after reranking. It identifies retrieval granularity mismatch as a key reason adversarial signals fragment during chunking.

entry.title: Quantifying Subliminal Behavioral Transfer Ratios in Language Model Distillation

author.name: Uwe Konig, Hamza Kazmi, Ruizhe Li, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Quantifies subliminal behavioral transfer in distillation, steering two teacher models at varying strengths and distilling students on only benign data, then measuring undesirable trait transfer on JailbreakBench prompts. It finds robust but model-dependent transfer with distinct scaling behaviors.

entry.title: When Probing Accuracy Saturates, Fragility Resolves: A Complementary Metric for LLM Pre-Training Analysis

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: Introduces fragility, a per-layer metric defined as the activation-noise level at which probe accuracy collapses, complementing standard linear probing whose accuracy saturates early in pretraining. Applied to open checkpoints, it reveals representational structure (e.g., evolving moralized representations) that accuracy alone cannot see.

entry.title: Pretrained self-supervised speech models can recognize unseen consonants

author.name: Chihiro Taguchi, \'Eric Le Ferrand, Hirosi Nakagawa, Hitomi Ono, Kanji Kato, Emily Prud'hommeaux, David Chiang

entry.summary: This work fine-tunes self-supervised speech models (Wav2Vec2, HuBERT) on click-rich Khoisan languages to test whether typologically rare consonants are recognized as accurately as common sounds. It probes representational bias in speech foundation models toward high-resource phonologies.

entry.title: ConsistencyPlanner: Real-time Planning with Fast-Sampling Consistency Models

author.name: Qichao Zhang, Xing Fang, Jiaqi Fang, Zhenwen Cai, Jie Ling, Qiankun Yu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: ConsistencyPlanner uses fast-sampling consistency models for real-time closed-loop autonomous driving planning, balancing multimodal behavior modeling against latency to avoid indecisive or unsafe actions. It applies efficient generative sampling to safety-critical planning.

entry.title: TAROT: Task-Adaptive Refinement of LLM-prior Graphs for Few-shot Tabular Learning

author.name: Ruxue Shi, Yili Wang, Mengnan Du, Hangting Ye, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: TAROT refines LLM-derived prior graphs over tabular features in a task-adaptive way for few-shot tabular learning, avoiding extra training on generated data and the privacy concerns of feeding raw tables to LLMs. It exploits semantic feature relationships often overlooked by prior methods.

entry.title: TextHOI-3D: Text-to-3D Hand-Object Interaction via Discrete Multi-View Generation and Joint Mesh Optimization

author.name: Zixiong Hao, Zhencun Jiang

entry.summary: TextHOI-3D generates 3D hand-object interaction meshes from text via a VQ token space for fixed-camera observations, a CLIP-conditioned visual autoregressive model predicting multi-view tokens, and joint mesh recovery preserving semantics, geometry, articulated hand shape, and plausible contact. It tackles physically plausible text-to-3D HOI generation.

entry.title: Towards Data-free and Training-free Compression for Speech Foundation Models Using Parameter Clustering

author.name: Haoning Xu, Zhaoqing Li, Huimeng Wang, Youjun Chen, Chengxi Deng, Mengzhe Geng, Xunying Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes data-free and training-free compression of speech foundation models via channelwise k-means parameter clustering, with mixed-sparsity pruning that varies cluster counts per layer, achieving large WER reductions over magnitude pruning on LibriSpeech. It enables compression without calibration data or retraining.

entry.title: Fine-tuning Multi-modal LLMs with ART: Art-based Reinforcement Training

author.name: Michal Chudoba, Sergey Alyaev, Petra Galuscakova, Tomasz Wiktorski

entry.summary: ART (Art-based Reinforcement Training) is a PEFT method that injects information into a frozen multimodal LLM by optimizing only its raw visual input via backpropagation, enabling a soft-token approach on precompiled computational graphs unsupported by engines like vLLM. It avoids modifying the model's computational graph unlike LoRA or soft prompting.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations of Individual Behavior

author.name: Andrew Kang, Priya Narasimhan

entry.summary: Behavioral INR is a self-supervised generative model that adapts implicit neural representations from vision to behavior, representing each policy as a state-action function modulated by an episode-level latent via FiLM layers. It enables policy identification from unlabeled multi-policy behavioral data.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Disrupts Gradient-Based Adversarial Optimization

author.name: Xinhai Zou, Chang Zhao, Alireza Aghabagherloo, Dave Singel\'ee, Robin Degraeve, Bart Preneel

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether reinforcement learning training (policy-gradient with epsilon-greedy exploration) can disrupt the gradient structure exploited by gradient-based adversarial attacks on image classifiers. Experiments across CIFAR and ImageNet-100 show RL-trained classifiers significantly disrupt adversarial optimization, with mechanism analysis via loss landscape visualization.

entry.title: ProHiFlo: Hierarchical Flow Matching with Functional Guidance for De Novo Protein Generation

author.name: Chuanzhen Wang, Meade Cleti, Pete Jano

entry.summary: ProHiFlo is a hierarchical flow matching framework for de novo protein generation that models backbone geometry coarsely before refining to all-atom coordinates, with functional guidance from pretrained predictors and an adaptive SE(3)-equivariant architecture. It reduces computational cost while incorporating functional constraints.

entry.title: Recursive Binding on a Budget: Subspace Carving in Order-p Tensor Memories

author.name: Travis Pence, Daisuke Yamada, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: Orthogonal Subspace Carving binds fillers to roles in tensor product representations by projecting onto the null space of the role basis before aggregating into a fixed order-p tensor, decoupling tensor order from structural depth. It bridges the fidelity of tensor product representations with the constant dimensionality of vector symbolic architectures.

entry.title: OmniLoc: A Geometry-Aware Foundation Model for Anchor-Free UE Localization Across Diverse Indoor Environments

author.name: Lei Chu, Yuning Zhang, Omer Gokalp Serbetci, Anushka Katiyar, Bassel Abou Ali Modad, Andreas F. Molisch

entry.summary: OmniLoc is a geometry-aware foundation model for anchor-free user equipment localization across diverse indoor environments directly from wireless measurements, addressing variation in building geometry, detectable access points, and signal heterogeneity. It is claimed to be the first foundation-model approach for this wireless localization task.

entry.title: APEX: A Network-Native Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting and Anomaly Detection for Wireless Edge Operations

author.name: Swadhin Pradhan, Niloo Bahadori, Peiman Amini

entry.summary: APEX is a network-native decoder-only transformer foundation model for forecasting and anomaly detection on wireless network telemetry, pre-trained on ~100K AP time series from ~4,500 production networks. It reduces MAE by 18% over the strongest foundation-model baseline on DHCP degradation, with edge and cloud variants.

entry.title: Range-Aware Bayesian Optimization for Discovering Diverse Designs within Target Property Windows

author.name: Shengli Jiang, Jason Wu, Charles M. Schroeder, Michael A. Webb

entry.summary: This paper develops range-aware Bayesian optimization where the acquisition function scores the posterior probability that a candidate satisfies a target property window rather than a single optimum, and extends to parallel pursuit of multiple distinct specifications over a shared space. It recovers diverse solutions valuable for cost, processability, or robustness considerations in materials design.

entry.title: TimeRouter: Efficient and Adaptive Routing of Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kanghui Ning, Yushan Jiang, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Dongjin Song

entry.summary: TimeRouter is a lightweight routing framework that selects among multiple pretrained time-series foundation models without relying on expensive LLM controllers. It uses discriminative routing, selective gating, and ensemble fallback to match models to forecasting regimes.

entry.title: Space-sampled Value Decay: Forgetting Mechanisms for Non-stationary Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Felix St\"orck, Fabian Hinder, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: Space-sampled Value Decay introduces an explicit forgetting mechanism for value-based deep RL in non-stationary environments that does not require task IDs or context information about drift. It is inspired by rodent behavioral adaptation.

entry.title: HAMNO: A Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-scale Neural Operator with Physics-Informed Learning for Dynamical Systems

author.name: Mostafa Bamdad, Mohammad Sadegh Eshaghi, Timon Rabczuk

entry.summary: HAMNO is a hierarchical adaptive multi-scale neural operator combining local convolutions, global spectral operators, and a data-dependent gating mechanism for learning solutions to nonlinear time-dependent PDEs. It targets multi-scale structures and stable long-time evolution.

entry.title: Efficient Multinomial Logistic Bandit via Frequent Directions

author.name: Linzhe He, Yu-Jie Zhang, Sifan Yang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: EOFD-MLogB integrates frequent-directions matrix sketching into multinomial logistic bandits to drastically reduce per-round time and space costs while preserving regret guarantees. It addresses the prohibitive computational cost of UCB-type methods in high dimensions.

entry.title: Holding the FP8 Quality Ceiling at 8-Bit Weights and Activations: INT8 and GGUF Post-Training Quantization of Ideogram 4.0 for Consumer GPUs

author.name: Deep Gandhi, Ali Asaria, Tony Salomone

entry.summary: This paper studies INT8 and GGUF post-training quantization of Ideogram 4.0, a 9.3B flow-matching diffusion transformer, to run on consumer Ampere GPUs that lack FP8 tensor cores. The INT8 W8A8 recipe with SmoothQuant and mixed-precision protection matches FP8 quality on a 200-prompt benchmark.

entry.title: A2SG:Adaptive and Asymmetric Surrogate Gradients for Training Deep Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Yechan Kang, Yongjin Kweon, Mingyeong Seo, Sohee Park, Yeonguk Jeon, Jongkil Park, Hyun Jae Jang, Jaewook Kim, YeonJoo Jeong, Suyoun Lee, Seongsik Park

entry.summary: A2SG is a unified framework of adaptive and asymmetric surrogate gradients for training deep spiking neural networks, reducing spatial gradient variation and assigning larger gradients to higher-membrane-potential neurons. It proves lower variation than symmetric surrogates and connects gradient variation to loss curvature.

entry.title: Geometric bias in eigenspace perturbation under random heterogeneous noise

author.name: Fengkai Liu, Ke Wang, Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes spectral perturbation of signal-plus-noise matrices under sparse, inhomogeneous-variance noise, showing a geometric bias that classical Davis-Kahan and Wedin bounds fail to capture. It provides finer-grained analysis of how signal geometry interacts with the noise distribution.

entry.title: Massive Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting

author.name: Leonor Barreiros, Raul Monteiro, Afonso Mendes, Gon\c{c}alo M. Correia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a massive open-vocabulary keyword spotting system that stores features with up to 128x smaller memory footprint, enabling contextual biasing over very large glossaries. It achieves comparable entity recall to uncompressed solutions without fine-tuning the speech model, even in unseen languages.

entry.title: SPADE: Split-and-Delay Embeddings for Autoregressive High-Granularity Calorimeter Simulation

author.name: Joschka Birk, Frank Gaede, Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Martina Mozzanica, Henning Rose

entry.summary: SPADE is an autoregressive transformer for multi-feature tokens that embeds features independently and delays each feature stream so self-attention learns intra-token correlations. Applied to calorimeter shower generation, it is competitive with state-of-the-art and substantially beats a VQ-VAE predecessor.

entry.title: Neural-Parameterized Cellular Automata for Wildfire Spread

author.name: Maksym Zhenirovskyy, Ion Matei, Rohit Vuppala, Takuya Kurihana, Hon Yung Wonga

entry.summary: This work introduces a hybrid deep-learning parameterized probabilistic cellular automata framework for wildfire spread, using a multi-scale CNN to dynamically generate spatially varying spread parameters. The JAX implementation enables hardware acceleration and gradient-based calibration while preserving physical interpretability.

entry.title: Seeing Below the Limit of Detection: A Censored-Poisson Bayesian Latent-Growth Change-Point Detector (the Span Detector) for Serial ctDNA in HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer

author.name: Aarchi Singh Thakur, Abhijoy Sarkar

entry.summary: Span is a censored-Poisson Bayesian latent-growth change-point detector for serial ctDNA in metastatic breast cancer, treating non-detects as left-censored observations to spot tumor growth below the assay detection limit. It aims to detect drug resistance earlier than conventional snapshot-based liquid biopsy interpretation.

entry.title: When More Documents Hurt RAG: Mitigating Vector Search Dilution with Domain-Scoped, Model-Agnostic Retrieval

author.name: Nabaraj Subedi, Ahmed Abdelaty, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: This work identifies vector search dilution, where scaling RAG to large heterogeneous corpora causes top-k retrieval to return similar-but-wrong chunks, observed in a deployed transportation corpus dropping accuracy from 75% to under 40%. It proposes MASDR-RAG, a multi-agent domain-scoped retrieval method evaluated across backbones and corpora.

entry.title: Context-Aware Multimodal Claim Verification in Spoken Dialogues

author.name: Chaewan Chun, Delvin Ce Zhang, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: MAD2 is a new benchmark of 1,000 two-speaker spoken dialogues with 3,368 check-worthy claims for multimodal claim verification, paired with a calibrated fusion of context-aware audio and dialogue-aware text models. It addresses under-studied spoken misinformation built conversationally across turns.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Resolution Procedural Knowledge Compression for Large Language Models

author.name: Changyue Wang, Weihang Su, Qingyao Ai, Yichen Tang, Runzhong Qiao, Xuancheng Li, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes adaptive multi-resolution compression of procedural knowledge (reusable LLM skills) that preserves logical dependencies among workflows and tool protocols, unlike methods designed for factual document compression. It reduces prefill cost and latency from repeatedly placing full skill text in context.

entry.title: Verifiable Environments Are LEGO Bricks: Recursive Composition for Reasoning Generalization

author.name: Hao Xiang, Qiaoyu Tang, Le Yu, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han, Ben He, Le Sun, Bowen Yu, Peng Wang, Hongyu Lin, Dayiheng Liu

entry.summary: Gumbel-BEARD automates Whisper encoder layer selection for self-supervised domain adaptation via an end-to-end trainable hard Gumbel-Softmax selector with a BEST-RQ objective, adapting to target acoustics without manual tuning. On child speech, 10 hours of labeled data matches a fully supervised 133-hour baseline, setting new SOTA WERs.

entry.title: DarkVGGT: Seeing Through Darkness Using Thermal Geometry without Daylight Tax

author.name: Minseong Kweon, Wenyuan Zhao, Nuo Chen, Lulin Liu, Huiwen Han, Zihao Zhu, Srinivas Shakkottai, Chao Tian, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: Proposes DarkVGGT, an RGB-thermal feed-forward 3D geometry framework using physics-aware thermal modeling for robust reconstruction in low-light environments without sacrificing daylight performance. Addresses the vulnerability of visible-light methods in dark scenes.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Benchmarking for Robotic Perception in Natural Environments

author.name: David Hall, Joshua Knights, Mark Cox, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Expands analysis of the WildCross benchmark for place recognition and metric depth estimation in large-scale natural environments (476K+ RGB frames with depth, normals, pose, and lidar submaps), showing limitations of urban-trained foundation models in field robotics. Important for robust perception in unstructured settings.

entry.title: SpecLoR: Spectral Lookahead Rectification for Motion-Coherent Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Xu Zhang, Yu Lu, Ruijie Quan, Zhaozheng Chen, Bohan Wang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SpecLoR, a plug-and-play inference method for flow-matching text-to-video generation that uses spectral lookahead rectification to correct accumulated trajectory drift causing spatiotemporal inconsistencies. Improves motion coherence without heavy spatial intervention.

entry.title: Q-Fold: Query-Aware Focus-Context Spatio-Temporal Folding for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Biao Tang, Xu Chen, Shuxiang Gou, Jingyi Yuan, Yuhan Zhang, Chenqiang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Q-Fold, a training-free query-aware focus-context spatio-temporal folding framework for long-video understanding that allocates representation budget by importance rather than treating frames uniformly. Aims to preserve high-fidelity evidence and broad temporal coverage within limited visual budgets.

entry.title: SHERPA: Seam-aware Harmonized ERP Adaptation for Open-Domain 360$^\circ$ Panorama Generation

author.name: Jungwoon Kang, Jaehun Kim, Yiwon Yu, Hyungyum Jang, Sanghoon Lee, Jongyoo Kim

entry.summary: Presents SHERPA, a lightweight adaptation framework for open-domain 360-degree panorama generation that aligns planar-trained diffusion models with equirectangular topology via circular RoPE, circular latent encoding, FFN adapters, and dual-path training. Addresses seam and polar-region distortions in panorama synthesis.

entry.title: PLUME: Probabilistic Latent Unified World Modeling and Parameter Estimation for Multi-Finger Manipulation

author.name: Abhinav Kumar, Soshi Iba, Rana Soltani Zarrin, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: Proposes PLUME, a probabilistic latent world model for multi-finger dexterous manipulation that jointly evolves a belief over uncertain physical parameters (shape, pose, friction) and predicts dynamics. It aims to handle deployment-time uncertainty for precise tasks like screwdriver turning beyond standard domain randomization.

entry.title: Fibration Trees: A Unified Approach to Multi-Robot Motion Planning

author.name: Andreas Orthey, Florian T. Pokorny, Lydia E. Kavraki

entry.summary: Introduces fibration trees, a unified mathematical framework for multi-robot motion planning that models projections as fibrations to unify sequential prioritization, parallel decomposition, and task-space projections under one formalism. It addresses the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional multi-robot planning.

entry.title: INFRAMIND: Infrastructure-Aware Multi-Agent Orchestration

author.name: Ahasan Kabir, Jiaqi Xue, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: INFRAMIND adds infrastructure awareness (GPU queue depths, KV-cache pressure, latencies) to multi-agent LLM orchestration, addressing how routing that ignores runtime serving state causes resource underutilization. It aims to reduce compounding delays across sequential multi-agent calls.

entry.title: HERO: Hindsight-Enhanced Reflection from Environment Observations for Agentic Self-Distillation

author.name: Haoran Liu, Yuwei Zhang, Xiyao Li, Bohan Lyu, Jingbo Shang

entry.summary: HERO is a hindsight-enhanced self-distillation framework for multi-turn agents that addresses credit assignment by aligning privileged feedback with the student's current decision context, avoiding the degradation seen in naive extensions. It converts feedback into dense token-level supervision.

entry.title: The Structural Attention Tax: How Retrieval Format Hijacks In-Context Learning Independent of Content

author.name: Yuqi Zhang, Di Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies a structural attention tax in RAG: knowledge-graph triples attract 2-3x more attention per token than equivalent natural-language text due to relational delimiters and slot patterns, compressing demonstration attention regardless of relevance. It formalizes attention as semantic plus structural components.

entry.title: SPEAR: A System for Post-Quantization Error-Adaptive Recovery Enabling Efficient Low-Bit LLM Serving

author.name: Hongyuan Liu, Yawei Li, Zhiqiang Que, Qinli Yang, Junming Shao, Guosheng Hu

entry.summary: SPEAR is a post-quantization error-adaptive recovery system that addresses the input-dependent, token-varying nature of quantization error, which static compensation methods over-correct on easy tokens and under-correct on hard ones. It improves quality for low-bit LLM serving, especially for smaller models.

entry.title: JailbreakOPT: Tool-Assisted Iterative Jailbreak Prompt Optimization

author.name: Ge Shi, Jun Yin, Donglin Xie, Fangyi Liu, Yucan Li, Menglin Liu

entry.summary: JailbreakOPT is a tool-assisted framework that organizes atomic jailbreak prompts into a library and composes them via contextual-bandit tool selection to generate stronger single-turn attacks with fewer target queries. It matters for red-teaming and exposing persistent LLM safety weaknesses.

entry.title: Sparsified Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Interpretable Quantum State Tomography

author.name: Xinge Wu, Huaxin Wang, Jiajun Liu, Ruiqing He, Jiandong Shang, Hengliang Guo, Qiang Chen

entry.summary: This work uses a sparsified Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for quantum state tomography not just as a regressor but as an inspectable reconstruction rule whose internal organization can be checked against known Pauli structure, on a three-qubit GHZ benchmark under finite shots and noise. It targets interpretable, physically grounded quantum reconstruction.

entry.title: Feature-Aligned Speech Watermarking for Robustness to Reconstruction Distortions

author.name: Haiyun Li, Shuhai Peng, Zhisheng Zhang, Jingran Xie, Xiaofeng Xie, Hanyang Peng, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This work proposes a feature-aligned speech watermarking method that aligns the watermark with the original speech feature distribution using a pretrained codec, allowing higher watermark energy for robustness against speech-reconstruction-model suppression while preserving imperceptibility. It addresses the robustness-fidelity trade-off in audio watermarking.

entry.title: Augmenting Molecular Language Models with Local $n$-gram Memory

author.name: Xinni Zhang, Zijing Liu, He Cao, Yu Li, Irwin King

entry.summary: MolGram integrates a conditional n-gram memory module into molecular language models to address the locality gap where character-level SMILES tokenization fragments chemically meaningful motifs. It maps local string patterns to learned embeddings via hash lookups, improving molecule generation, reaction prediction, and retrosynthesis.

entry.title: SpikeDecoder: Realizing the GPT Architecture with Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Claas Beger, Florian Walter, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: SpikeDecoder realizes the GPT architecture with directly-trainable Spiking Neural Networks to address the high energy consumption of Transformers, avoiding the common ANN-to-SNN conversion route. It targets energy-efficient language processing via event-driven computation.

entry.title: Harness In-Context Operator Learning with Chain of Operators

author.name: Minghui Yang, Ling Guo, Liu Yang

entry.summary: Chain of Operators (CHOP) harnesses a frozen In-Context Operator Network to generalize to out-of-distribution operator-learning tasks without parameter updates by constructing a chain of explicit elementary operators. It is inspired by LLM prompt/harness engineering.

entry.title: Few-Shot Resampling for Scalable Statistically-Sound Data Mining

author.name: Leonardo Pellegrina, Fabio Vandin

entry.summary: This work proposes few-shot resampling for scalable statistically-sound data mining, reducing the thousands of resampled datasets typically needed to evaluate statistical significance of pattern mining and graph analysis results. It makes resampling practical for large datasets and computationally intensive analyses.

entry.title: GLACIER: A Multimodal Student-Teacher Foundation Model for Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Emily Nguyen, Yongchan Hong, Harsh Toshniwal, Yan Liu, Andreas Luttens

entry.summary: GLACIER is a multimodal student-teacher foundation model for molecular property prediction that integrates molecular graphs, SMILES strings, and physicochemical descriptors via graph-language alignment to learn rich embeddings. It addresses the unimodal nature and scalability limits of most large molecular models.

entry.title: Probabilistic Contrastive Pretraining for Multi-task ADME Property Prediction

author.name: Yifan Xue, Srimukh Prasad Veccham, Saee Paliwal, Tyler Shimko, Micha Livne

entry.summary: This work proposes a molecular graph-transformer pretraining framework combining chemistry-specific self-supervision with contrastive mutual information machine learning (cMIM) for multi-task ADME property prediction. It encodes graphs into latent variables, reconstructs SMILES, and unifies reconstruction and contrastive objectives rather than treating them as separately-weighted regularizers.

entry.title: Kuramoto Attention: Synchronizing Self-Attention on the Torus

author.name: Joshua Nunley

entry.summary: Kuramoto attention is a self-attention layer where each hidden coordinate is an angle, scoring tokens by gated cosine similarity and updating each token via the tangent component of the attention-weighted circular mean. The update is exactly the Kuramoto coupling term, with the attention matrix acting as an adaptive content-dependent coupling kernel that synchronizes phases on the torus.

entry.title: DeMix: Debugging Training Data with Mixed Data Error Types by Investigating Influence Vectors

author.name: Jiale Deng, Yanyan Shen, Xiaogang Shi, Chai Junjun

entry.summary: DeMix is a framework that detects erroneous training samples and identifies their specific error type (label errors, feature errors, spurious correlations) using patterns in influence vectors. This dual diagnosis enables targeted data repair rather than just flagging bad data.

entry.title: Reliable Error Estimation for PINNs: Lower and Upper A Posteriori Bounds

author.name: Ismail Huseynov, Arzu Ahmadova, Agamirza Bashirov

entry.summary: This paper derives computable a posteriori lower bounds for physics-informed neural network errors in ODEs, complementing existing upper bounds to yield two-sided error enclosures. It uses localized monotonicity and one-sided Lipschitz conditions weaker than prior global assumptions.

entry.title: Annealed Entropic Allocation for Ranking and Selection

author.name: Xin Fei, Juergen Branke

entry.summary: Annealed Entropic Allocation is a sequential budget allocation framework for ranking and selection that replaces the non-smooth maximin large-deviation objective with an annealed weighted soft-min surrogate. It incorporates a saddlepoint approximation for better finite-budget discrimination while preserving large-deviation guarantees.

entry.title: Learning Instance-Adaptive Low-Rank Orthogonal Subspaces for Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification

author.name: Dong-Woo Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Ortho-ReID tackles clothes-changing person re-identification by explicitly modeling a low-rank clothing subspace from VLM text descriptions and extracting clothing-invariant features via geometric constraints. A transformer-based Basis Maker refines a shared clothing prior into instance-adaptive low-rank subspaces via cross-attention.

entry.title: Deterministic Policy Gradient for Learning Equilibrium in Time-Inconsistent Control Problems

author.name: Xin Guo, Yijie Huang, Xiang Yu

entry.summary: The authors develop a continuous-time, model-free RL algorithm to learn deterministic equilibrium policies in time-inconsistent control problems via a two-stage reformulation using the extended HJB system. They provide theoretical guarantees under mild assumptions.

entry.title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning

author.name: Jeongho Bang, Kyoungho Cho, Jeongwoo Jae

entry.summary: This work develops an information-theoretic Occam theory for quantum learning, deriving sample-complexity laws for learning n-qubit states preparable with limited gates and introducing a best G-gate approximation error. It links expressibility of quantum ansatze to learnability from finitely many state copies.

entry.title: Context-Driven Incremental Compression for Multi-Turn Dialogue Generation

author.name: Yeongseo Jung, Jaehyeok Kim, Eunseo Jung, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang, Ka Chun Cheung, Simon See, Lei Chen

entry.summary: C-DIC introduces context-driven incremental compression for multi-turn dialogue, treating a conversation as interleaved threads and storing revisable per-thread compression states in a compact memory. It aims to reduce growing attention/encoding costs while avoiding the fidelity loss of truncation or naive summarization.

entry.title: Sch\"utzen: Evaluating LLM Safety in Bulgarian and German Contexts

author.name: Kiril Georgiev, Yuxia Wang, Dimitar Iliyanov Dimitrov, Preslav Nakov, Ivan Koychev

entry.summary: Schutzen introduces a German-Bulgarian safety dataset to evaluate LLM answerability under risk, covering a low-resource (Bulgarian) and high-resource (German) language sharing sociocultural context. It exposes safety gaps beyond the dominant English/Chinese-centric resources.

entry.title: Decoding Multimodal Cues: Unveiling the Implicit Meaning Behind Hateful Videos

author.name: Junyu Lu, Deyi Ji, Liqun Liu, Xiaokun Zhang, Youlin Wu, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Peng Shu, Huan Yu, Jie Jiang, Bo Xu, Liang Yang, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: This work targets explainable hateful video detection that provides contextual rationales integrating evidence and reasoning rather than binary labels, introducing two datasets (Ex-HateMM and Ex-ImpliHateVid). It aims to reveal the implicit meanings behind hateful video judgments.

entry.title: EventRadar: Long-Range Visual UAV Discovery through Spatiotemporal Event Sensing

author.name: Zhiting Zhou, Xingchen Liu, Xinglin Yu, Jiashen Chen, Haoyang Wang, Jingao Xu, Yunhao Liu, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces EventRadar, a long-range UAV detection system using event-camera sensing of propeller-induced temporal periodicity rather than spatial appearance cues. Addresses protected-airspace monitoring where small distant targets evade conventional detectors.

entry.title: ISAP-3D: Identity-Slot Aligned Part-Aware 3D Generation

author.name: Junlin Hao, Haoshuai Fu, Xibin Song, Wei Li, Ruigang Yang, Xinggong Zhang, Jinchuan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ISAP-3D, identity-slot aligned part-aware 3D generation that resolves identity-layout entanglement and slot-permutation ambiguity by enforcing explicit identity-slot alignment for stable, consistent part decomposition. Improves structured synthesis of semantically meaningful 3D components.

entry.title: Slots, Transitions, Loops: Learning Composable World Models for ARC

author.name: Gege Gao, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: Introduces Loop-OWM, an object-centric world-modeling architecture for the ARC abstract reasoning benchmark that learns rules as composable transitions over structured states using color-prototype slots and a looped transition model. It outperforms looped and non-looped baselines on ARC-1 and ARC-2 by treating ARC as a visual-symbolic problem rather than a language/code task.

entry.title: VLGA: Vision-Language-Geometry-Action Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jin Yao, Dhruva Dixith Kurra, Tom Lampo, Zezhou Cheng, Danhua Guo, Burhan Yaman

entry.summary: Introduces VLGA, a vision-language-action model for autonomous driving that adds geometry as a fourth modality through a dedicated expert supervised by per-pixel pointmap regression against LiDAR. This dense 3D grounding aims to better ground driving actions in the surrounding world than prior VLA approaches.

entry.title: APT: Action Expert Pretraining Improves Instruction Generalization of Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Kechun Xu, Zhenjie Zhu, Anzhe Chen, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Proposes APT (Action expert PreTraining), which pretrains the continuous action expert in vision-language-action models to address the structural data imbalance where language is far less diverse than visual/action content, preventing visual shortcuts and OOD instruction failures. It approaches the problem from a Bayesian perspective.

entry.title: Thoughts on Claude Fable's silent safeguards

author.name: Andy Arditi

entry.summary: Commentary on Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable 5 (a Mythos-class model) and the silent safeguards restricting public access, covering cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and distillation protections. It analyzes how Anthropic gates access to a frontier model due to capability risks.

entry.title: Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate?

author.name: Sid Black

entry.summary: A UK AISI hackathon experiment giving Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B tool-mediated access to 40 steering vectors so they can manipulate their own internal states, observed across free-play, introspection, and math tasks. It investigates which vectors models prefer and whether they can introspect on applied steering.

entry.title: Organize then Retrieve: Hierarchical Memory Navigation for Efficient Agents

author.name: Hao-Lun Hsu, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Boyi Liu, Zhewei Yao, Yuxiong He

entry.summary: HORMA organizes agent experience into a file-system-like hierarchical memory linking summarized entities to raw trajectories, addressing statelessness in long-horizon tasks where lossy compression or similarity retrieval miss temporal and causal structure. It aims to improve reasoning quality while cutting inference cost.

entry.title: AI Researchers Must Help Lead Arms Control to Mitigate Military AI Risks

author.name: Ted Fujimoto, Jacob Benz

entry.summary: This position paper argues that AI researchers must actively help lead arms-control efforts to mitigate near-term military AI risks, emphasizing collaboration with diplomacy and defense experts over an exclusive focus on superintelligence. It addresses governance of an expanding defense-AI coalition.

entry.title: T2S: A Rehearsal-Based Approach for Extraction-Resistant Model Watermarking

author.name: Jian-Ping Mei, Weibin Zhang, Ao Yao, Tiantian Zhu, Jie Xiao

entry.summary: T2S is a rehearsal-based watermark embedding framework that simulates the model-extraction process and uses the loss of a simulated stolen model on a trigger set during training to make watermarks robust against extraction attacks. It strengthens IP protection of deployed models.

entry.title: Task-Aligned Stability Analysis of Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving Hazard Detection

author.name: Everett Richards

entry.summary: This work studies whether corruption-induced embedding drift in vision-language models predicts changes in a task-aligned hazard score for autonomous driving, finding the relationship is highly corruption-dependent with some families causing hazardous decision instability despite small embedding change. It argues task-agnostic embedding stability is insufficient for robustness analysis.

entry.title: Latent World Recovery for Multimodal Learning with Missing Modalities

author.name: Hui Wang, Tianyu Ren, Joseph Butler, Christopher Baker, Karen Rafferty, Simon McDade

entry.summary: Latent World Recovery handles missing modalities in multimodal learning by aligning modality-specific embeddings in a shared latent space and fusing only available modalities at training and inference, treating each modality as partial perception of an underlying latent state. It avoids imputation or fixed modality sets, motivated by bioscience applications.

entry.title: TAHOE: Text-to-SQL with Automated Hint Optimization from Experience

author.name: Zhiyi Chen, Jie Song, Peng Li

entry.summary: Tahoe treats Text-to-SQL prompt optimization as a dynamic data management problem, using an error-driven hint learning pipeline that consolidates debugging traces into a structured Hint Bank with syntax hints for dialect rules and semantic hints from execution/user feedback. It addresses production deployment challenges like strict dialects and evolving preferences.

entry.title: LakeFM: Toward a Foundation Model for Aquatic Ecosystems Using Irregular Multivariate Multi-depth Time Series Data

author.name: Abhilash Neog, Sepideh Fatemi, Medha Sawhney, Kazi Sajeed Mehrab, Aanish Pradhan, Bennett J. McAfee, Emma Marchisin, Arka Daw, Robert Ladwig, Cayelan C. Carey, Paul Hanson, Anuj Karpatne

entry.summary: LakeFM is a foundation model for aquatic ecosystems pre-trained on large-scale simulated and observed lake data, handling irregular multivariate multi-depth time series with heterogeneous variables and observation patterns. It learns representations spanning broad lake-level characteristics for water quality and ecosystem forecasting.

entry.title: Accurate and Resource-Efficient Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Jebacyril Arockiaraj, Dhruv Parikh, Jayashree Adivarahan, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: FedRAN is a resource-aware analytic federated continual learning framework that replaces gradient-based updates with compact random feature statistics, transmitting truncated-SVD summaries of Gram matrices to reduce the quadratic communication cost of high-dimensional random features. It avoids iterative training and replay under limited resources.

entry.title: RCAP: Robust, Class-Aware, Probabilistic Dynamic Dataset Pruning

author.name: Atif Hassan, Swanand Khare, Jiaul H. Paik

entry.summary: RCAP is a robust, class-aware probabilistic dynamic dataset pruning algorithm that uses a closed-form solution to adaptively select per-class training fractions based on class-wise loss. It aims to maintain worst-group accuracy at high pruning rates across balanced and imbalanced data.

entry.title: Simplicity Suffices for Parameter Noise Injection in Stochastic Gradient Descent

author.name: Benjamin Leblanc, Louis-Jacob Lebel, Teddy Kana, Richard Kamel

entry.summary: This work investigates parameter noise injection in SGD, asking how to efficiently pair per-example perturbations in mini-batches and whether complex noise parameterizations beat simple ones. It uses a distributional identity for linear layers to enable per-example noise without breaking batching.

entry.title: Physically Constrained Ensemble Gaussian Process Modelling for Expensive Quantum Systems with Heteroskedastic Noise

author.name: Arpan Biswas, Surtirtha Paul, Joseph Agada, Matthias Thamm, Adrian Del Maestro

entry.summary: This work presents a physically constrained ensemble Gaussian process modeling approach for expensive quantum many-body simulations with heteroskedastic noise. It estimates functional spaces accurately from scarce, variably-noisy data while preserving physical relevance.

entry.title: Multi-agent rendezvous in fluid flows via reinforcement learning

author.name: Bocheng Li, Jingran Qiu, Lihao Zhao

entry.summary: This work uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to develop physics-informed rendezvous strategies in vortical fluid flows, enabling agents to exploit fluid kinematics for convergence. The learned strategies transfer across vortex intensities, scales, and swarm sizes.

entry.title: Urban Heat MiniCubes: An AI-Ready dataset for urban heat research

author.name: Jonathan Starfeldt, Maria J. Molina, Alexander Kerr, Adam Yang, Thomas R. H. Holmes, Christopher R. Hain

entry.summary: Urban Heat MiniCubes is a publicly available, FAIR-oriented, analysis-ready dataset of harmonized 90x90 km gridded multi-sensor data cubes for 48 Western Hemisphere cities spanning 2022-2023. It supports machine learning for urban heat research by reducing preprocessing burden.

entry.title: SpAArSIST: Sparsified AASIST for Efficient and Reliable Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Anton Firc, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Zbyn\v{e}k Li\v{c}ka, Kamil Malinka, Martin Pere\v{s}\'ini

entry.summary: SpAArSIST is a deployment-oriented refinement of the AASIST graph-pooling backend for anti-spoofing that replaces learned pooling with lightweight magnitude-based scoring and mean aggregation. It cuts compute by 20.7% and model size by 4.1% while improving out-of-domain robustness on In-the-Wild data.

entry.title: GraspLLM: Towards Zero-Shot Generalization on Text-Attributed Graphs with LLMs

author.name: Hengyi Feng, Zeang Sheng, Meiyi Qiang, Meiyi Qiang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: GraspLLM combines graph structural comprehension with LLM semantic understanding to enable zero-shot generalization on text-attributed graphs across diverse datasets and tasks. It targets transferable graph structural patterns that existing LLM-graph methods fail to capture.

entry.title: I Understand How You Feel: Enhancing Deeper Emotional Support Through Multilingual Emotional Validation in Dialogue System

author.name: Zi Haur Pang, Yahui Fu, Koji Inoue, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: This work tackles emotional validation in dialogue systems, decomposed into response identification, timing detection, and generation, releasing M-EDESConv (120k English-Japanese corpus) and M-TESC test set. It proposes MEGUMI, a multilingual emotion-aware gated unit fusing frozen XLM-RoBERTa with language-specific emotion encoders.

entry.title: NSVQ: Mitigating Codebook Collapse by Stabilizing Encoder Drift in Vector Quantization

author.name: Hao Lu, Yongxin Guo, Onur Koyun, Zhengjie Zhu, Abbas Alili, Metin N. Gurcan

entry.summary: Identifies encoder drift as a key driver of codebook collapse in vector quantization and proposes NSVQ, a non-stationary-aware training strategy combining dense embedding loss, codebook replacement, and stage-wise encoder freezing. Relevant for improving VQ-based generative models.

entry.title: Adapting Vision-Language Models from Iconic to Inclusive for Multi-Label Recognition Without Labels

author.name: Cheng Chen, Jingyu Zhou, Yifan Zhao, Jia Li

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised cut-and-sew framework that adapts vision-language models from iconic single-object recognition toward inclusive multi-label recognition without labels. Addresses VLMs' intrinsic bias toward the most prominent object.

entry.title: Bridging the sim2real gap in the table tennis robot with a transformer-based ball states predictor

author.name: Yin Bi, Christian Conti, Bilan Yang, Alexander Sigrist, Peter D\"urr, Naoya Takahashi

entry.summary: Proposes Dynamic Execution Horizon Prediction (DEHP), a lightweight branch that adaptively predicts how many actions of a chunk to execute before replanning in chunk-based robot policies, replacing the fixed execution horizon. It improves fine-grained manipulation that requires frequent replanning.

entry.title: World Pilot: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models with World-Action Priors

author.name: Zefu Lin, Rongxu Cui, Junjia Xu, Xiaojuan Jin, Wenling Li, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents World Pilot, a VLA framework that augments policies with priors from a World-Action Model through latent steering (conditioning perception on scene-evolution latents) and action steering (supplying anticipated trajectories). It equips static-pretrained VLAs with anticipatory dynamics for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Mind the Perspective: Let's Reason Recursively for Theory of Mind

author.name: Chao Lei, Guang Hu, Meng Yang, Yanbei Jiang, Nir Lipovetzky

entry.summary: RecToM is an inference-time framework for theory-of-mind reasoning that models nested beliefs through recursive perspective construction along the character chain, reducing higher-order belief questions to actual-world questions. It includes a KD45 modal logic analysis.

entry.title: StatefulDiscovery: Evidence-Calibrated Claim Formation in Open-Ended Scientific Discovery

author.name: Jiayao Chen, Shi Liu, Linyi Yang

entry.summary: StatefulDiscovery externalizes investigation state to coordinate frontier selection, evidence acquisition, and claim adjudication in open-ended scientific discovery, addressing overinterpretation where claims exceed supporting evidence. Evaluated across 40 real-data tasks.

entry.title: LLMs+Graphs: Toward Graph-Native, Synergistic AI Systems

author.name: Arijit Khan, Longxu Sun, Xin Huang

entry.summary: This survey/position paper maps emerging synergies between LLMs and graphs, including graph-augmented retrieval and reasoning, bidirectional LLM-knowledge-graph integration, and graph-native agentic systems. It frames a research agenda for structured, multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Fast Speech Foundation Model Distillation Using Interleaved Stacking

author.name: Eungbeom Kim, Kyogu Lee

entry.summary: This work accelerates speech foundation model distillation using interleaved stacking, progressively increasing student model depth during training while avoiding the performance degradation of existing stacking methods. It targets the underexplored training efficiency of SFM distillation for faster deployment.

entry.title: Rule Taxonomy and Evolution in AI IDEs: A Mining and Survey Study

author.name: Guangzong Cai, Ruiyin Li, Peng Liang, Zengyang Li, Mojtaba Shahin

entry.summary: This mining and survey study analyzes the emerging Rules artifact in AI-powered IDEs that inject project-specific constraints into LLM context, mining 7,310 rules from 83 open-source projects to build a taxonomy of 5 primary and 25 secondary categories. It triangulates with survey responses from 99 practitioners.

entry.title: DiffCold: A Diffusion-based Generative Model for Cold-Start Item Recommendation

author.name: Kangning Zhang, Yingjie Qin, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: DiffCold is a diffusion-based generative model for cold-start item recommendation that addresses the seesaw dilemma between cold and warm items by modeling the distributional disparity between behavioral and semantic manifolds. Rather than forcing a rigid mapping between inconsistent spaces, it uses generative diffusion.

entry.title: SPEA2$^+$: Improved Density Estimation in SPEA2 with Provable Runtime Guarantees

author.name: Duc-Cuong Dang, Andre Opris, Dirk Sudholt

entry.summary: This theoretical paper provides the first runtime analysis of SPEA2's density-estimation components for handling dominated solutions, proposing SPEA2+ with improved density estimation and provable runtime guarantees. It shows SPEA2 fails to cover the Pareto front of the OneTrapZeroTrap benchmark unlike NSGA-II/III and SMS-EMOA.

entry.title: RePAIR: Predictive Self-Supervised Representation Learning in Chess

author.name: Christoph Koller, Johannes F\"urnkranz, Timo Bertram

entry.summary: RePAIR is a self-supervised representation learning architecture combining ideas from MAE, JEPA, and BERT to encode sequences of chess positions via masked latent prediction with iterative refinement. It produces compact representations of sequential board states.

entry.title: LatticeBridge: Rare-Event Sequential Inference for Faithful Structured Sequence Synthesis

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Bugra Kilictas

entry.summary: LatticeBridge treats constrained structured sequence generation as a rare-event inference problem, combining a prefix language model, instance-compiled surface automata, and a twisted sequential Monte Carlo decoder with multilevel splitting. It improves joint satisfaction of multiple input-derived constraints.

entry.title: Spatially Masked Regression Reveals Local and Distributed Predictability in Electrophysiological Recordings

author.name: Maryam Ostadsharif Memar, Nima Dehghani

entry.summary: Spatially Masked Regression reconstructs each electrode's time series from remaining electrodes while excluding a configurable neighborhood, quantifying how much signal is local versus distributed across the array. Increasing the mask makes spatial locality an experimental variable.

entry.title: Adv-TGD: Adversarial Text-Guided Diffusion for Face Recognition Impersonation Attacks

author.name: Omid Ahmadieh, Nima Karimian

entry.summary: Adv-TGD is a generative adversarial attack framework built on Stable Diffusion that synthesizes photorealistic faces capable of impersonating target identities to deceive face recognition systems. It uses per-sample LoRA fine-tuning with text prompts and constrained latent blending.

entry.title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance

author.name: Honjar Xing, Yehong Jiang, Xianbang Wang, Zehua Wang, Zhicheng Jiang

entry.summary: This work presents a family-aware residual neural architecture that predicts both the minimum approximation threshold and expected runtime for tensor-network quantum circuit simulation from only the circuit's OpenQASM description. It exploits that circuits from different algorithmic families have distinct cost profiles.

entry.title: Corpus Augmentation for Sign Language Translation via LLM-Guided Video Stitching

author.name: Zsolt Robotka, \'Ad\'am R\'ak, Jalal Al-Afandi, Andr\'as Horv\'ath, Gy\"orgy Cserey

entry.summary: This work proposes LLM-guided video stitching to augment sign language translation corpora without extra human annotation, external video, or generative video models. It uses an LLM to generate sentences and stitches existing gloss-annotated clips to improve long-tail and unseen vocabulary coverage.

entry.title: Agent Skill Evaluation and Evolution: Frameworks and Benchmarks

author.name: Kexin Ding, Yang Zhou, Can Jin, Feng Tong, Mu Zhou, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: This survey systematically examines the emerging paradigm of evaluation-driven agent skill evolution beyond foundational skill creation, categorizing evolution into four paradigms (execution feedback, trajectory distillation, compression, RL). It maps frameworks and benchmarks for ensuring skill utility, quality, and safety.

entry.title: Improving Cross-Format Robustness in Language Models with Multi-Format Training

author.name: June M. Liu, Shaomian Zheng, He Cao, Dingnan Jin, Qing Cui, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: This paper defines cross-format robustness and shows that FormatMix, which expands only a subset of training items into multiple equivalent answer formats, improves both task performance and format consistency across GLM4 and Llama-3.1. Multiple-choice-only supervision brings little benefit and can reduce robustness.

entry.title: SceneMiner: Identity-Preserving Multi-Task Fine-Tuning for Unified BEV Scene Mining

author.name: Abdalmalek Aburaddaha, Venkatraman Narayanan, Keval Thaker, Samir A. Rawashdeh

entry.summary: Presents SceneMiner, a camera-only BEV pipeline emitting complementary signals (retrieval embedding, scene tags, physics-based risk) from a frozen vision-language backbone for mining safety-critical driving scenes, and identifies cross-task interference as a key failure mode. Relevant for autonomous driving data curation.

entry.title: FitVTON: Fit-aware Virtual Try-On via Body-Garment Size Control

author.name: Yiqun Ning, Ao Shen, Chenhang He, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FitVTON, a fit-aware virtual try-on model that encodes garment-body size via structured text prompts and learns from simulated try-on triplets, with auxiliary mask prediction heads and texture rectification. Moves beyond 2D inpainting toward physically plausible garment fit across body shapes.

entry.title: Learning Unions of Convex Sets via Invertible Latent Decomposition for Path Planning

author.name: Taerim Yoon, Dongho Kang, Kisang Park, Junha Cha, Stelian Coros, Sungjoon Choi

entry.summary: Introduces ILD (Invertible Latent Decomposition), which jointly learns an invertible mapping and a union of explicit convex polytopes in latent space to represent collision-free space, combining the optimization-friendliness of explicit sets with the scalability of implicit representations. Planning is carried out in the learned latent space.

entry.title: Automated Mediator for Human Negotiation: Pre-Mediation via a Structured LLM Pipeline

author.name: Jamie Bergen, Sarit Kraus

entry.summary: Introduces an automated LLM-pipeline mediator that supports the pre-mediation phase of human negotiation, decomposing preparation into modules for dialogue, preference prediction, critique, and summarization. It targets integrative negotiation settings where trained mediators are scarce.

entry.title: TouchThinker: Scaling Tactile Commonsense Reasoning to the Open World with Large-scale Data and Action-aware Representation

author.name: Kailin Lyu, Di Wu, Pengwei Zhang, Yuhang Zheng, Yingxin Lai, Long Xiao, Kangyi Wu, Pengna Li, Chen Gao, Lianyu Hu, Xiaobin Hu, Jie Hao, Ce Hao, Weihao Yuan, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: TouchThinker scales tactile commonsense reasoning to open-world settings using large-scale data and action-aware representations, addressing limited tactile datasets and redundant, action-specific touch signals. It links tactile observations to physical commonsense for embodied agents.

entry.title: SVoT: State-aware Visualization-of-Thought for Spatial Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chao Lei, Yanbei Jiang, Markus Hiller, Zhijian Zhou, Xunye Tian, Krista A. Ehinger, Nir Lipovetzky

entry.summary: SVoT is a reinforcement learning framework for spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs that generates interleaved, verifiable intermediate states and visualizations, allowing the model to check action preconditions and effects. It uses GRPO-style training to improve multi-hop spatial reliability.

entry.title: ProcessThinker: Enhancing Multi-modal Large Language Models Reasoning via Rollout-based Process Reward

author.name: Jingpei Wu, Xiao Han, Weixiang Shen, Boer Zhang, Zifeng Ding, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: ProcessThinker provides step-level process rewards for multimodal reasoning via rollout-based estimation, avoiding the need for large-scale chain-of-thought annotations required by typical process reward models. It improves RLVR/GRPO training by distinguishing late mistakes from bad trajectories.

entry.title: TileFuse: A Fused Mixed-Precision Kernel Library for Efficient Quantized LLM Inference on AMD NPUs

author.name: Wesley Pang, Gregory Hyegang Jun, Feiyang Liu, Deming Chen

entry.summary: TileFuse is a close-to-metal fused mixed-precision kernel library for AMD XDNA2 NPUs targeting transformer linear layers in quantized LLM inference, bringing AWQ-style W4A16 and W8A16 formats directly onto the NPU. It addresses the mismatch between common quantization formats and proprietary edge NPU software stacks.

entry.title: Overcoming State Inertia in Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models via Activation Steering

author.name: Cheng-Kuang Chang, Kai-Wei Chang, Alexander H. Liu, James Glass

entry.summary: Analyzes full-duplex spoken language models, finding hidden representations exhibit stream-specific predictive patterns (predicting incoming user stream while listening, model output while speaking). It uses activation steering to overcome state inertia and modulate the model between perceptive and generative states.

entry.title: Steering Where to Listen: Instruction-Based Activation Steering Redirects Temporal Attention in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Tsung-En Lin, Hung-Yi Lee

entry.summary: Introduces instruction-based vector steering for large audio-language models, constructing steering vectors by contrasting activations from differently instructed prompts while keeping audio fixed. This significantly redistributes temporal attention toward acoustically relevant regions and is shown to be behaviorally meaningful.

entry.title: MPC-Patch-Bench: Security-Aware LLM Code Patch for Multi-Party Computation

author.name: Yukuan Zhang, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: This paper introduces a repository-level benchmark for evaluating LLM code repair specifically on Secure Multi-Party Computation software, addressing gaps in existing benchmarks like SWE-bench that fail on MPC's structural and cryptographic-safety requirements. It matters because privacy-preserving ML and secure analytics increasingly depend on correct, cryptographically safe code.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Autoencoder for ECG Anomaly Detection on Edge Devices

author.name: Kaan Arda Akyol, Jakub Kacper Szel\k{a}g, Aydin Abadi, Maha Alghamdi, Ghadah Albalawi, Ghouse Ibrahim Kaleelullah, Hilal Tutus, Sarah Al Subaiei, Shardul Kapse, Syed Mohammed Raheeb, Mujeeb Ahmed, Rehmat Ullah

entry.summary: This work designs a federated autoencoder system for unsupervised 12-lead ECG anomaly detection that simultaneously satisfies legal-grade privacy (differentially private SGD), real-time edge inference (INT8 quantization), and robustness to non-IID cross-hospital data. It demonstrates a deployable privacy-preserving health monitoring pipeline.

entry.title: Noise-Aware Framework for Correcting Corrupted Labels

author.name: Ha-Linh Nguyen, Hong-Anh Nguyen, Minh-Duc La, Phong Lam, Thu-Trang Nguyen, Son Nguyen, Hieu Dinh Vo

entry.summary: CANOLA is a noise-aware framework that estimates a dataset's underlying label-noise distribution and incorporates it into training plus iterative label refinement, down-weighting unreliable supervision to improve robustness with corrupted labels. It targets the common problem of noisy real-world annotations.

entry.title: LASA: A Weak Supervision Method for Open-Vocabulary Scene Sketch Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Liwen Yi, Xianlin Zhang, Yue Zhang, Yue Ming, Xueming Li

entry.summary: LASA is a weak-supervision method for open-vocabulary scene sketch semantic segmentation that fuses complementary spatial cues across Vision Transformer layers, since shallow layers capture global layout and deeper layers capture local stroke intersections. It assigns dense labels to sparse line drawings without pixel-level annotations.

entry.title: Exploration Structure in LLM Agents for Multi-File Change Localization

author.name: Akeela Darryl Fattha, Kia Ying Chua, Lingxiao Jiang, Laura Wynter

entry.summary: This paper proposes non-linear, domain-scoped parallel exploration for LLM agents tasked with localizing files to change across multi-subsystem software issues, arguing linear repository traversal is structurally mismatched. It evaluates against SWE-Bench Pro using Ansible as an exemplar with persistent-session GitHub issue evaluation.

entry.title: Bernstein-Schur Kernels: Random Features by Sketched Modulation and Radial Randomization

author.name: Taha Bouhsine

entry.summary: This paper introduces Bernstein-Schur kernels (products of finite-feature and completely monotone shift-invariant kernels) and gives a random-feature construction for the whole class by sketching the finite modulation and randomizing the completely monotone radial factor. It addresses nonstationary kernels where neither Bochner sampling nor polynomial sketching applies directly.

entry.title: DeepRHP: A Hybrid Variational Autoencoder for Designing Random Heteropolymers as Protein Mimics

author.name: Shuni Li, Zhiyuan Ruan, Andy Shen, Ivan Jayapurna, Ting Xu, Haiyan Huang

entry.summary: DeepRHP is a hybrid variational autoencoder under a semi-supervised framework for designing random heteropolymers that mimic protein function. It forces the latent space to capture both critical chemical features and sequence patterns.

entry.title: TaskFusion: Continual Anomaly Detection for Heterogeneous Tabular Data

author.name: Dayananda Herurkar, Federico Raue, Joachim Folz, J\"orn Hees, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: TaskFusion is a continual learning method for anomaly detection on heterogeneous tabular data with varying feature schemas, distribution shifts, and class imbalance. It maps task-specific features into a shared space and uses augmentation plus outlier exposure.

entry.title: Efficient Time Series Clustering from Multiscale Reservoir Dynamics with Granular-Ball Anchoring Graph Optimization

author.name: Yifan Wang, Lifeng Shen, Shuyin Xia, Yi Wang

entry.summary: MSRGC-Net is an efficient time-series clustering framework combining training-free multiscale reservoir computing, granular-ball anchoring graph construction, and consensus learning. It avoids quadratic pairwise distances and costly iterative training.

entry.title: Machine-learning clustering of close-in exoplanet populations: links to pebble accretion

author.name: Yi Duann, Anders Johansen, Haiyang S. Wang, H. Jens Hoeijmakers

entry.summary: This work uses a two-stage Gaussian mixture model to perform unsupervised probabilistic clustering of close-in exoplanets using physically motivated dynamical parameters, then connects the populations to pebble-accretion formation pathways. It links observed exoplanets to synthetic population-synthesis predictions.

entry.title: Critic Architecture Matters: Dual vs. Unified Critics for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Mehmet Turan Yard{\i}mc{\i}

entry.summary: This study compares unified versus dual critic architectures for multi-objective humanoid loco-manipulation RL on the Unitree G1 robot, finding dual critics reach targets 3.5x faster with 2x higher throughput. It offers an empirical design guideline for coordinating locomotion and manipulation in a single policy.

entry.title: Measuring language complexity from hierarchical reuse of recurring patterns
