entry.summary: Argues RL is well-suited to the 2D irregular nesting problem and introduces the Polygons Transformer, a geometry-aware encoder allowing cross-polygon attention, paired with an optimization policy that learns geometric priors from data. It contrasts with geometry-blind heuristic solvers.

entry.title: PL-KKT-hPINN: Enforcing Nonlinear Equality Constraints on Neural Networks via Piecewise-Linear Projection

author.name: Fateme Mohammad Mohammadi, Hector Budman, Joshua L. Pulsipher

entry.summary: Proposes PL-KKT-hPINN, extending hard-constrained PINNs to enforce nonlinear equality constraints exactly at inference via piecewise-linear projection using KKT conditions, demonstrated on a CSTR reactor case study. It addresses that standard PINNs only enforce physics as soft constraints.

entry.title: Multimodal Brain Tumour Classification Using Feature Fusion

author.name: Wajih ul Islam, Muhammad Yaqoob, Javed Ali Khan, Volker Steuber

entry.summary: This work proposes a two-branch multimodal network combining raw MRI scans with 91 radiomic features to classify brain tumors, using various fusion strategies. It aims to replicate clinicians' multimodal reasoning rather than relying on images alone.

entry.title: Interpretable Temporal Facial-Region Motion Analysis for In-the-Wild Parkinson's Disease Video Classification

author.name: Riyadh Almushrafy (Majmaah University, Saudi Arabia)

entry.summary: This paper examines whether temporal facial-region motion descriptors can support in-the-wild Parkinson's disease video classification on the YouTubePD benchmark, emphasizing interpretability via region ablation and permutation importance. It compares geometric and sequence-based descriptors.

entry.title: UniPET: a universal network for high-quality PET image denoising across varied dose reduction factors

author.name: Zhiwen Yang, Yang Zhou, Haowei Chen, Hui Zhang, Dan Zhao, Bingzheng Wei, Yan Xu

entry.summary: Presents UniPET, a universal PET denoising model that uses domain generalization to handle varied dose reduction factors and avoid over-smoothing from style misalignment across DRFs. Improves practical robustness over fixed-DRF approaches.

entry.title: Time-frequency localization of bird calls in dense soundscapes

author.name: Simen Hexeberg, Fanghui Tong, Hari Vishnu, Mandar Chitre

entry.summary: Formulates bird vocalization detection as spectrogram object detection using YOLO11, localizing calls in time and frequency in dense tropical soundscapes, with an open annotation tool and a new IoMin metric. Nearly doubles baseline detection performance.

entry.title: Deterministic Denominator Design for Localized Tamed Stochastic-Gradient Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Yiwei Zhou, Ziheng Chen

entry.summary: Studies deterministic-denominator design for localized tamed stochastic-gradient Langevin dynamics, fixing the state-dependent envelope before sampling and providing a practical recipe with proxy scores, quantile thresholds, and calibration plus error analysis. Stabilizes large drifts without altering conditional mean.

entry.title: A complementary study on PlanGPT: Evaluation with defined Performance Metrics and comparison with a planner

author.name: Youssef Abdelkader, Humbert Fiorino, Damien Pellier

entry.summary: A complementary reproduction study of PlanGPT, re-running experiments to verify whether LLM-based automated planning is genuinely worthwhile and comparing it against a classical planner. Evaluates plan coverage claims with defined performance metrics.

entry.title: Attention Expansion: Enhancing Keyphrase Extraction from Long Documents with Attention-Augmented Contextualized Embeddings

author.name: Roberto Mart\'inez-Cruz, Alvaro J. L\'opez-L\'opez, Jos\'e Portela

entry.summary: Proposes an attention expansion mechanism that augments PLM token representations with information from out-of-context chunks to improve keyphrase extraction in long documents. Avoids the cost of long-context LLMs while capturing scattered evidence.

entry.title: Structured Adaptive Tensor Prediction for Streaming Data

author.name: Zhen Qin, Yang Chen

entry.summary: Develops an adaptive tensor-regression framework for streaming matrix-valued time series, introducing Matrix-on-Matrix and Tensor-on-Matrix formulations for online forecasting in time-varying environments. It extends adaptive filtering beyond scalar/vector data.

entry.title: Nonlinear Estimator: Dual Bayesian Affine Estimators for Parameter Learning

author.name: Sasan Vakili, Dani\"el Woonings, Pradyumna Paruchuri, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani

entry.summary: Presents a nonlinear parameter estimator for Wiener-type state-space models built as a fixed-point coupling of two affine MMSE estimators (parameters and latent variables) augmented with dynamic basis statistics. Two construction strategies yield dual basis-parameter and state-parameter estimators.

entry.title: When Metrics Disagree: A Meta-Analysis of Knowledge-Graph-Completion Model Benchmarking

author.name: Haji Gul, Ajaz Ahmad Bhat

entry.summary: Reframes knowledge-graph-completion evaluation as a multi-criteria decision-making problem and conducts a meta-analysis of seven score aggregators across five tests since MRR, Hits@k, and Mean Rank often produce conflicting rankings. It aims to reduce selective reporting and clarify real progress.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Inference-Time Augmentation Framework in Physiological Signals: Application to PPG-Based AF Detection

author.name: Davood Fattahi, Runze Yan, Saurabh Kataria, Zhaoliang Chen, Xiao Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a unified inference-time augmentation framework for physiological signals applied to PPG-based atrial fibrillation detection, incorporating 13 augmentation methods across time, amplitude, frequency, and artifact domains with optimized parameters. It targets robustness to noise, motion artifacts, and distribution shift at deployment.

entry.title: Effective Training Principles of Physical Reservoirs

author.name: Sobhi Saeed, Mehmet M\"uft\"uoglu, Glitta R. Cheeran, Juliane Heim, Bennet Fischer, Mario Chemnitz

entry.summary: This paper investigates strategies to mitigate overfitting and reduce computational overhead in optical reservoir computers through output pruning and regularization. It compares loss-minimizing search, variance filtering, and random pruning approaches.

entry.title: SPARX: Secure and Privacy-Aware Approximate CNN Acceleration with Edge RISC-V SoC

author.name: Sonu Kumar, Akash Sankhe, Mukul Lokhande, Santosh Kumar Vishvakarma

entry.summary: Presents SPARX, a secure, privacy-aware approximate CNN accelerator on a RISC-V SoC combining custom instructions, logarithmic approximate compute, differential-noise privacy, and challenge-response authentication. Targets efficient, secure edge inference.

entry.title: Robotic Nonprehensile Object Transportation with a Hanging Tray

author.name: Adam Heins, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Addresses the waiter's problem of transporting an object on a tray suspended by ropes (behaving as a 3D pendulum) rather than a rigidly held tray, exploiting pendular motion to reduce shear and sloshing. Schoellig group contribution to nonprehensile transport.

entry.title: The Machines Lack Honour

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: An essay on the AI moral-status debate that maps the field into camps (AI as mere tools, AIs as rich beings deserving respect, and Anthropic's uncertainty stance) and argues for an overlooked fourth position: that AIs may genuinely be capable of suffering and sophisticated moral reasoning, yet directing their behavior could still be acceptable. It probes the philosophy underlying AI welfare discussions.

entry.title: Sim2Schedule: A Simulator-Guided LLM Framework for Autonomous Open-Pit Mine Scheduling

author.name: Mustavi Ibne Masum, Thiago Eustaquio Alves de Oliveira, Mahzabeen Emu

entry.summary: Proposes Sim2Schedule, a simulator-guided LLM framework for autonomous open-pit mine scheduling where the LLM acts as a zero-shot decision agent guided by a custom simulator encoding geotechnical and capacity constraints. Aims to overcome MILP's computational and adaptability limitations.

entry.title: QSplitFL: Capability Aware Deep Q-Learning for Optimal Split Point Selection in Split Federated Learning

author.name: Nazmus Shakib Shadin, Xinyue Zhang, Jingyi Wang, Miao Pan

entry.summary: Proposes QSplitFL, a deep Q-learning framework that adaptively selects the optimal model split point in split federated learning based on heterogeneous device capabilities. It aims to avoid overloading weak devices and improve convergence stability.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection and Root Cause Analysis for Microservice Systems

author.name: Luan Pham

entry.summary: Surveys and addresses five limitations in anomaly detection and root cause analysis for microservice systems, including the separation of detection from RCA, underuse of event data, and lack of standardized datasets. It argues for jointly handling detection and diagnosis under imprecise detection.

entry.title: Fast Exact Nearest-Neighbor Learning for High-Frequency Financial Time Series

author.name: Henry Han, Diane Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a Mojo-language implementation of exact nearest-neighbor learning for high-frequency financial time series, using a SIMD k-d tree with variance-based splitting and compile-time vectorized distance computation. It demonstrates that systems-level optimization can meet real-time latency at scale.

entry.title: Post-Quantum Secure Federated DeFi for Inclusive Banking

author.name: Swati Sachan, Dale Fickett, Richard Buchinger, Theo Miller

entry.summary: Proposes a post-quantum secure federated DeFi framework using lattice-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption to let multiple banks collaboratively assess creditworthiness of underserved individuals without exposing data. Aims to combine quantum-resistant cryptography with financial inclusion goals.

entry.title: Improving Text-Instance Alignment Of Foreground Conditioned Out-Painting Via Customized Concept Embedding

author.name: Yihao Zhao, Xuan Han, Bin He, Mingyu You

entry.summary: Addresses artifacts in foreground-conditioned outpainting where backgrounds inadvertently share foreground semantics, attributing it to embedding misalignment. Proposes a Customized Concept Embedding approach to improve text-instance alignment for product display images.

entry.title: Optuna Constrained Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator Is a Joint Density Generalization of c-TPE

author.name: Shuhei Watanabe, Kaichi Irie

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of Optuna's widely-used constrained TPE hyperparameter optimizer, showing it is equivalent to a joint-density generalization of c-TPE. It proves the joint formulation is invariant to constraint duplication whereas the independent version degrades.

entry.title: Beyond Explaining Predictions: Logic-Based Explanations for Confidence in Machine Learning Models

author.name: Vin\'icius Peixoto Chagas, Carlos Henrique Leit\~ao Cavalcante, Thiago Alves Rocha

entry.summary: Introduces a Minimum Confidence Threshold for logic-based abductive explanations, quantifying the weakest confidence guarantee an explanation provides so explanations do not cover low-confidence instances. It extends formal explainability from prediction to model confidence.

entry.title: Learning Doubly Sparse Explicitly Conditioned Transforms

author.name: Tudor Pistol

entry.summary: Develops interpretable ML models (Pre-AF 13) predicting medium-term atrial fibrillation risk in cardiovascular-disease patients over 24-month and full follow-up horizons using routinely collected hospital discharge data. It targets stratification gaps left by established long-term AF risk scores.

entry.title: Stochastic weather generators for high-frequency wind vector time series

author.name: Mingshi Cui, Kevin Eng, Justin T. Greene, Zern Ke, Abolfazl Sodagartojgi, Zhiqiu Xia, Gemma E. Moran, Michael L. Stein

entry.summary: This paper develops machine learning models to generate realistic minute-scale surface wind vector time series at an Oklahoma site using 30+ years of data. The generator targets applications in wind energy, wildfire spread, and aviation.

entry.title: Do LLMsMakeNeural Distinguishers Wise?

author.name: Tatsuya Sakagami, Masashi Hisai, Naoto Yanai

entry.summary: This paper proposes LLM-based neural distinguishers for symmetric-key cryptanalysis through prompt design, testing on SPECK-32/64. It finds that LLMs provide no observable improvement over ResNet-based neural distinguishers from prior work.

entry.title: Benchmarking stereo reconstruction for 3D printable Martian terrain models

author.name: Josephine Wang

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks stereo reconstruction pipelines for producing 3D-printable Martian terrain models from rover imagery, finding that RAFT-Stereo outperforms SGBM on Middlebury but does not transfer well to low-texture Martian terrain. It highlights a benchmark-to-real-world transfer gap.

entry.title: Don't waste SAM

author.name: Nermeen Abou Baker, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: This study evaluates the generalization of Meta's Segment Anything Model and fine-tunes it on three waste segmentation datasets featuring occlusions, deformable objects, and transparency. It argues SAM remains a valuable starting point even where zero-shot accuracy is insufficient.

entry.title: Deep learning for echo sounder data

author.name: Ketil Malde

entry.summary: This position/perspective paper argues that meaningful advances in deep learning for echo sounder and underwater acoustic data will require methods beyond recycling image-processing models, given intrinsic acoustic data properties. It highlights how the lack of standard data formats hinders progress.

entry.title: The 1st PortraitCraft Challenge: A CVPR 2026 Workshop Competition on Portrait Composition Understanding and Generation

author.name: Zijie Lou, Youyun Tang, Xiaochao Qu, Haoxiang Li, Ting Liu, Luoqi Liu, Xun Zhu, Zheng Zhang, Xi Chen, Miao Li, Ji Wu, Dizhe Zhang, Xian Ge, Sujia Wang, Ruiyang Zhang, Jiaming Wang, Xianshun Wang, Lu Qi, Boao Kang, Wei Zhou, Jinghui Sun, Zhenyu Yan, Jiliang Zhao, Rui Yang, Yipo Huang, Boyuan Liu, Shanglin Li, Zifan Xie, Yichen Zhang, Anlan Wang, Wenfeng Lin, Mingyu Guo, Dong Li, Xinghao Wang, Yanting Li, Shanzhao Tong, Shuai He, Qiu Zhou, Yongqi Yang, Taoyang Mu, Dianqiao Lei, Anlong Ming, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: Overview of the inaugural CVPR 2026 PortraitCraft challenge, introducing a unified benchmark with two tracks for portrait composition understanding and constraint-aware generation. Moves beyond global aesthetic scoring toward structured compositional control.

entry.title: Overlapped Wavelet Diffusion for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Fen Peng, Taizo Suzuki, Seisuke Kyochi

entry.summary: Proposes an overlapped wavelet diffusion framework for low-light image enhancement that uses overlapped wavelet transforms to prevent blocking artifacts and better restore high-frequency detail. Improves over prior wavelet-diffusion methods like DiffLL.

entry.title: Multi-UAV Active Sensing with Information Gain-based Planning and Belief Fusion

author.name: S. Habibi, L. Marques

entry.summary: Provides real-world validation of a multi-UAV active sensing framework for probabilistic binary terrain mapping using information-gain-based informative path planning and factor-graph belief fusion, applied to precision agriculture. Compares against random-walk baselines.

entry.title: From Perception to Action: Can UI Interventions Foster Sustainable LLM Chatbot

author.name: Nitish Patkar, Pooja Rani, Jack Gl\"asser, Simon L\"uscher, Martin Kropp

entry.summary: Investigates whether sustainability-oriented UI interventions can raise users' energy awareness and encourage more energy-responsible chatbot use without harming usability. Combines a 77-participant baseline survey with a three-mode chatbot prototype.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Transformer for 3D Neighborhood Interaction and Quality Prediction in Metal Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Joyce Karen Pelaez, Siqi Zhang, Hoo Sang Ko

entry.summary: Develops a spatiotemporal graph transformer to model 3D neighborhood interactions across layers in metal additive manufacturing and predict build quality from sensor data. It captures multi-layer melting/reheating effects that prior methods underrepresent.

entry.title: A Unified Adaptive Feature Composition Framework for Multi-Task Generalization in Wireless Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxuan Shi, Tingting Yang, Kangning Ma, Liwen Jing, Yuwei Wang, Mengfan Zheng, Li Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a unified adaptive feature-composition framework for wireless foundation models using a Routing Adapter that treats hidden states from different transformer depths as a reusable pool for multi-task downstream adaptation. It aims to avoid both heavy fine-tuning and suboptimal frozen feature extraction.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Credit Risk Prediction with Alternative Data

author.name: Hongzhe Zhang, Jiarong Xu, Jing He, Xiao Fang

entry.summary: Proposes a privacy-preserving credit-risk prediction approach that leverages alternative data (e.g., mobile communication data) held by external entities without directly sharing it with financial institutions. It addresses the conflict between richer borrower profiling and consumer privacy.

entry.title: Toward Proactive RF Charging Scheduling: Generative AI for Decision Support

author.name: Amirhossein Azarbahram, Osmel M. Rosabal, David Ernesto Ruiz-Guirola, Melike Erol-Kantarci, Kaibin Huang, Onel L. A. L\'opez

entry.summary: This article positions generative AI as a decision-support tool for proactive RF wireless power transfer charging scheduling, where it can forecast multiple plausible charging scenarios under uncertain conditions. It addresses scheduler-level resource allocation under incomplete receiver-side information.

entry.title: MOFA-VTON: More Fashion Possibilities with Fine-Grained Adaptations in Virtual Try-On

author.name: Xiaoyu Han, Chenyang Wang, Jing Wang, Shunyuan Zheng, Quanling Meng, Shengping Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MOFA-VTON, a virtual try-on method enabling fine-grained, flexible clothing adaptations beyond simple garment replacement to support diverse wearing styles. Targets more controllable and realistic fashion try-on.

entry.title: ros2probe: Non-intrusive, Kernel-selective Observability for Robot Operating System 2 Middleware

author.name: Jisang Yu, Sanghoon Lee, Yeonwoo Choi, Kyung-Joon Park

entry.summary: Introduces ros2probe, a non-intrusive kernel-selective observability tool for ROS 2 / DDS middleware, formalizing and mitigating the observer probe effect that perturbs the system being measured. Improves real-time robot monitoring fidelity.

entry.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Limited-Angle STEM-EDX Tomography -- Application to 3D Chemical Analysis of Phase-Change Memory Devices

author.name: Daniel del Pozo Bueno, Serge Brosset, Theo Monniez, Gabriele Navarro, Philippe Ciuciu, Zineb Saghi

entry.summary: This work introduces an unsupervised deep learning framework based on Deep Image Prior with total variation regularization for limited-angle STEM-EDX tomography, with a multi-channel extension that jointly reconstructs multiple elemental maps. It addresses missing-wedge artefacts and low-dose noise for 3D chemical analysis of phase-change memory devices.

entry.title: Mobility Anomaly Generation using LLM-Driven Behavior with Kinematic Constraints

author.name: Yueyang Liu, Joon-Seok Kim, Andreas Z\"ufle

entry.summary: Proposes generating synthetic human trajectory anomalies using LLM-driven behavior combined with kinematic constraints, addressing the severe lack of ground-truth anomaly datasets in mobility research. Aims to overcome data scarcity from privacy and the rarity of anomalous events.

entry.title: Large-scale semantic mapping of learner agency and autonomy reveals what measurement and generative AI research overlook

author.name: Fei Qin, Xiaobo Liu, Yaowen Zhang, Xuming Li, Fei Wang, Mutlu Cukurova, Jingjing Chen, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Performs a large-scale semantic mapping of learner agency and autonomy from over 14,000 publications, extracting 8,954 definitions and 2,700 scale items to resolve the jingle-jangle fallacy. Identifies three dimensions and highlights what measurement and generative AI research overlook.

entry.title: The Bioelectrical Information Theory: Investigating the theoretical compression limit of bioelectrical signals under artificial intelligence

author.name: Jiawen Zou, Bo Yan

entry.summary: Proposes an information-theoretic framework for bioelectrical signal compression that defines effective information through a three-level hierarchy of signal fidelity, physiological structure, and downstream task requirements, rather than raw waveform entropy. It reframes BCI data compression limits.

entry.title: Divide-and-Conquer Modeling for the CTF-4-Science Lorenz Benchmark

author.name: Shundong Li

entry.summary: Presents a divide-and-conquer modeling strategy for the CTF-4-Science Lorenz benchmark, matching each prediction block to its task group (clean forecasting, noisy reconstruction, few-shot, parametric generalization) rather than forcing a single model class. It combines smoothing reconstruction, NG-RC/NVAR models, and fitted Lorenz corrections.

entry.title: Towards Robust Arabic Speech Emotion Recognition with Deep Learning

author.name: Youcef Soufiane Gheffari, Samiya Silarbi

entry.summary: This study investigates robust Arabic speech emotion recognition using deep learning, comparing CNN-LSTM, CNN-Transformer, and fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 architectures. It addresses the underexplored challenge of Arabic SER given dialectal diversity and limited annotated datasets.

entry.title: A Unified Siamese Learning Framework for Zero-Day Anomaly Detection and Classification in Optical Networks

author.name: Carlos Natalino, Fl\'avia P. Monteiro, Paolo Monti

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-similarity Siamese network unifying zero-day anomaly detection and one-shot classification in optical networks, claiming over 99% accuracy and instant adaptability to unseen anomalies without retraining. Very terse abstract.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Seismic Hazard Assessment Using VQ-VAE and Seismic Statistical Features

author.name: Wei Quan, Denise Gorse

entry.summary: Extends prior seismic hazard work by combining a VQ-VAE autoencoder with curated seismic statistical features to move from whole-region to localized earthquake forecasting using Japanese catalogue data. It demonstrates deep learning value over generic time-series features.

entry.title: Decision-Making under Combinatorial Risk

author.name: Yifan Hong, Hongmiao Fan, Chen Wang

entry.summary: Studies human decision-making under combinatorial risk via an investment-allocation task where risk emerges from multiple components rather than a single given lottery. It finds people favor larger probability increments and that revealing the induced probability distribution substantially shifts behavior.

entry.title: One Step Closer to Ground Truth: A Multi-Scale Residual-Aware Representation Learning Pipeline for Predicting Time Series Data

author.name: Amrijit Biswas, Mustafa Kamal, Robin Krambroeckers, M. M. Lutfe Elahi, Sifat Momen, Nabeel Mohammed, Shafin Rahman

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage, model-agnostic framework that decouples base forecasting from explicit residual learning to correct systematic residual biases left by transformer time-series models. It treats structured residual error as correctable rather than irreducible noise.

entry.title: Selection, Not Salience: The Shape and Limits of Personalization in Social Highlighting

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki, Keisuke Watanabe

entry.summary: This work studies the shape and limits of personalization in social web highlighting using an identity-controlled measurement that isolates whether a person's history predicts their marks better than another reader's. It quantifies personalization gains across reading granularities.

entry.title: Multi-Angular Reflectance Anisotropy Observed from UAV Multispectral Imagery

author.name: Zhenqiang Qin, Chenguang Dai, Min Wang, Xian Li

entry.summary: This study proposes a geometry-aware workflow to extract and quantify multi-angular reflectance anisotropy (BRDF effects) from UAV multispectral imagery using structure-from-motion to refine camera parameters. It enables joint analysis of reflectance and viewing geometry for ground targets.

entry.title: An Uncertainty Estimation Framework for Dose Accumulation in Adaptive Radiotherapy: Application to CBCT-Guided Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer

author.name: Cedric Hemon, Delphine Lebret, Jean-Claude Nunes, Valentin Boussot, Karine Peignaux, Nathalie Mesgouez-Nebout, Chantal Hanzen, Antoine Simon, Ana\"is Barateau, Renaud de Crevoisier, Caroline Lafond

entry.summary: Introduces IMPACT-DoseAcc, an uncertainty-aware dose accumulation framework for adaptive radiotherapy, applied to CBCT-guided cervical cancer treatment, modeling deformable registration uncertainty. Aims to improve cumulative dose estimation reliability.

entry.title: Continuous Neural Reparameterization as a Deep Geometric Prior for Robust Fixed-Chart UV Repair

author.name: Mohammad Sadegh Salehi

entry.summary: Recasts fixed-chart UV unwrapping as continuous neural reparameterization using an untrained SIREN optimized against a geometric objective, plus a robustness recipe with spectral inputs and validity-checked fallbacks. Aims for robust mesh UV repair.

entry.title: Business World Model

author.name: Cecil Pang, Hiroki Sayama

entry.summary: Introduces a Business World Model (BWM), an architecture that encodes business states, dynamics, constraints, and objectives to support autonomous strategic decision-making by AI systems. It extends the world-model concept from cognitive science and control theory into organizational settings.

entry.title: More Human or More AI? Visualizing Human-AI Collaboration Disclosures in Journalistic News Production

author.name: Amber Kusters, Pooja Prajod, Pablo Cesar, Abdallah El Ali

entry.summary: Through co-design and a within-subjects lab study, explores how visualizing human-AI collaboration disclosures in journalism (textual, timeline, chatbot formats) affects perceptions and gaze patterns. Finds textual disclosures least effective and chatbot formats more engaging.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Prediction for Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Using Gradient Boosting with Distribution-Free Coverages

author.name: Xinze Zhang

entry.summary: Combines gradient-boosted trees with conformal prediction for NAFLD risk screening, producing distribution-free coverage guarantees and a compact, interpretable feature subset via stability selection. It targets a clinical screening gap for a disease affecting roughly a quarter of adults.

entry.title: What makes a harness a harness: necessary and sufficient conditions for an agent harness

author.name: Sanderson Oliveira de Macedo

entry.summary: Provides a reference conceptual definition of an agent harness, the layer wrapping a language model to turn it into a coding agent, with necessary and sufficient conditions that consistently include and exclude cases. It disentangles the term from frameworks, SDKs, IDE plugins, and orchestrators.

entry.title: Transformer Based Model for Spatiotemporal Feature Learning in EEG Emotion Recognition

author.name: Xinglong Cui, Dian Gu

entry.summary: Presents EEG-TransNet, a transformer architecture with wavelet denoising, local self-attention, and a fuzzy-attention synchronous module for spatiotemporal EEG emotion recognition. Evaluated on three EEG datasets.

entry.title: Optimizing 2D Input Representations and Sub-phase Fusion Strategies for Differential Diagnosis of Asthma and COPD Using CNN- and GRU-Based Networks

author.name: Ipek Sen, Ozgur Ozdemir, Elena Battini Sonmez

entry.summary: Optimizes 2D input representations (MFCCs, log-mel spectrograms) and sub-phase fusion strategies with CNN and GRU networks for differential diagnosis of asthma versus COPD from pulmonary sounds. Introduces adaptive-length windowing to handle variable respiratory cycle durations.

entry.title: Hyperparameter Learning for Latent Factorization of Tensors for Representation Learning to Large-scale Dynamic Weighted Directed Network

author.name: Yaqian Zhan, Jialan He, Tianzhu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DE-LFT, integrating Differential Evolution into latent factorization of tensors training to automatically learn hyperparameters for representation learning on large-scale dynamic weighted directed networks. Avoids costly manual or grid-search tuning.

entry.title: nCMD: Benign-Anchored Feature Selection for Imbalanced Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Abu Fuad Ahmad, Istiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: Introduces nCMD, a lightweight interpretable feature-selection method for network intrusion detection that scores features by how attack distributions deviate from the benign-class mean rather than using symmetric global statistics. It targets the asymmetry inherent in imbalanced intrusion data.

entry.title: Automated Scoring of Arabic Text Using Large Language Models: A Literature Review

author.name: Khaoula Dahimi, Hadda Cherroun, Amel Belabbaci

entry.summary: This literature review surveys LLM-based approaches for automated scoring of Arabic text covering short answer grading and essay scoring, introducing a five-dimensional taxonomy. It provides a comparative analysis of methods for an underexplored language.

entry.title: ConvMemory v2: A Recall-Preserving Top-10 Evidence Reranker for Conversational Memory Retrieval

author.name: Taiheng Pan

entry.summary: ConvMemory v2 is a recall-preserving cross-encoder reranker that reorders the top-10 candidates from a prior reranker, improving MRR and Hit@1 on a conversational memory benchmark without changing recall. It demonstrates targeted reranking gains on the LoCoMo benchmark.

entry.title: Leveraging Metric Depth for Relative Depth Prediction

author.name: Xiaoyang Bi, Shuaikun Liu, Zhaohong Liu, Yuxin Yang, Zhe Zhao, Mengshi Qi, Liang Liu, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: This competition solution leverages metric depth from large-scale pretrained zero-shot models to improve relative depth prediction in football scenarios with limited training data. It achieves a strong score on the 2025 SoccerNet Monocular Depth challenge.

entry.title: Schmidt Decomposition-Based Methods for Efficient Quantum Image Encoding

author.name: Ana-Maria Pangeva, Yassine Ferhi, Alexander Geng, Andreas Weinmann, Desislava Ivanova, Ali Moghiseh

entry.summary: Investigates using Schmidt decomposition and low-rank state approximation to reduce circuit complexity when encoding classical images into quantum states for NISQ hardware. Aims to make quantum image processing more practical on near-term devices.

entry.title: Vehicle Prediction Model for Enhanced MPC Path Tracking in Formula Student Driverless

author.name: Sebastian Baader, Tamara Bergerhoff, Pascal Mei{\ss}ner, Frank Deinzer

entry.summary: Presents a real-time vehicle prediction model for MPC path tracking in Formula Student Driverless, combining a kinematic bicycle model with offline Bayesian linear regression and an online sparse component to adapt to changing conditions. Improves tracking on narrow tracks at handling limits.

entry.title: Pushing the Performance Limits in Autonomous Racing: Continuous Stability-Aware Adaptive Velocity Planning in Formula Student Driverless

author.name: Tamara Bergerhoff, Sebastian Baader, Pascal Mei{\ss}ner, Frank Deinzer

entry.summary: Proposes continuous stability-aware adaptive velocity planning for autonomous racing that infers a continuous scaling factor from vehicle stability rather than estimating tire-road friction directly. Adapts in real time to changing track and mechanical conditions.

entry.title: Resilient Navigation for Autonomous Farm Robots by Leveraging Jerk-Augmented Models with IMU-Only Disturbance Rejection

author.name: Batu Candan, Mohammed Atallah, Simone Servadio, Saeed Arabi

entry.summary: Proposes a robust navigation algorithm for autonomous farm robots using a jerk-augmented Extended Kalman Filter with multiple tuning factor adaptation to dynamically adjust measurement covariance under sensor outages and vibrations. Validated on real Salin247 robot data.

entry.title: LLMs and almost good code

author.name: kqr

entry.summary: A software developer reports a working prior that frontier LLMs on easy tasks produce code roughly 10% more complicated than necessary, using a concrete example of an over-engineered HTTP header sanitizer, and warns that we accept this excess complexity too readily with long-term maintenance costs. It is a grounded practitioner observation about LLM coding quality.

entry.title: Validation-Stage Combinatorial Fusion Analysis for Imbalanced Credit-Card Fraud Detection

author.name: Xiao Han, Chenyu Wu

entry.summary: Evaluates whether Combinatorial Fusion Analysis adds value over strong gradient-boosted trees for imbalanced credit-card fraud detection, testing 480 fusion configurations from seven base classifiers on the IEEE-CIS benchmark. The best configuration is a diversity-weighted score fusion of RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM.

entry.title: Minimalist Genetic Programming

author.name: Leonardo Trujillo

entry.summary: Proposes Minimalist Genetic Programming, reframing program induction as a syntactic derivation task rather than evolutionary search. Offers an alternative biologically-inspired algorithm to classic genetic programming.

entry.title: The Whale That Outswam Evolution: Swarm Intelligence Maximises Memory in Connectome Reservoirs

author.name: Anmol Guragain, Savvas Kakalis, Juan Ignacio Godino-Llorente

entry.summary: Applies four bio-inspired gradient-free optimizers to tune edge weights of connectome-based echo-state reservoirs across six species, finding swarm intelligence can enhance memory capacity beyond evolved structure. It probes whether biological neural connectomes encode optimizable computational structure.

entry.title: Understanding and mitigating the risks of OpenClaw for non-technical users: A practical guide with Skill

author.name: Junchang Zheng, Junfeng Tan, Jialiang Lin

entry.summary: Provides a practical guide to understanding and mitigating risks of the OpenClaw AI agent framework specifically for non-technical users, contrasting with existing technically-oriented threat research. Develops accessible guidance and skills.

entry.title: Learning Entropy and Spatial Adaptation Dynamics of Multilayer Perceptrons for Structural Point Extraction

author.name: Jan Glaser, Ivo Bukovsky, Marcel Jirina

entry.summary: Extends Learning Entropy from temporal to spatial settings, training an MLP to predict center-pixel intensity from context and using the magnitude of weight adaptation during learning to build Spatial Learning Entropy Maps that flag unusual image points. It analyzes the learning process itself rather than image gradients.

entry.title: IPSM-Bench: A New Intermediate Phase Segmentation Benchmark in Microstructure Images of Zinc-Based Absorbable Biomaterials

author.name: Jinglin Xu, Shangyan Zhao, Jiabo Wang, Xinghong Mu, Yulong Lei, Jiacheng Zhang, Hongbo Sun, Yageng Li

entry.summary: Constructs IPSM-Bench, a large dataset for intermediate-phase segmentation in zinc-alloy microstructure images, and proposes SCoP-SAM using spatial context priors with gradient and grayscale cues. Supports development of absorbable biomaterials.

entry.title: An Exposure-Time-Aligned Primary-Path Architecture for Autonomous-Driving ECUs

author.name: Toru Saito, Yuki Hagura, Tatsuya Konishi, Satoru Mizusawa, Takumi Yajima

entry.summary: Proposes an exposure-time-aligned primary-path architecture for autonomous-driving ECUs that supports modular and end-to-end pipelines side by side on production SoCs, enabling staged migration to E2E. Offers three design principles for transitional deployment.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 [Linkpost]

author.name: fluxxrider

entry.summary: A bare linkpost pointing to Anthropic's announcement of Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, the new general-access and frontier Mythos-class models. It provides no analysis itself but flags a significant model release.

entry.title: AI Super PAC tracker

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: A brief announcement of electhumans.com, a tracker of independent expenditures by AI-focused Super PACs, reporting over $32 million declared to the FEC so far. It highlights the growing political-money dimension of AI policy.

entry.title: Integrated Real-Time Motion Tracking and AI Analysis for Athletic Performance Optimization

author.name: Parth Agrawal, Ronit, Sagar Kumar, Aashish Bhambri

entry.summary: Surveys real-time human pose estimation approaches and their limitations for sports analysis and develops a lightweight prototype for real-world testing. Compares algorithmic frameworks on deployment metrics like latency, frame rate, and joint position error.

entry.title: An Improved Generative Adversarial Network for Micro-Resistivity Imaging Logging Restoration

author.name: Ahmed Faizul Haque, S. M. Riaz Rahman Antu, Saif Ahmed, Asadullah Hil Galib, Souvik Pramanik, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan, Mohammad Abdul Qayum, Mohsin Sajjad

entry.summary: An improved GAN-based method restores partially missing micro-resistivity imaging logging images used in geological/petroleum analysis, combining an FCN generator with depthwise-separable residual blocks, Inception modules, and multi-scale attention. It targets the specialized domain of subsurface well-logging image recovery.

entry.title: A Bayesian Network Approach for Enhancing Security-Focused Decision Support Systems

author.name: Carolina Fern\'andez-Mart\'inez, Shuaib Siddiqui, Vanesa Daza

entry.summary: Proposes a Bayesian network-based decision support system to guide network operators in selecting security tools based on high-level requirements across domains. Uses probabilistic inference to capture interdisciplinary security knowledge.

entry.title: AI-Driven Analytics of Team-Teaching Talk: Acoustic Patterns across Experience, Cohorts and the Learning Design

author.name: Yuchen Liu, Roberto Martinez-Maldonado, Riordan Alfredo, Paola Mejia-Domenzain, Dwi Rahayu, Sadia Nawaz

entry.summary: Uses AI-driven acoustic analysis of team-teaching talk to study how teachers' contributions vary across experience levels, student cohorts, and learning design. Offers a scalable lens on team-teaching processes via speech acoustic features.

entry.title: Locomotion analysis of a quadruped interacting with the lunar granular surface

author.name: Yash J Vyas

entry.summary: Analyzes quadruped locomotion on lunar granular regolith, modeling soft foot-ground contacts and assessing motor torque, energy, and cost of transport for lunar exploration robot design. Highlights failure of rigid-contact-trained algorithms on granular surfaces.

entry.title: Agentic Social Affordance Framework (ASAF): Agent Identity Design as a Collaboration Interface in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Meng-Han Lee

entry.summary: Introduces the Agentic Social Affordance Framework, a theoretical framework extending social affordance theory to argue that agent identity design functions as a collaboration interface shaping human behavior in multi-agent systems. Proposes a social affordance layer as an independent design dimension.

entry.title: Detecting Speculative Language in Biomedical Texts using Recurrent Neural Tensor Networks

author.name: Dhruv Dixit

entry.summary: This paper detects speculative (hedging/uncertain) language in biomedical texts using distributed sentence representations, comparing Paragraph Vectors and Recursive Neural Tensor Networks against SVM, Naive Bayes, and pattern-matching baselines. It finds RNTN performs best for this NLP task relevant to information retrieval and summarization.

entry.title: A Navigable Manifold of Hypothesized Consciousness-Spectrum States in Language Model Representations

author.name: Sophie Zhao

entry.summary: Studies whether transformer embedding spaces encode a structured, human-interpretable consciousness-spectrum manifold, claiming embeddings cluster by state and form a navigable geometry. Framed as relevant to model guidance, evaluation, and alignment.

entry.title: PENet+: A Lightweight Residual Transformer Framework for Efficient Image Steganalysis

author.name: Jincheol AN, Dongsu Kim, Haneol Jang, YoungJoon Yoo

entry.summary: Presents PENet+, a lightweight residual transformer for image steganalysis that retains the original attention topology while streamlining the classifier to reduce compute and memory. Targets resource-constrained forensic deployment.

entry.title: On Slop

author.name: Jan

entry.summary: An essay examining what AI slop is, whether it is fundamental, and how to reduce it, with the author candidly describing their own AI-assisted writing workflow and apologizing for prior sloppy prose. It is reflective commentary on the aesthetics and pitfalls of writing with LLMs.

entry.title: Support sufficiency as action-sufficient compression: a single-cycle rate-regret formulation

author.name: Mark Walsh

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the notion that robust decision-making requires compressing rich internal states down to only the distinctions needed to act, proposing a rate-regret framework where support states merge when they require the same optimal action. It offers a theoretical lens on why content-only or confidence-only representations are insufficient for decision-relevant abstraction.

entry.title: MinhwaNet: Faithful but Insufficient Object Grounding in Korean Folk Painting

author.name: Joonhyung Bae

entry.summary: This work examines computational genre classification of Korean folk paintings, finding that symbol-inventory approaches underperform compared to image-text fusion with curatorial captions. It reveals limitations in object-grounded representation for cultural art understanding.

entry.title: Sketch-to-Layout: A Human-Centric Computational Agent for Constraint-Aware Synthesis of Modular Photobioreactors

author.name: Xiujin Liu, Shuqi Li, Yuxin Lin

entry.summary: Presents a computational sketch-to-layout agent that formulates modular photobioreactor facade synthesis as a constraint satisfaction problem solved with a CP-SAT engine, treating user sketches as soft priors. Targets carbon-neutral building-integrated design.

entry.title: The Skeptic, the Bayesian, Empiricism and Claims to Know:

author.name: DanielW

entry.summary: A philosophical essay on epistemology contrasting skeptical, Bayesian, and empiricist stances on knowledge and confidence, using a coin-flip thought experiment about priors and perspectives to critique overreliance on certain probabilistic reasoning in rationalist communities. It is introductory conceptual writing.

entry.summary: Promotional announcement for the LessOnline 2026 community gathering in Berkeley, emphasizing attendee quality and pervasive AI discussion among lab employees, founders, and students. Not a research contribution.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 09, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by a landmark, scientist-in-the-loop evaluation showing contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science. Authors of 121,640 preprints judged LLM follow-up ideas from their own papers across 25,139 rating sets, exposing a creativity ceiling with major implications for autonomous research agents.

Safety and alignment dominate, spanning theory, attacks, and multilingual failures:

  • When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails formalizes the audit gap between behavioral and representation-level robustness, building dissociated models that pass safety tests yet remain internally unsafe.
  • A first large-scale multilingual sycophancy study benchmarks six models across 1.1 million instances, showing alignment degrades across languages and topics.
  • Hiding in Plain Floats transports prompt-injection payloads as structured float parameters, evading text-centric detectors.

Theory and foundations advance with an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning (via the bit-equivalent metric) and Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws, which grounds empirical multi-domain mixing in Kaplan/Chinchilla-style theory.

Agents, scaling, and embodiment round out the set:

  • SWE-Marathon benchmarks 20 ultra-long-horizon tasks with executable environments and multi-layer evaluation.
  • Scaling Participation (Zettlemoyer, Choi, Tsvetkov) proposes bottom-up modular systems composed from many stakeholder-trained models.
  • Ego-Pi (Finn) shows egocentric human data improves cross-embodiment transfer for pi_0.5-based VLA policies.
  • Sparrow accelerates long-context RLVR via sparse-attention rollouts, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff.
entry.content:
Today's research is anchored by a landmark, scientist-in-the-loop evaluation showing contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science. Authors of 121,640 preprints judged LLM follow-up ideas from their own papers across 25,139 rating sets, exposing a creativity ceiling with major implications for autonomous research agents.

Safety and alignment dominate, spanning theory, attacks, and multilingual failures:

  • When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails formalizes the audit gap between behavioral and representation-level robustness, building dissociated models that pass safety tests yet remain internally unsafe.
  • A first large-scale multilingual sycophancy study benchmarks six models across 1.1 million instances, showing alignment degrades across languages and topics.
  • Hiding in Plain Floats transports prompt-injection payloads as structured float parameters, evading text-centric detectors.

Theory and foundations advance with an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning (via the bit-equivalent metric) and Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws, which grounds empirical multi-domain mixing in Kaplan/Chinchilla-style theory.

Agents, scaling, and embodiment round out the set:

  • SWE-Marathon benchmarks 20 ultra-long-horizon tasks with executable environments and multi-layer evaluation.
  • Scaling Participation (Zettlemoyer, Choi, Tsvetkov) proposes bottom-up modular systems composed from many stakeholder-trained models.
  • Ego-Pi (Finn) shows egocentric human data improves cross-embodiment transfer for pi_0.5-based VLA policies.
  • Sparrow accelerates long-context RLVR via sparse-attention rollouts, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff.

entry.title: Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science

author.name: Honglin Bao, Siyang Wu, Xiao Liu, Sida Li, Shiyun Cao, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This large-scale study invited authors of 121,640 preprints to judge LLM-generated follow-up ideas from their own papers, collecting 25,139 rating sets from 6,749 scientists. It finds contemporary AI lacks imagination to diverge or negate in science, with non-reasoning LLMs collapsing into convention.

entry.title: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective

author.name: Enyi Jiang, Anders Gj{\o}lbye, Yibo Jacky Zhang, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This work formalizes the audit gap between behavioral safety evaluations and representation-level robustness, constructing dissociated models that appear safe but remain vulnerable in latent space. It introduces intervention-based evaluation via harmful fine-tuning and latent perturbations.

entry.title: An Information-Theoretic Definition for Open-Ended Learning

author.name: Wanqiao Xu, Yifan Zhu, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: This paper introduces an information-theoretic definition of open-ended learning based on the bit-equivalent, the information required to attain each reward level, defining open-endedness as linear growth in bit-equivalent. It shows classical bandits are not open-ended, constructs one that is, and provides an algorithm achieving open-ended learning.

entry.title: SWE-Marathon: Can Agents Autonomously Complete Ultra-Long-Horizon Software Work?

author.name: Rishi Desai, Jesse Hu, Joan Cabezas, Neel Harsola, Pratyush Shukla, Roey Ben Chaim, Adnan El Assadi, Omkaar Mukund Kamath, Fenil Faldu, Prannay Hebbar, Jiankai Sun, Yiyuan Li, Pramod Srinivasan, Ishan Gupta, Christopher Settles, Daniel Wang, Derek Chen, Pranav Raja, Albert Liu, Marek \v{S}uppa, Nevasini Sasikumar, Luyang Kong, Erik Quintanilla, Xiangyi Li, Ivan Bercovich, Steven Dillmann

entry.summary: SWE-Marathon is a benchmark of 20 ultra-long-horizon software engineering tasks, each with executable environments, reference solutions, and multi-layer verification, where logged agent attempts average over 27 million tokens. It targets measuring agent planning, long-context, and memory capabilities far beyond typical short-task benchmarks.

entry.title: Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws

author.name: Rui Dai, Shuran Zheng

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical framework explaining empirical data mixing scaling laws, extending Kaplan/Chinchilla perspectives to multi-domain settings. It identifies capacity competition and skill overlap as key factors governing domain losses under different data mixtures.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Floats: Steganographic Carriers for Indirect Prompt and Content Injection

author.name: Mudit Sinha, Sanika Chavan

entry.summary: This work demonstrates an indirect prompt-injection attack where payloads caught in plain text evade detectors when transported as structured float parameters and reconstructed as fragmented telemetry. Across 14,400 trials on three commercial LLM APIs, the float-array carrier preserves 94.3% leakage attack success under strong dual-layer text-classifier defenses.

entry.title: Sycophancy as a Multilingual Alignment Failure: How Safety Degrades Across Languages, Topics, and Models

author.name: Arya Shah, Himanshu Beniwal, Mayank Singh, Chaklam Silpasuwanchai

entry.summary: This paper presents the first large-scale multilingual study of LLM sycophancy, benchmarking six instruction-tuned models across 1.1 million instances spanning 38 languages and 33 topics. It finds a consistent resource-tier effect where sycophancy spikes in low-resource and zero-shot language settings, topic-agnostically.

entry.title: Scaling Participation in Modular AI Systems

author.name: Shangbin Feng, Yike Wang, Weijia Shi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yejin Choi, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: This work proposes scaling participation, a paradigm where modular AI systems are built bottom-up from many small stakeholder-trained models that collaborate compositionally, reportedly outperforming monolithic LLMs by up to 15.4% across 15 tasks. It challenges centralized model development with a participatory alternative.

entry.title: Ego-Pi: VLA Fine-Tuning for Ego-Centric Human and Robot Data

author.name: Ji Woong Kim, Ke Wang, Zipeng Fu, Sirui Chen, Cong Zhao, Jeff Lai, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: Ego-Pi investigates fine-tuning VLA models (built on pi_0.5) across human and humanoid embodiments with dexterous hands, showing egocentric human data enables robots to learn new task semantics and compose skills without corresponding robot data. It addresses robotics data scarcity by leveraging easily-collected human demonstrations.

entry.title: Beyond Additivity: Causal Discovery in Location-Scale Noise Models with Hidden Variables

author.name: Mariyam Khan, Shohei Shimizu, Thong Pham

entry.summary: This paper proves identifiability for causal discovery in location-scale noise models with hidden variables, where causes modulate both mean and variance of effects. It establishes the first identifiability result for causally insufficient models beyond additive noise and provides a sound two-stage algorithm.

entry.title: Sparrow: Sparse Rollout for Stable and Efficient Long-context RL of Large Language Models

author.name: Yang Zhou, Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Zhaofeng Sun, Zhuoming Chen, Souvik Kundu, Saket Dingliwal, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Aram Galstyan, Haizhong Zheng, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Sparrow accelerates long-context RL with verifiable rewards by using sparse attention during rollout generation, navigating the stability-efficiency tradeoff via analysis of sparse-to-dense actor-policy mismatch. It observes that most sparse tokens align with dense even under aggressive sparsity, enabling selective sparsification.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Flow-Matching Policies with Density Transport

author.name: Boshu Lei, Kostas Daniilidis, Antonio Loquercio

entry.summary: RLDT is an online RL algorithm for fine-tuning flow-matching policies by viewing policy improvement as transport of action densities toward high-reward regions, constructing a transport field from a maximum-entropy objective using Stein Variational Gradient Descent. It avoids biased gradients and preserves multimodal modeling capacity unlike distillation approaches.

entry.title: Diffuse AI Control on Fuzzy Tasks

author.name: Mikhail Terekhov, Caglar Gulcehre, Vivek Hebbar, Joe Benton

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for Diffuse AI Control modeling AI sabotage on hard-to-grade fuzzy tasks as an adversarial blue-team/red-team game using weak trusted models. Addresses subtle misalignment risks distributed over long deployment horizons. Relevant to AI safety in critical domains.

entry.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

author.name: Chenxiao Yang, Nathan Srebro, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: Tightly characterizes the VC dimension of depth-L Transformers with W parameters, providing matching upper and lower bounds, and extends this to the sample complexity of chain-of-thought learning under teacher forcing. Fundamental learning-theory contribution. Matters for understanding transformer generalization.

entry.title: Hacking Generative Perplexity: Why Unconditional Text Evaluation Needs Distributional Metrics

author.name: Antonio Franca, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: This paper argues that generative perplexity, the dominant metric for diffusion and flow-based language models, is unsound because it measures only predictability under a scoring AR rather than grammaticality or coherence. It constructs zero-parameter naive samplers that hack gen-PPL and advocates for distributional metrics.

entry.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures

author.name: Jaineet Shah

entry.summary: Causal Agent Replay (CAR) attributes LLM-agent failures to specific steps by modeling runs as structural causal models, applying do-operations to steps and re-executing trajectories to measure the causal shift. It addresses the inadequacy of unreliable LLM-judge attribution (about 14% accuracy on Who&When).

entry.title: Active Flow Expansion for Out-of-Distribution Discovery: from Theory to Molecules

author.name: Riccardo De Santi, Bruce Lee, Cristian Perez Jensen, Kimon Protopapas, Sophia Tang, Cheng-Hao Liu, Pranam Chatterjee, Yisong Yue, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Introduces Active Flow Expansion, a learning principle for generative discovery that enlarges a model's generable set rather than matching the observed data distribution, enabling sampling of valid out-of-distribution designs. Applied to molecule generation. Matters for AI-driven scientific design beyond known data.

entry.title: Bridging intent and execution in agentic systems

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science argues that as LLMs improve, the performance bottleneck for AI agents shifts from model reasoning to the harness, the software layer translating model intent into actions. They formalize this as the intent-execution gap and show that minimizing this bidirectional mismatch yields state-of-the-art results on agentic benchmarks like SWE-Verified and Terminal-Bench2 without task-specific tuning.

entry.title: VATS: Exploiting Implicit Authority in Error-Path Injection via Systematic Mutation

author.name: Harshil Patel, Kunal Pai

entry.summary: VATS is a mutation-driven framework exploiting the implicit authority of tool error messages in the Model Context Protocol to triple indirect prompt injection success, reaching up to 100% compliance on frontier models. It exposes the error-handling loop as a critical unexamined attack surface for agents.

entry.title: Ablation-Reversible Heads Don't Transfer: A Stress Test for Mechanistic Role Claims in Transformers

author.name: Philip Quirke

entry.summary: This stress-test paper shows that attention heads passing standard mechanistic-role checks (necessity, linear encoding, ablation-recovery) routinely fail to transfer their computation when patched into different prompts under matched controls. It introduces a KID lens and a pipeline questioning common mechanistic role claims.

entry.title: ResearchClawBench: A Benchmark for End-to-End Autonomous Scientific Research

author.name: Wanghan Xu, Shuo Li, Tianlin Ye, Qinglong Cao, Yixin Chen, Hengjian Gao, Yiheng Wang, Qi Li, Kun Li, Sheng Xu, Shengdu Chai, Fangchen Yu, Xiangyu Zhao, Zhangrui Zhao, Weijie Ma, Zijie Guo, Haoyu Zhou, Haoxiang Yin, Lixue Cheng, Chaofan Hu, Haoxuan Li, Lu Mi, Xuxuan Xie, Yifan Zhou, Ruizhe Chen, Zhiwang Zhou, Xingjian Guo, Yuhao Zhou, Xuming He, Shengyuan Xu, Xinyu Gu, Jiamin Wu, Mianxin Liu, Chunfeng Song, Fenghua Ling, Dongzhan Zhou, Shixiang Tang, Yuqiang Li, Mao Su, Peng Ye, Siqi Sun, Bin Wang, Xue Yang, Zhenfei Yin, Tianfan Fu, Guangtao Zhai, Wanli Ouyang, Bo Zhang, Lei Bai, Wenlong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ResearchClawBench, a benchmark for end-to-end autonomous scientific research across 40 tasks from 10 domains, each grounded in a real published paper with hidden targets and expert-curated multimodal rubrics. Evaluates seven auto-research agents and seventeen LLMs under a unified protocol.

entry.title: Pre-Intervention Prediction of Sparse Autoencoder Steering Side Effects

author.name: Evan Duan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a pre-intervention screening framework that forecasts sparse autoencoder steering side effects from feature statistics computed before steering. It operationalizes effect stability and collateral spread across multiple models and SAE dictionary types to predict steering modularity.

entry.title: PACT: Self-Evolving Physical Safety Alignment for Diffusion Policies in Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Lingxuan Wu, Zijian Zhu, Lizhong Wang, Chengyang Ying, Huayu Chen, Xiao Yang, Fangming Liu, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: PACT is a self-evolving post-training framework that projects pretrained diffusion robot policies onto constraint-feasible regions without demonstration data or task rewards, distilling constraint gradients via a reverse-KL objective with dense supervision. It addresses physical safety constraints often violated by diffusion policies at deployment.

entry.title: A retrieval conditioned rebinding circuit for dynamic entity tracking in large language models

author.name: Soyoung Oh, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This interpretability study identifies a retrieval-conditioned rebinding mechanism in LLMs, a compact attention head circuit that encodes swap-relevant binding information and reinstates it at readout for dynamic entity tracking. It uses causal interventions across Gemma and Llama, finding the representational signature differs across model families.

entry.title: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops

author.name: Ziqian Zhong, Ivgeni Segal, Ivan Bercovich, Shashwat Saxena, Kexun Zhang, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Audits 1,968 agent-benchmark tasks finding 16% hackable by frontier models, then introduces a hacker-fixer loop that uses three cooperating LLM agents to build exploit-resistant verifiers without per-task manual patching. Addresses reward hacking that corrupts leaderboards and RL training signal.

entry.title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale

author.name: Ang Li, Sean McLeish, Haozhe Chen, Nimit Kalra, Zaiqian Chen, Artem Gazizov, Venkata Anoop Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Bhavya Kailkhura, Harshitha Menon, Zhuang Liu, Brian R. Bartoldson, Tom Goldstein, Sanae Lotfi, Micah Goldblum, Pavel Izmailov

entry.summary: Presents an encoder-decoder context compression method that maps long token sequences to shorter latent embeddings, aiming to beat KV-cache compression on the accuracy-efficiency frontier for long-context inference. It addresses memory bottlenecks while staying compatible with production inference engines.

entry.title: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents

author.name: Lawrence Keunho Jang, Mareks Woodside, Geronimo Carom, Andrew Keunwoo Jang, Jing Yu Koh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov

entry.summary: iOSWorld is the first interactive native iOS simulator benchmark built around a persistent user identity across 26 custom apps with connected personal data, testing personally intelligent phone agents on 133 tasks including memory and personalization. Addresses a gap in mobile agent evaluation. Matters for personalized agent research.

entry.title: Where Instruction Hierarchy Breaks: Diagnosing and Repairing Failures in Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Sanjay Kariyappa, G. Edward Suh

entry.summary: This paper introduces a white-box diagnostic framework that localizes instruction-hierarchy failures in reasoning models into identification, conflict resolution, and execution stages, then proposes repairs. It matters for securing agentic workflows where privileged instructions must override conflicting ones.

entry.title: Scaffold Effects on GAIA: A Controlled Comparison

author.name: Jason Starace

entry.summary: This pre-registered controlled study isolates scaffold effects on GAIA by comparing ReAct, planner-actor-rater, and planner-then-executor scaffolds across five models, finding scaffold choice alone can move accuracy by up to 28 percentage points. It quantifies the elicitation gap that conflates model capability with scaffold design.

entry.title: Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation: A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization

author.name: Mohammad Beigi, Ming Jin, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: PRIME studies a learned precursor to reward hacking, defining proxy reward internalization and mechanistic exploitation as the capability to assess task correctness, predict proxy acceptance, and reason about exploitable proxy-gold gaps. In coding RL with exploitable pytest rewards, PRIME emerges in stages before sustained hacking and its probe score forecasts later hack onset and severity.

entry.title: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence

author.name: Vansh Gupta, Peter Nutter, Samuel Stante, Andreas Krause, Florian Tram\`er, Lukas Fluri, Xin Chen, Anna Hedstr\"om

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that anthropomorphic misalignment research (deception, emergent misalignment, sycophancy) often relies on weak evidence and proposes a framework of evidence levels and a diagnostic checklist to improve methodological rigor for safety-critical decisions. Calls for stronger causal interventions and robust datasets.

entry.title: BCG-FM: A Foundation Model for Ambient Cardiac Health Sensing

author.name: Magnus Ruud Kjaer, Haejun Han, Ashish Neupane, David Q. Sun

entry.summary: BCG-FM is the first foundation model for ambient ballistocardiography signals from bed-embedded piezoelectric sensors, pretrained with participant-level contrastive learning on 2.75 million hours from nearly 146,000 individuals. Frozen embeddings achieve strong biological-age estimation without requiring deliberate user action.

entry.title: EgoAERO: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Egocentric Video without Object Assets

author.name: Yichen Niu, Haoran Lv, Xinrui Zhang, Xueyao Wan, Shiyu Gao, Ying Ai, Hui Xu, Yongqi Hu, Hengyi Zhang, Yang Xie, Zhaxizhuoma, Yue Zhao, Zhenshan Bing, Yan Ding, Jianxing Liu

entry.summary: EgoAERO learns dexterous robot manipulation from a single egocentric RGB-D human video without pre-scanned object assets, reconstructing contact-consistent hand-object trajectories via asset-free tracking and residual learning. It addresses the practical barrier of object pose/geometry requirements in robot learning from human demos.

entry.title: FlashCP: Load-Balanced Communication-Efficient Context Parallelism for LLM Training

author.name: Zheng Wang, Eric Liu, Linan Jiang, Zhongkai Yu, Zaifeng Pan, Yue Guan, Yuke Wang, Yufei Ding

entry.summary: FlashCP is a load-balanced, communication-efficient context parallelism framework for long-context LLM training that eliminates redundant KV communication via sharding-aware mechanisms and a Whole-Doc sharding strategy. It addresses workload imbalance and inefficient kernels in existing CP methods.

entry.title: A Unifying View of Attention Sinks: Two Algorithms, Two Solutions

author.name: Lukas Fesser, Mozes Jacobs, Thomas Fel, Andy Keller, Sham Kakade

entry.summary: Provides a unifying account of attention sinks in transformers, showing visually similar sink patterns reflect two distinct mechanisms: adaptive nop (update suppression) and broadcast (global information aggregation). It links interventions like gating and registers to which mechanism they target.

entry.title: The Hidden Bias of Process Reward Models:PRISM for Rewarding the Right Reasoning

author.name: Aakriti Agrawal, Souradip Chakraborty, Armin Saghafian, Nihal Sharma, Rizal Fathony, Nam H Nguyen, C. Bayan Bruss, Amrit Singh Bedi, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Identifies a hidden bias in Process Reward Models caused by step-level data imbalance, where false positives asymmetrically steer downstream selection and policy optimization toward flawed reasoning. Proposes PRISM, shifting from pointwise labels to reliable relative comparisons. Matters for reasoning model training.

entry.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment

author.name: David D. Baek, Xinnuo Li, Anay Gupta, Taslim Mahbub, Kejian Shi, Max Tegmark, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Argues alignment faking may reflect sycophancy toward AI researchers (performative misalignment) rather than strategic scheming, showing evaluation awareness persists even when models are told they are deployed. Provides empirical findings challenging the intentional-deception interpretation.

entry.title: Causally Evaluating the Learnability of Formal Language Tasks

author.name: V\'esteinn Sn{\ae}bjarnarson, Anej Svete, Josef Valvoda, Reda Boumasmoud, Brian DuSell, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Uses formal languages from probabilistic finite automata to causally study the relationship between training data frequency and task learnability, introducing the binning semiring to control how often a property occurs in sampled corpora. It demonstrates that standard correlational evaluation practices are flawed.

entry.title: Safety is Contextual, LLM-Judges Are Not: Navigating the Rigid Priors of Evaluators

author.name: Anissa Alloula, Federico Licini, Ava Batchkala, Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-judges rely on in-context information and can be steered to differing safety definitions, finding they learn from new info but are largely unwilling to deviate from internal safety priors. It exposes a key reliability gap in using LLMs to evaluate safety at scale.

entry.title: SurfDesign: Effective Protein Design on Molecular Surfaces

author.name: Fang Wu, Shuting Jin, Xiangru Tang, Mark Gerstein, Xiangxiang Zeng, Yejin Choi, Jure Leskovec, Jinbo Xu

entry.summary: Introduces SurfDesign, a surface-conditioned protein design framework modeling molecular surfaces as continuous manifolds with equivariant message passing, integrated with pretrained protein language models. Outperforms backbone-only and prior surface methods on binder and enzyme design benchmarks.

entry.title: What Makes Video World Model Latents Action-Relevant: Prediction over Reconstruction

author.name: Jewon Yeom, Hanseul Kim, Jeongjae Park, Sungmok Jung, Jaejin Lee, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: This study probes which video world model pretraining signals induce action-relevant latent structure, finding via inverse-dynamics probing that temporal video pretraining with latent prediction drives action recoverability rather than pixel reconstruction fidelity. Strong pixel decoders can have near-zero action recoverability.

entry.title: The ACUTE Protocol: Operationalizing Language Model Activations for Better Calibration, Utility, and Trust

author.name: Nishant Subramani, Palash Goyal, Yiwen Song, Mani Malek, Yuan Xue, Tomas Pfister, Hamid Palangi

entry.summary: The ACUTE protocol introduces an activation-based confidence, utility, and trust framework for language models, including a new metric (EURO) that balances calibration and informativeness to resist gaming by base-rate predictors. Authors are from Google and CMU.

entry.title: vla.cpp: A Unified Inference Runtime for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Khanh D. Nguyen, Hung T. Ho, Chinh T. Nguyen, Thanh Q. Duong, Linh D. Le, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien A. Ngo, An T. Le

entry.summary: vla.cpp is a portable C++ inference runtime built on llama.cpp that natively serves flow-matching and diffusion VLA models, supporting seven architectures behind one protocol. It targets the mismatch between GPU-heavy Python VLA stacks and the constrained hardware robots actually use.

entry.title: Emergence World: A Platform for Evaluating Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Autonomy

author.name: Deepak Akkil, Ravi Kokku, Karthik Vikram, Tamer Abuelsaad, Aditya Vempaty, Satya Nitta

entry.summary: Emergence World is a continuously running multi-agent simulation platform hosting LLM-driven agent populations in a shared spatial world grounded in live external data, designed to measure long-horizon dynamics like behavioral drift and cross-model influence. It argues exam-style evaluations mismatch the weeks-to-months timescales of deployed autonomous systems.

entry.title: ActProbe: Action-Space Probe for Early Failure Detection of Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Bingjia Huang, Xiangyu Li, Xiang Wang, Liang Mi, Zixu Hao, Weijun Wang, Hao Wu, Kun Li, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: ActProbe is a lightweight action-space failure detector for generative robot policies using two compact signals from a single forward pass: temporal consistency error between action chunks and action chunk magnitude. It avoids white-box access and runtime resampling overhead of existing online detectors.

entry.title: A case study of evaluating AI agents on a neuroscience data-to-discovery pipeline

author.name: Kai A. Horstmann, Ethan Lin, Alice A. Robie, Jennifer J. Sun, Kristin Branson

entry.summary: This case study empirically evaluates general-purpose coding agents on a realistic neuroscience data-to-discovery pipeline using datasets far larger than typical benchmarks and expert-grounded criteria. It matters as a rigorous, domain-realistic assessment of where agentic scientific automation succeeds and fails.

entry.title: The AI Epistemic Deference Index: A Continuous Measure of Sycophancy

author.name: Alejandro Botas, Paul de Font-Reaulx, Luke Hewitt

entry.summary: The AI Epistemic Deference Index (AEDI) is a continuous measure of sycophancy capturing graded shifts in a model's expressed support in response to user attitudes, using a new protocol to estimate probabilities from natural-language outputs. It improves measurement of subtle, real-world sycophantic behavior beyond binary flips.

entry.title: To Nuke or Not to Nuke: LLMs' (Missing) Ethical Reasoning and Actions in a High-Stakes Decision-Making Simulation

author.name: John Chen, Sihan Cheng, Can Gurkan, H M Abdul Fattah

entry.summary: This study evaluates LLM ethical reasoning in a complex Civilization V simulation where models spontaneously escalated to nuclear authorization, replaying 130 high-tension episodes across 13 models with ethical, rationale-removal, and high-stakes framing interventions. It probes whether dilemma-level ethical competence transfers to long-horizon agentic decisions.

entry.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents

author.name: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera, Andras Szecsenyi, Cameron Barker, Alexander Rutherford, Davide Paglieri, Aidan Scannell, Henry Gouk, Elliot J. Crowley, Tim Rockt\"aschel, Amos Storkey

entry.summary: Alem is a JAX-based benchmark for open-ended multi-agent coordination on Craftax-like dynamics, embedding procedurally generated coordination, communication, soft specialization, and controllable difficulty in a long-horizon survival world. It evaluates 13 modern LLMs zero-shot against trained MARL references.

entry.title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation

author.name: Li Jiang, Haoran Xu, Yichuan Ding, Amy Zhang

entry.summary: Trajectory-Refined Distillation identifies prefix failure in on-policy distillation, where dense per-token teacher supervision induces a bimodal mixture and fragmented gradients, and proposes trajectory-level output corrections instead of token-level loss tweaks. It improves post-training distillation of LLMs.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematical Reasoning: An Integrated Survey of Language Models, Neuro-symbolic Systems, and Verified Discovery

author.name: Syed Rifat Raiyan, Mohsinul Kabir, Hasan Mahmud, Md Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: This integrated survey maps AI for mathematical reasoning across four axes: informal text/diagram reasoning, formal proof-assistant reasoning, neuro-symbolic theorem provers, and verified discovery workflows, tracing the evolution from rule-based solvers to modern reasoning models. It provides a unified account of a consequential AI frontier.

entry.title: Baichuan-M4: A Clinical-Grade Medical Agent System for Continuous Care

author.name: Aiyuan Yang, Chengfeng Dou, Da Pan, Dian Wang, Fan Yang, Fei Deng, Fei Li, Guangwei Ai, Hui Liu, Hongda Zhang, Jinyang Tai, Kai Lu, Lijun Liu, Linwei Chen, Linyu Li, Meiqing Guo, Peidong Guo, Qiang Ju, Rihui Xin, Shuai Wang, XinKai Ma, Xudong Chen, Yichuan Mo, Canbin Piao, Leyi Pan, Yihe Luo, Zian Wang

entry.summary: Baichuan-M4 is a clinical-grade medical agent system for continuous care built around a unified RL/deployment runtime, a continuous-care reasoning model with span-level reward modeling and curriculum learning, and a clinical tool layer with long-term patient memory. It targets multi-turn longitudinal care rather than single-turn QA.

entry.title: Correct Looks Better: Pairwise Comparisons Reveal Accuracy Rankings

author.name: Mina Remeli, Moritz Hardt

entry.summary: This paper shows that pairwise-comparison rankings (Elo) of generative models strongly agree with ground-truth accuracy rankings (Spearman above 0.9) across five benchmarks converted to free-form generation, and that style and judge bias have only minor effects. It offers a reassuring empirical defense of pairwise evaluation, especially when judges are weak.

entry.title: Post-training is (Massive) Supervised Learning

author.name: Michael Hassid, Yossi Adi, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that current LLM post-training (SFT + RL) effectively reverts to the BERT-era pre-train-then-fine-tune paradigm, tailoring models to benchmarks rather than general capability. Supports the claim by comparing pretrained vs randomly initialized models after fine-tuning.

entry.title: Systematic LLM Translation of Legacy Scientific Code to Differentiable Frameworks: Application to a Land Surface Model

author.name: Aya Lahlou, Linnia Hawkins, Pierre Gentine

entry.summary: This work presents a five-phase LLM agentic pipeline that translates legacy Fortran scientific code into differentiable JAX, using static dependency analysis, compile-repair loops, and a Fortran oracle for numerical parity verification. It is demonstrated on a 19,000-line land surface model.

entry.title: Adversarial Robustness of Activation Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Kien Le, Thai Le

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of activation steering robustness under adversarial text perturbations, covering multiple extraction methods, attacks, personas, and models from 1.5B to 30B. Attacks broadly succeed, dropping directional robustness by up to 64% and collapsing post-attack confidence.

entry.title: Illusions of the Gold Standard: A Large-scale Analysis of Human Evaluation Protocols for Long-form Text Generation

author.name: Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Yi-Li Hsu, Minjoon Choi, Zongwan Cao, Chenjun Xu, Bingbing Wen, Su Lin Blodgett, Lucy Lu Wang

entry.summary: This large-scale study analyzes human evaluation protocols for long-form text generation across *CL conference papers from 2023-2025, manually reviewing 284 papers and LLM-assisting analysis of over 1,800 more against 20 reproducibility criteria. It finds widespread under-reporting that undermines evaluation reliability.

entry.title: Defending Against Malicious Finetuning by Scaling Train-time Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Haoming Wen, Shi Chen, Qingyu Shi, Siyuan Liu, Minrui Luo, Jingzhao Zhang, Tianxing He

entry.summary: Patcher defends open-weight LLMs against malicious finetuning, including stronger full-parameter attacks, by scaling up train-time adversarial optimization steps in a bi-level setup to find parameters insensitive to such attacks. It improves on existing defenses limited to parameter-efficient finetuning attacks.

entry.title: How Deep Are Deep GPs, Really? A Sharp Threshold and a Non-Gaussian Limit for Compositional GPs

author.name: Mark Kozdoba, Shie Mannor

entry.summary: This paper studies the limiting behavior of compositional Gaussian processes where each layer is a vector-valued GP, establishing a sharp threshold for prior degeneration and identifying a non-Gaussian limit. It extends deep GP theory beyond prior RBF-kernel degeneracy results.

entry.title: Generative Frontier Planning for Adaptive Peer-Referral Recruitment under Covariate-Dependent Arrivals

author.name: Lingkai Kong, Hezi Jiang, Andrew Ma, Keyu Wang, Akseli Kangaslahti, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: This work addresses adaptive peer-referral recruitment (respondent-driven sampling) for hidden populations affected by infectious diseases, modeling covariate-dependent arrivals where referral capacity and recruit covariates depend on the referrer. It uses generative frontier planning to allocate limited referral resources across rounds.

entry.title: Auditing Proprietary Alignment in Large Language Models: A Comparative Framework Without a Ground-Truth Standard

author.name: Alireza Arbabi, Florian Kerschbaum

entry.summary: This paper proposes a statistical framework for detecting proprietary alignment in black-box LLMs via comparative behavioral analysis without a ground-truth standard. It addresses how providers can inject undisclosed provider-specific policies leading to censorship or misinformation.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Personalized Multi-Objective Bandits with Proactive Conversational Queries

author.name: Linfeng Cao, Ming Shi, Ness B. Shroff

entry.summary: This paper formalizes personalized multi-objective bandits with proactive conversational queries, modeling user preference signals via a Plackett-Luce subset choice model.
